title: Norges Bank Commits €1.2bn to CIP Renewable Energy Fund
content:
Norges Bank Investment Management has committed €1.2 billion to Copenhagen
Infrastructure Partners’ sixth flagship renewable energy fund, CI VI.
The agreement was signed on 1 October 2026.
The commitment builds on the investor’s relationship with CIP, having
invested €900 million in their fifth flagship fund, CI V, in 2024.
“CI VI allows us to keep investing in renewable energy projects at the
development stage and builds on a partnership that has worked well for
the fund since 2024,” said Harald von Heyden, Global Head of Energy and
Infrastructure at Norges Bank Investment Management.
CI VI will mainly target renewable energy generation and energy storage
projects across OECD countries in North America, Western Europe and the
Asia Pacific region.

title: SECI launches next renewable ammonia auction in India
content:
SECI launches next renewable ammonia auction in India
Madhya Bharat Agro Products requests 54,000 tons per year in Dhule
The Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) has launched its second subsidy program for renewable ammonia, focused on one fertiliser producer in Dhule, central India. Madhya Bharat Agro Products will accept delivery from the winning bidder of 54,000 tons per year of renewable ammonia, based on a 10-year Green Ammonia Purchase Agreement (GAPA), in which SECI acts as an “intermediary procurer”.
In the SECI’s first auction round (completed September 2026) Madhya Bharat Agro Products Unit 3 in Dhule entered into a GAPA agreement with InSolare Energy and SCC Infrastructure for the delivery of 70,000 tons per year, at a delivery price of 53 ₹/kg (~US$600 per ton). Madhya Bharat Agro Products and fellow Ostwal Group company Krishana Phoschem signed agreements worth 200,000 tons per year total supply of renewable ammonia.
After the signings in March 2026, Ostwal Group indicated they expect supply of these volumes to commence in ~3 years. The GAPA agreements with SECI mandate that the deadline for commissioning of full ammonia production capacity for the supply projects is twelve months after the “Scheduled Commencement of Supply Date”, which itself is 36 months (3 years) after the date of signing.

title: Data Center Batteries Shift to Active Power Role
content:
Stationary Batteries
Market Analysis
Design & Manufacturing
AI workloads and total cost of ownership priorities drive 16.2% annual growth as operators shift from backup to active power management.
October 5, 2026
4 Min Read
The sun is rising on battery energy storage systems such as those needed to power data centers.
Young777 / iStock via Getty Images
At a Glance
Data center battery market projected to reach $4.27 billion by 2035 with 16.2% annual growth rate
AI training jobs create power spikes reaching 10% of total facility capacity within seconds of demand
Lithium iron phosphate chemistry gains adoption over NMC due to superior thermal stability in facilities
The data center battery energy storage market is experiencing dramatic transformation as artificial intelligence workloads and operational economics reshape infrastructure priorities. According to the 2026 Data Center Energy Storage Industry Insights Report surveying 150 global professionals, 84% of operators now consider total cost of ownership (TCO) a top priority when selecting energy storage systems, while 57% identify higher power-density requirements and smaller footprints as major AI-driven impacts.
DataM Intelligence projects the global market will surge from $952.3 million in 2025 to $4.27 billion by 2035, representing 16.2% compound annual growth. North America leads with 40.2% market share, while Asia-Pacific emerges as the fastest-growing region. Lithium-ion batteries captured approximately 67% of 2025 market share, driven by migration from lead-acid systems and demand for higher energy density with lower maintenance.
Related:
Battery Technology’s Role in AI Growth and Innovation
Batteries now serve as active power buffers, not just backup
The fundamental shift extends beyond market statistics. As
Battery Technology reported from The Battery Show North America 2025
, the era of treating batteries as passive backup systems has ended. AI workloads force data centers to deploy advanced battery systems as active power buffers rather than emergency solutions. Data centers
highlight numerous conference sessions on AI at the 2026 Battery Show
in Detroit next week.
Traditional data center racks consumed two to 10 kilowatts with predictable demand that conventional UPS systems easily managed. AI training jobs now demand entire supercomputer capacity instantly, creating power spikes of 2% to 10% of total facility capacity within seconds. This unpredictable variability forces operators to deploy large-scale Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) that draw grid power at steady rates, store it, and discharge rapidly during AI training spikes.
Strategic partnerships and manufacturing expansion are accelerating deployment
Recent collaborations underscore market evolution. Vertiv and CPower's April 2026 partnership integrates Vertiv's EnergyCore Grid BESS with CPower's virtual power plant platform, enabling behind-the-meter storage for demand response, resilience, and grid services. Major players including Schneider Electric, Eaton, ABB, Huawei Digital Power, and Delta Electronics compete as operators transition toward intelligent energy-management architectures.
Cummins secured its largest BESS contract
for a U.S. data center, deploying a 5 MWh LFP battery system managing AI workloads while addressing community concerns about diesel generator noise and emissions. The system features liquid cooling, flexible DC architecture compatible with multiple power conversion and energy management systems, and bridge-to-grid capability for integration with backup generators.
Related:
La Verne Battery Fire Evacuates 500—New Tech Could Stop the Next One
Cummins' LFP battery system. Credit: Cummins
Panasonic announced plans
to adapt portions of its Kansas EV battery factory to produce energy storage systems specifically for data centers, highlighting rapid manufacturing diversification beyond automotive applications. The company's rack-mounted systems incorporate multiple storage modules with lithium-ion cells, offering backup functionality and peak shaving capabilities that cover shortages during demand periods.
Market segmentation reveals distinct deployment patterns
Systems ranging from 100 kWh to 1 MWh lead with 38% market share, reflecting suitability for distributed and medium-scale requirements. Hyperscale data centers dominate with 42% share, driven by large power requirements and rapid computing expansion. On-grid systems hold 61% deployment share, supported by utility power integration and energy-management capabilities.
Backup power leads applications with 49% share, though operators increasingly deploy batteries for peak shaving (21%), renewable integration (16%), and grid services (9%). Europe accounts for 27% of the market, driven by renewable-energy integration and grid flexibility requirements, while Asia-Pacific represents 26%, supported by rapid digitalization and hyperscale development.
Related:
Fail-Safe BESS Technology Prevents Thermal Runaway at Single-Cell Level
M&A activity and safety considerations shape the competitive landscape
The mergers and acquisitions landscape reflects market significance. Nextpower agreed to acquire Prevalon Energy for up to $365 million in May 2026, adding large-scale BESS and energy-management capabilities. T1 Energy's June 2026 agreement to acquire KORE Power expands capabilities in battery storage systems, software, and AI data center infrastructure. Brookfield's $7 billion acquisition of Aypa Power in July 2026 provides access to a large North American battery-storage platform.
Technical challenges extend beyond capacity scaling. Battery industry experts emphasize that safety protocols for data center applications must exceed electric vehicle standards. Bringing high-energy-density batteries with flammable chemistries like NMC into data center white space represents significant risk, driving increased adoption of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry offering superior thermal stability and safety characteristics. The transition from passive backup to active power management represents fundamental reimagining of data center power architecture, with BESS solutions becoming essential tools enabling developers to build resilient energy ecosystems supporting faster deployment and reliable operation of hyperscale and AI-driven campuses.

title: Ports deploy battery fleets to cut diesel use
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Battery News
APM Terminals Elizabeth and HHLA TK Estonia have ordered battery-electric terminal trucks and cranes, signaling a move to fleet-scale, full-shift battery operation.
October 4, 2026
4 Min Read
Crains and containers at the Muuga container yard
HHLA TK Estonia
At a Glance
APM Terminals Elizabeth orders 96 electric terminal trucks with 310 kWh batteries from Orange EV maker.
Konecranes delivers first European full-battery RTG cranes with 296 kWh systems to Estonia terminal.
Battery packs enable eight-hour crane shifts and multi-shift truck operations without diesel refueling.
As global trade volumes grow, container terminals face mounting pressure to cut their on-land emissions. Shipping lines have drawn most of the maritime decarbonization spotlight, but many port operators also run large fleets of diesel cargo-handling equipment around the clock.
Within a typical container yard, drivers use terminal trucks to shuttle boxes between ship-to-shore cranes and storage stacks. Operators then use gantry cranes to place those boxes. Because many terminals sit close to residential neighborhoods, nearby residents live with the exhaust and noise that equipment produces.
Electrifying that equipment, however, presents a different engineering problem than electrifying passenger cars.
Terminal operators generally need machines that work through multi-shift schedules with little downtime. Engineers must therefore balance battery capacity, cycle life, and charging strategy to meet that requirement. Operators must also secure enough grid capacity and charging infrastructure to support entire fleets, a sizable investment at sites that operators designed around diesel fueling. For those reasons, many operators have moved cautiously, trialing a few electric units before committing to fleet-wide changes.
Related:
2026 Ford Mustang Mach-E Delivers Range but BlueCruise Falls Short in Testing
Recently, several operators have moved past that caution with larger orders. In this article, we'll take a look at two new orders that bring battery-electric trucks and cranes to terminals in New Jersey and Estonia.
APM Terminals Elizabeth orders 96 electric terminal trucks
In August 2026, Orange EV
announced
that APM Terminals Elizabeth in New Jersey had ordered 96 of its electric terminal trucks, also known as terminal tractors. According to Orange EV, the order marks one of the largest port electrification commitments in history. Before the New Jersey order, APM Terminals had already expanded its Orange EV fleet at APM Terminals Los Angeles (Pier 400). After a year-long pilot with 20 rental trucks, the operator added 40 more trucks there this summer, bringing that fleet to 60.
For the Elizabeth order, APM Terminals selected Orange EV's HUSK-e XP model. Orange EV designed each truck for heavy terminal work, rating it to move up to 180,000 lbs. of combined weight. To power that work, the company equips the trucks with a 310 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery, the largest pack in its lineup.
Orange EV and APM Terminals team members. Credit: OrangeEV
Importantly, APM Terminals based the purchase on more than upfront unit cost, according to Orange EV. The operator also weighed uptime, spare parts availability, and service response standards. On uptime, Orange EV reports that its installed fleet averages more than 97% uptime.
Related:
The EV Insurance Penalty Is Over: 6 Models with Major Premium Reductions
Ultimately, Orange EV CEO Kurt Neutgens links the Elizabeth order to the Pier 400 expansion. As he explained, the two orders are “evidence of an inflection point in ports as operators move past the pilot and testing phase.”
Konecranes brings full-shift battery cranes to Estonia
Beyond yard trucks, terminal operators are also targeting diesel use in their cranes. In March 2026, Konecranes
announced
that HHLA TK Estonia had ordered two rubber-tired gantry (RTG) cranes for the Port of Muuga.
Konecranes designed the cranes to run full operational shifts on battery power. According to the company, the order marks the first time it has shipped RTGs with batteries of this scale to Europe. HHLA TK Estonia will use the 1-over-5, six-lane cranes to replace older RTGs, and the Finnish manufacturer plans to deliver the cranes in Q4 2026.
The Muuga container yard. Credit: HHLA TK Estonia
For context, terminal operators in a typical yard drive RTG cranes on rubber tires to straddle and stack rows of containers. Traditionally, manufacturers have powered those cranes with onboard diesel generators. To cut emissions, Konecranes now offers options ranging from renewable diesel and hybrid drives to fully electrified fleets under its Ecolifting roadmap.
Related:
Bentley Unveils Torcal EV With 876 HP, V8-Inspired Drum Sound & 375-Mile Range
Within that range, Konecranes pairs a large battery with fixed charging for the Estonian cranes. The company specified a 296 kWh battery system, which it says enables up to eight hours of independent operation. To recharge the cranes, HHLA TK Estonia will use an integrated 25-meter busbar charging system. According to Konecranes, operators running the cranes fully on battery power eliminate tailpipe emissions during crane operations and reduce yard noise.
Beyond the Muuga deployment, Konecranes regional sales manager Philipp Reiter sees broader significance in the order. As he noted, “This order demonstrates how battery technology is shifting from being a mitigation solution to providing power for full-scale operational use.”
Electrifying the container yard
Overall, port operators are bringing battery technology to two of the main workhorses of the container yard. APM Terminals has moved from a year-long pilot at Pier 400 to a 96-truck order in New Jersey. Meanwhile, HHLA TK Estonia is moving battery cranes into full-shift duty. In each case, the buyers chose large battery packs, with 310 kWh per truck and 296 kWh per crane.
As these fleets grow from pilot units to dozens of machines, terminal operators will face new questions about the infrastructure behind the batteries. They will need to plan grid connections, charging schedules, and energy management with the same care they give berth and crane scheduling. Operators that solve those problems first could set the template for how ports move the world's cargo without diesel.

title: Vertical Data Centers Face Cost-Proximity Trade-Offs
content:
A proposed 20-story data center tower in downtown Kansas City, Missouri, offers an alternative to sprawling suburban campuses: stack computing, power, and cooling on a small urban parcel and leverage dense, carrier-rich connectivity. But stacking infrastructure vertically introduces additional costs and operational complexity, and the case for a downtown address depends on whether proximity and network diversity justify the construction premium.
Designed by storied Chicago architecture firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) for developer Revitalization Unlimited, the facility would occupy approximately 0.23 acres. The project remains subject to approval; a related
city development plan ordinance
is listed as on hold until October 13.
Why Proximity Matters for Urban Sites
Steve Austin, founder and CEO of Revitalization Unlimited, argues that
inference workloads
and dense network interconnections support a central location.
Related:
Data Center Architects Reimagine Facilities as Urban Assets
“Inference is the model actually answering a user, and it has to happen near that user because latency matters,” he told
Data Center Knowledge
Austin pointed to nearby carrier infrastructure, planned diverse fiber entrances, and a carrier-neutral design as advantages for customers that value fast connections to users and other networks. Whether that proximity is worth a premium depends on the workload.
Luis Fernandes, IDC senior research manager for cloud and data centers within enterprise infrastructure, cited high-speed financial transactions as an example where physical proximity can matter.
“It is not uncommon for stock traders to seek addresses closest to the actual stock exchange servers where transactions are processed in order to gain a few fractions of a second in any given transaction,” Fernandes told
Data Center Knowledge
He added that the economics depend on the premium for building vertically.
Michael Martin, managing director of data center operations at JLL, said customers generally approach location decisions based on their business requirements rather than a preference for downtown.
“The reality is that clients don’t come to us asking for a downtown data center,” he said. “They’re usually trying to solve a business problem.”
Martin sees opportunities in financial services, telecommunications, content delivery, and inference at urban sites, while large AI training clusters typically favor abundant land and power.
The Cost of Building Upward
Austin estimated total development costs at $183 million, or roughly $1,300 per square foot, acknowledging that it exceeds the per-square-foot cost of a suburban facility. Much of the expenditure would go toward mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection systems – about $107 million of the estimated $167 million in hard construction costs.
Related:
Urban Data Centers: Who Needs Them and Where to Find Them
The proposed building would support 24 MW of IT load. Only two of its 20 floors would house computing equipment, according to Austin, with approximately 109,000 of its 141,000 gross square feet devoted to mechanical space. Those proportions illustrate the trade-off: land saved at ground level must be recaptured by stacking substantial supporting infrastructure above it.
Fernandes said equipment placement in vertical builds creates practical challenges. Most vendors design power and cooling equipment for horizontal placement, with very little consideration for vertical deployment, he said.
Weight, freight elevator dimensions, and crane access all matter. Replacing equipment may require coordination with surrounding streets, while pumping cooling water introduces demands different from those in a conventional commercial tower.
Smaller Physical, Not Necessarily Smaller Footprint
Fernandes cautioned against assuming reduced land consumption equates to a smaller overall environmental footprint.
Related:
Do We Really Need Mega Next-Gen Data Center Campuses?
“There is no data to suggest that a vertical build will impact the overall environmental footprint,” he said.
Austin said the Kansas City design targets a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.25 and would use 30 MW of
on-site Bloom fuel cells
as the primary electricity source. These are proposed performance and operating characteristics.
Self-generation
also requires examining the fuel supply. Austin identified natural gas as one of the facility’s expected operating expenses, meaning that independence from the electricity grid should not be confused with the absence of environmental impacts.
Cooling claims likewise need precision. Fernandes questioned the description of the project as a closed loop while also noting that it includes
evaporative cooling
, which consumes water. Cities and prospective customers will need operating figures to evaluate those trade-offs.
Looking beyond the Kansas City proposal, Martin sees potential in converting suitable existing buildings for smaller or edge workloads.
“Reusing existing structures, utility connections, and supporting infrastructure can reduce waste while also improving project economics and speed to market,” he said. That case depends on a building’s suitability for added power, cooling, and operational demands.
What Communities Gain – and Expect – in Return
Austin emphasized tax revenue and local spending while acknowledging limited
permanent staffing
“On-site operations staff is a couple of dozen,” he said. “The rest are technicians, contractors, and service firms the facility pays continuously, plus the jobs supported by their spending.”
He said the developer is seeking no tax abatement and is prepared to accept binding conditions covering active ground-floor space, noise, generator operating hours, construction apprenticeships, and public reporting.
Fernandes argued community benefits should extend beyond tax receipts, suggesting partnerships with trade schools and facilities such as libraries or daycare services.
“[Make] the data center a part of the community instead of something forced upon a community,” Fernandes noted.
Designing for Flexibility and Reuse
Long-term usefulness is another consideration. Fernandes noted older facilities can be retrofitted or reassigned to less demanding workloads, although a tower’s physical constraints would need to be assessed.
Martin said adaptability should guide design decisions as computing requirements change.
“The facilities that remain valuable over the long term are the ones that can adapt,” he said. “That means flexibility in power distribution, cooling architecture, structural capacity, and overall building design.”
The broader test is whether a specific location provides enough operational and public value to justify the additional complexity. Austin maintains that his proposal meets that test.
“We are not arguing that every data center belongs downtown,” he said. “We are arguing this one does, and we are paying a construction premium to prove it.”

title: Why Data Center Site Selection Is Now a Three-Front Battle
content:
For the past three years, site selection for hyperscale and enterprise data centers in North America followed a simple, singular rule: find power. As artificial intelligence workloads escalated electricity demand, developers rushed to secure interconnection capacity wherever megawatts were available. But that era of single-variable site selection has officially come to a close.
In late September 2026, state governors, public utility commissions, and environmental regulators across the United States launched a wave of concurrent actions
tightening data center oversight
. The message from statehouses in California, Texas, New York, Massachusetts, and New Jersey is unequivocal: securing a utility power commitment is no longer a guaranteed green light. Data center development has shifted into a three-front regulatory battle spanning grid cost responsibility, water transparency, and local land-use accountability.
Related:
Community Partnerships Are Becoming Data Centers’ Most Valuable Asset
For facility operators, real estate strategists, and enterprise architects, understanding this new regulatory landscape is no longer just a compliance exercise; it is a fundamental prerequisite for project survival.
Grid Cost Responsibility and Ratepayer Protections
The first front of this regulatory shift targets electric infrastructure costs and ratepayer protections. Historically, the multimillion-dollar distribution and transmission upgrades required to hook up massive industrial facilities were frequently socialized across a utility’s broader customer base. Today, state regulators are aggressively closing that cost-shifting loop.
California’s newly enacted package
, including AB 1577, AB 2383, and SB 887, explicitly mandates that data center developers cover the full incremental cost of electric grid upgrades required to serve their facilities, shielding low-income residential ratepayers from rate hikes. In Massachusetts, Governor Maura Healey’s
Executive Order 658
requires large data centers (with peak demand exceeding 25 MW) to bear all associated energy infrastructure costs and to fund ratepayer protection mechanisms if projects do not meet clean power obligations directly.
Meanwhile, in the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, utility commissions are erecting formal barriers to contract review. The Alabama Public Service Commission has
opened generic proceedings
requiring Alabama Power to demonstrate that large-load contracts fully recover incremental costs before agreements are approved.
Pennsylvania’s Public Utility Commission
is revisiting ratemaking and emergency load-control rules amid a severe capacity shortfall identified in the PJM market. In Oregon, large energy users served by Portland General Electric are already confronting an
average 29% rate increase
under the state’s POWER Act.
Related:
Losing the Plot: Why a Responsible Approach to Land Is Pivotal to Data Center Development
The operational takeaway for data center developers is clear: power purchase agreements (PPAs) and interconnection contracts must now build in full, non-socialized capital recovery for grid upgrades.
Water Transparency and Conservation
While power grid constraints have dominated industry headlines,
water consumption
has emerged as the most immediate statutory trigger for project halts. Data center space cooling is extraordinarily resource-intensive; according to the US Energy Information Administration, space cooling on data center floor space is up to 2.9 times as energy-intensive as non-data center floor space. When space cooling is combined with evaporative cooling towers, local water tables face unprecedented strain.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott recently escalated state oversight by
directing a pause
on new data center permitting decisions by the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality until grid operator ERCOT (Electric Reliability Council of Texas) completes a comprehensive statewide audit. Crucially, the governor tied this permit pause directly to enforcement of mandatory water-use reporting, tasking the Texas Water Development Board with referring noncompliant facilities to local prosecutors and disqualifying them from state water permits.
Related:
Vertical Data Centers Face Cost-Proximity Trade-Offs
In California,
new statutory reporting and planning rules
require data center developers to provide local governments and water authorities with granular data on expected water consumption, water supply availability, efficiency technologies, and drought contingency plans before breaking ground. Furthermore, developers may be required to finance municipal water infrastructure improvements needed to serve the facility as part of local approvals. New Jersey’s newly enacted S 3379 similarly requires data centers to provide semiannual reporting of energy and water use to the Board of Public Utilities.
For data center engineering teams, air-cooled systems,
closed-loop liquid cooling
, and wastewater recycling are no longer optional ESG highlights; they are increasingly required or strongly favored as conditions for securing state environmental permits.
Land Use and Community Benefits
The third front of the new regulatory reality centers on land use and community benefits. As municipalities grow wary of hosting vast, low-employment industrial footprints that consume local resources, states are providing local governments with standardized playbooks to demand tangible economic returns.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul recently launched a
Host Community Investment Framework
, establishing a benchmark of $1 million per megawatt of utility demand for local community benefit agreements. Under this template, local municipalities are encouraged to leverage project approvals to secure direct investments in roads, water and sewer infrastructure, public transit, workforce housing, public safety, and local schools. California has simultaneously eliminated broad environmental exemptions for data centers via
, requiring full environmental reviews and compliance with local land-use standards before projects can receive streamlined judicial review.
What Changes Now
As server energy consumption accelerates toward projected long-term highs, data center operators can no longer rely on legacy site-selection playbooks. The era of securing power in isolation is over. To successfully bring capacity online in 2027 and beyond, data center leaders must adopt an integrated development framework that addresses grid cost allocation, water conservation engineering, and host community investment simultaneously. Facilities that build transparency, self-funded infrastructure, and local economic alignment into their initial engineering plans will move through state permitting; those that focus solely on securing megawatts will find themselves stalled at the statehouse door.

title: Battery storage paired with 37% of new US residential solar in 2025 - Energy Storage
content: More than one-third of new residential solar installations in the United States included battery storage in 2025, as batteries increasingly shift from an optional addition to a standard component of rooftop solar projects. Battery storage was paired with 37% of new residential photovoltaic systems in 2025, up from 25% in 2024, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s latest US Distributed Solar and Storage Data update. The annual dataset includes roughly 5.3 million distributed solar and solar-plus-storage systems installed through the end of 2025. That includes about 450,000 systems installed during 2025, representing an estimated 93% of the U.S. distributed solar market for the year. About 74% of new residential solar installations in California included storage in 2025, up from 58% in 2024. But battery adoption also accelerated outside the state. Across all other states in Berkeley Lab’s comparison, the residential storage attachment rate climbed from 7% to 17% in one year. Berkeley Lab highlighted particularly large increases in Arizona and Texas. Hawaii and California continued to post the highest residential storage attachment rates in the country. California’s rise in solar-plus-storage installations follows the state’s transition to its Net Billing Tariff, commonly called NEM 3.0, in April 2023. The policy reduced the value of electricity exported by new rooftop solar customers during many hours, increasing the value of storing excess daytime generation for later use. That change quickly altered the composition of California’s rooftop solar market. More than half of California solar customers were pairing batteries with their PV systems , up from about 20% in October 2023. Battery attachment rates outside California more than doubled from 2024 to 2025 . Berkeley Lab did not attribute that increase to any single factor, but installers in other markets are increasingly confronting changes to net-metering structures and time-of-use electricity rates that can increase the value of consuming stored solar power rather than exporting it. Storage adoption also increased in the non-residential market, although it remains far below residential levels. Batteries were attached to 11% of US non-residential solar installations in 2025, up from 7% in 2024. California’s non-residential attachment rate increased from 12% to 18%, while the rate across all other states doubled from 4% to 8%. The typical amount of energy stored in residential batteries did not change significantly. Median residential storage capacity remained 13.5 kWh in both 2024 and 2025. However, the power those systems can deliver increased sharply. Median discharge capacity increased from 6 kW in 2024 to 11.4 kW in 2025. Berkeley Lab attributed much of that increase to growing deployment of the Tesla Powerwall 3, which has higher discharge capacity than previous versions. The report cautions that its attachment rates do not capture the entire distributed storage market. They exclude batteries added later to existing solar installations as well as standalone battery systems. That means the data measure how often installers pair batteries with new solar projects, rather than the full rate of residential battery deployment. Even under that narrower definition, the year-over-year increase suggests solar-plus-storage is rapidly becoming a larger part of the US residential market. title: China’s 700 MW Jintan salt-cavern CAES project completes full-system startup - Energy Storage
content: China Huaneng’s 700 MW Jintan salt-cavern compressed air energy storage (CAES) project has completed full-system startup of its two generating units in Changzhou, Jiangsu province. The milestone was reached on Sept. 12, with both 350 MW units undergoing integrated startup testing under operating conditions. At 700 MW, the second phase of the Jintan project has the largest installed power capacity of any salt-cavern CAES facility currently reported worldwide. The project will now proceed with pre-grid-connection tests and system commissioning. The plant uses four underground salt caverns at depths of around 1,000 meters, with total gas-storage volume of about 1.2 million cubic meters. Electricity is used to compress air to pressures exceeding 130 atmospheres during charging, while heat generated during compression is captured and stored. During discharge, the stored air is reheated and expanded through turbines without burning natural gas. A full charging cycle stores about 2.8 GWh of electricity. Project documents describe an approximately eight-hour charging period and four hours of rated power generation, with more than 70% round-trip energy conversion efficiency. The facility is expected to complete around 330 charge-discharge cycles annually and generate about 924 GWh per year. The second phase represents a major scale-up from the 60 MW/300 MWh first phase commissioned in 2022. Its compression system uses a dual-line, four-stage architecture to handle substantially higher airflow, while each generating unit employs a 350 MW air turbine with three reheating stages and four expansion stages. The turbine operates with a main air pressure of 13.5 MPa and has a design efficiency of more than 93%. Thermal storage is another major change from the first phase. Jintan Phase II replaces the heat-transfer oil used previously with medium-temperature pressurized water. Sixteen spherical tanks, each holding 3,500 cubic meters, provide 56,000 cubic meters of thermal storage volume. Pressurization raises the water operating temperature to around 180 C, allowing compression heat to be recovered and reused during generation. China Huaneng and China Salt Group jointly developed the project, with technical support from Tsinghua University and Xi’an Thermal Power Research Institute. Huaneng Jiangsu and China Salt’s salt-cavern business are responsible for project development, construction and operations. PowerChina subsidiary SEPCO1 has undertaken construction and installation work for Unit 2. The Jintan design differs in several respects from Zhongchu Guoneng’s operating 300 MW/1,800 MWh Feicheng CAES plant in Shandong. Feicheng, based on technology developed by the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Engineering Thermophysics, uses multi-stage wide-load compression, high-load turbine expansion and compact regenerative thermal-storage technology. It provides six hours of discharge and has a rated design efficiency of 72.1%. Jintan, by contrast, places greater emphasis on scaling individual turbine capacity to 350 MW, parallel four-stage compression and pressurized-water heat storage, while delivering four hours at rated output. Both projects illustrate China’s shift from demonstration-scale CAES toward several-hundred-megawatt long-duration storage plants designed to provide peak shifting, renewable energy integration and other grid-balancing services. title: Renalfa and Eurowind Energy inaugurate 773 MWh double-battery hybrid park - Energy Storage
content: Vienna-based independent power producer Renalfa IPP and Danish developer Eurowind Energy have inaugurated the Tenevo hybrid renewable energy complex in southeastern Bulgaria. The site combines a 242 MWp solar photovoltaic (PV) plant with two co-located battery energy storage systems (BESS) totaling 311 MW / 773 MWh. The site’s storage was developed in two phases: an initial four-hour, 65 MW / 260 MWh system and a second 246 MW / 512.5 MWh system with approximately two hours of storage. The expansion adds substantially more charging and discharging power, rather than simply extending the duration of the original battery. The initial BESS has been operational since 2025 . The full solar plant was commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, according to Renalfa IPP, following repairs to hailstorm damage. The companies expect the complex to generate around 332 GWh of electricity annually. Renalfa and Eurowind Energy say the hybrid approach is intended to make greater use of the available grid connection. They plan to add more than 250 MW of wind generation, with total investment across all phases expected to exceed €500 million. The PV plant received €50 million in financing from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and €53 million from Raiffeisen Bank International AG (RBI). A further €60 million financing package for the second BESS phase is expected to be signed shortly, according to the companies. EBRD’s project disclosure puts the cost of the second BESS at €72 million and records approval of a loan of up to €30 million in July. It identifies Hithium as the battery supplier and specifies lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology, with Solarpro responsible for procurement and installation. The bank says the absence of a contract-for-difference scheme and other mechanisms to stabilize revenues in Bulgaria has limited long-term lending for merchant renewable projects. It describes its financing as filling a gap in the local market. Tenevo is also among the first projects in Bulgaria to benefit from a guarantee under the European Union’s InvestEU program , according to the companies. The project company, Tenevo Solar Technologies, is a 50:50 joint venture between Renalfa IPP and Eurowind Energy. Renalfa IPP is itself a joint venture between Renalfa Solarpro Group and French infrastructure fund manager Rgreen Invest. title: Gas cars fall below 50% of global new car sales for the first time
content:
Gas cars are now a minority of the world’s new car sales. Gasoline-only vehicles made up 49% of global new-vehicle sales in the first half of 2026, down from 73% in 2021, according to Mobility Global data first reported by Nikkei.
It’s the first time on record that they’ve been under half. But there’s a catch: most of the cars taking their place still have a gas tank.
Gas cars lost 24 points of share in under five years
Mobility Global is the auto data firm formerly known as S&P Global Mobility, which was spun off from S&P Global this year. Nikkei reported its first-half numbers last week, and they show sales of gasoline-only cars down 10% from a year ago to 20.25 million units between January and June.
Their share fell three points in a single year, from 52% to 49%.
Battery-electric vehicles grew 12% to 6.87 million units and took 17% of the market, up three points. Conventional hybrids grew 10% to 7.27 million units, or 18%.
| Powertrain | H1 2026 sales | Change | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gasoline-only | 20.25 million | -10% | 49% |
| Hybrid | 7.27 million | +10% | 18% |
| Battery-electric | 6.87 million | +12% | 17% |
| Diesel, plug-in hybrid and other | not reported | not reported | about 16% |
That last row is our math. The reported shares add up to 84%, and the rest is diesel, plug-in hybrids and a few minor fuels.
Nikkei ties the acceleration to oil. Fuel prices spiked with the conflict in the Middle East, and buyers went looking for lower running costs.
The whole car market shrank about 5% in the first half, according to the IEA, so gas-only sales fell twice as fast as the market.
Gas car sales dropped the most in China, down 26%, followed by Europe at 13%. That matches what we’ve been reporting from both markets. In China, sales of gas cars and conventional hybrids fell 40% in August while battery-electric sales edged up. In the EU, ACEA’s registration data has battery-electric cars ahead of petrol cars for the year through August, 1,641,333 to 1,634,733, with petrol down 18.6%.
The EV numbers by region show where the growth is. Mobility Global has battery-electric sales up 32% in Europe to 1.81 million, up 81% in Southeast Asia to 350,000, and more than doubling in Oceania to 110,000. China was down 3% at 3.44 million, which is still half of the world’s total. North America was down 15%.
Yoshiaki Kawano, an associate director at Mobility Global, told Nikkei that few EV buyers go back to gasoline cars or hybrids. He expects demand based on “genuine consumer needs rather than subsidies” to grow as prices come down.
That lines up with the CDK study we covered in July, in which 94% of EV owners said they won’t go back to gas.
83% of new cars still have an engine
“Gas cars under 50%” is accurate, but you have to read the label. The 49% covers cars that run on gasoline and nothing else.
Hybrids are counted separately, and they outsold battery-electric vehicles in the first half, 7.27 million to 6.87 million. A hybrid is a gas car that uses less gas. Diesels and plug-in hybrids sit in the other 16%.
Only the 17% that’s battery-electric burns no fuel at all. So about 83% of the new vehicles sold in the world this year still came with an engine.
It’s also a six-month number, taken in the middle of an oil shock. We’ll see if the full year stays under 50%, but the trend may be accelerating.
The US isn’t going back to gas either
The Mobility Global data got passed around a lot over the weekend, often with a note that the US is the exception and that gas cars are regaining ground here since the federal tax credit ended.
EV sales did take a hit. Cox Automotive expects about 239,000 new EV sales in the third quarter, roughly 6% of the market and down about 45% from the 437,000 sold a year ago, when buyers rushed to beat the September 30 deadline. Just last week, Ford reported that its EV sales fell 80% in the quarter.
But those buyers didn’t go back to gas-only cars. Here’s Cox’s US powertrain mix for the second quarter:
| Powertrain | Q2 2025 | Q2 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Gas and diesel (ICE) | 77.6% | 76.8% |
| Hybrid | 13.0% | 16.3% |
| Battery-electric | 7.4% | 5.8% |
| Plug-in hybrid | 2.0% | 1.1% |
Hybrid volume was up 23%, and 16.3% is a record. The ICE share went down, not up. Electrified vehicles as a whole went from 22.4% to 23.2% of the market.
Cox also has gasoline back around $4.50 a gallon, up 41% from a year ago.
Electrek’s Take
Top comment by John Donovan
“Gas-only cars went from 73% to 49% of the market in less than five years, and nothing in the data suggests they’re getting that share back. ”
Hybrids without a plug still run 100% on gas. Yes, they might be a little more efficient than a gas car of the same weight, but they’re still “gas only” cars.
This is a real milestone, and I don’t want to undersell it. Gas-only cars went from 73% to 49% of the market in less than five years, and nothing in the data suggests they’re getting that share back. The last time gasoline wasn’t on top was the early 1900s, when steam and electric cars outsold it in the US.
I hate seeing media headlines claiming that “EV sales are down” and that “EV growth has stalled.”
The data is clear: that’s true in the US, but only in the US. The rest of the world is moving to electric vehicles, and it is not slowing down.

title: Hyundai's electric hatch goes on sale with up to 308 miles of range, starting at about $25,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 5 2026 - 7:14 am PT
The IONIQ 3 has received more interest than any
vehicle in the UK ever. Starting at about $25,000, Hyundai’s electric hatch undercuts much of the competition.
How much does the Hyundai IONIQ 3 cost in the UK?
Hyundai opened orders for the highly anticipated IONIQ 3 in the UK and Europe, its first compact electric vehicle under the IONIQ branding.
The response so far has been “extraordinary,” Ashley Andrew, president of Hyundai Motor UK, said after launching the new IONIQ 3 on Monday.
According to Andrew, the electric hatch has received “more customers registering their interest before launch than any new Hyundai we’ve introduced in the UK.” With the full £3,750 Electric Car Grant available on every trim, the IONIQ 3 is one of the most affordable, long-range EVs on the market.
The IONIQ 3 is now available to order in the UK, starting at just £18,495 OTR, or roughly $25,000, including the grant.
It’s available with two battery packs: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 N-Line (Source: Hyundai UK)
The extended-range IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.
Hyundai is offering leases from £355 a month for the IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery. The offer is with a £355 deposit and 8.9% APR, including the £3,750 Electric Car Grant
At that, Hyundai’s electric hatch is cheaper than much of the competition, including the Renault 5 E-Tech, priced from £21,495 in the UK, including the ECG. It also undercuts BYD’s new plug-in Dolphin G DM-i (£23,990).
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai said that those who already placed an order can convert their reservation into a full order and receive the full £3,750 Electric Car Grant instead of the previous £1,500 Hyundai Reservation Saving.
The IONIQ 3 measures 4,155 mm (163.5″) in length, 1,800 mm (70.9″) in width, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) in height, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), which is even a bit smaller than the Kia EV3 and Volkswagen ID.3.
While it’s under the IONIQ brand, the electric hatch features a distinct new “Aero Hatch” silhouette that maximizes efficiency with a drag coefficient of just 0.263. With a total boot capacity of up to 441 liters, Hyundai said the IONIQ 3 “sets the benchmark in the segment.”
Hyundai IONIQ 3 N-Line interior (Source: Hyundai UK)
The IONIQ 3 is also Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Based on the Android Automotive OS platform, Hyundai’s new system is more like using a smartphone. It offers apps and customizable screens, similar to Tesla models. It’s available with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.
Hyundai’s SmartSense driver assistance technology, Hyundai Digital Key 2, Plug & Charge, an integrated EV Route planner, and Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) all come as standard.
Unlike the IONIQ 5, which uses 800V, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. With DC fast charging, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes about a minute longer, at around 30 minutes.

title: It's now easier than ever to get your motorcycle license on an electric bike
content:
Electric Motorcycles
LiveWire
Micah Toll
| Oct 5 2026 - 4:39 am PT
LiveWire’s smallest electric motorcycle is about to take on a new role, and it could prove to be one of the most important ones yet. The LiveWire S4 Honcho Street has now met the Motorcycle Safety Foundation’s (MSF) criteria for use in rider training programs, opening the door for new riders to learn the ropes – and potentially earn their motorcycle endorsement – without first learning how to operate a clutch and gearbox on a gas-powered motorcycle.
The move could be particularly significant for the growing number of riders arriving at motorcycling through e-bikes and other electric two-wheelers.
LiveWire designed the
S4 Honcho
as its smallest and most approachable electric motorcycle yet, and those same qualities happen to make the mini-moto particularly well-suited to rider training. As essentially a 125cc-equivalent, it fits into the smallest category of conventional motorcycling.
The bike weighs just 266 lb (121 kg) and has a seat height under 30 inches, making it considerably less intimidating than many full-sized motorcycles. And because it uses an electric drivetrain, there’s no clutch lever or gearbox to master. Twist the throttle and go.
That means aesthetically, the bike looks like a motorcycle. Functionally, though, it’s nearly as simple to operate as a scooter or Class 2 electric bicycle.
The S4 Honcho is an urban-focused model that has a top-rated speed of 59 mph (95 km/h) but also includes reduced-speed riding profiles that LiveWire says are equivalent to first- and second-gear training environments, limiting the bike to 18 mph (29 km/h) or 28 mph (45 km/h), respectively.
That’s great for the parking-lot-style training used in MSF classes that teach new riders the skills they need to safely operate a motorcycle.
The bike’s range is rated at 53 miles (85 km) using the WMTC standard or up to 73 miles (117 km) at 20 mph (32 km/h). For parking lot training, that’s more than enough to get through an entire day, but the swappable battery system should also allow training schools to keep bikes running continuously instead of waiting around for them to recharge.
“The next generation of riders is coming up on e-bikes and electric vehicles, so their expectations for mobility are changing,” explained LiveWire Head of Commercial Jon Bekefy. “For many, an electric motorcycle is a more natural first step into motorcycling. The S4 Honcho removes traditional barriers to entry and paired with MSF’s world-class training programs, Honcho gives new riders a more approachable way to learn safely and build confidence. That matters for LiveWire, and it matters for the future of motorcycling.”
The Motorcycle Safety Foundation appears to see the potential as well.
Corey Eastman, the organization’s Director of Rider Education Expansion, said the Honcho will join the training demo fleet at the MSF RiderCoach Tour, giving coaches a chance to use the electric motorcycle during several MSF exercises and allowing training providers to evaluate it for their own programs.
It’s not yet clear which MSF programs and in which areas will adopt the Honcho as an option for new riders, though hopefully we’ll learn more as the bikes roll out this year. But for LiveWire, getting the Honcho into training programs could also introduce an entirely new group of riders to electric motorcycles before they ever throw a leg over a gas bike.
And frankly, that makes a lot of sense.
Electrek’s Take
I love this. It was already good news when the LiveWire S2 platform
began being used for rider training
last year, but now the smaller S4 Honcho bike makes the process even less intimidating and more approachable for a larger number of future riders. And since it starts at just $4,999 (or $5,499 for the street version), it’s an affordable bike that riders might want to continue on after learning with it for their training and licensing.
I’ve long believed
that small, lightweight and approachable electric motorcycles are going to be one of the most important tools for getting more people out of cars and onto two wheels. Not everyone needs a 500-pound motorcycle with 100 horsepower. In fact, most commuters absolutely don’t. And since most car trips are single occupant affairs, having a small and affordable electric motorcycle that can carry one or two people is a great alternative, or at least an addition to a household instead of getting a second car.
In fact, years ago I had to get my US motorcycle license at a Harley-Davidson dealer on a 500+ lb gasoline-powered motorcycle, after which I spent probably 99% of my time on electric bikes, ranging from LiveWires to Zeros to Energicas to Ryvids and just about everything in between. If there had been an electric option for my rider training class at the time, I would have jumped on it.
A little electric motorcycle that is comfortable, unintimidating, cheap to operate and capable of handling normal city and suburban roads is probably a much better transportation tool for a huge number of people.
But there’s been a frustrating chicken-and-egg problem for prospective electric motorcycle riders: getting the license.
Imagine you’ve spent the last several years riding e-bikes. Maybe you’re perfectly comfortable on two wheels and now you want something that can keep up with faster traffic. You’ve got no interest in gasoline motorcycles. You don’t want to own one, and you don’t particularly care about learning to operate one.
Yet depending on where and how you take your motorcycle course, your path toward getting licensed may involve learning clutch control and shifting gears on a gas motorcycle anyway.
That’s a pretty silly obstacle for someone who never wants to ride a bike that requires those skills.
And I’m not discounting them. Clutch control is an important skill if you want to ride a manual motorcycle. Ultimately, I’m glad I learned it because I’ve occasionally
borrowed or rented gasoline-powered bikes
, and it allows me to actually ride them. But if you’re buying an electric motorcycle, it’s about as relevant as learning to crank-start a Model T before being allowed to drive a Tesla.
There are plenty of genuinely important motorcycle skills that new riders need to learn: braking, cornering, low-speed maneuvering, situational awareness, looking through turns, emergency maneuvers, and generally understanding how to survive around drivers who somehow manage not to see a human being wearing fluorescent clothing sitting six feet in front of them. I even recommend MSF classes to electric bicycle riders because so many of the skills overlap.
But operating a clutch doesn’t need to be part of that equation for someone who intends to ride electric.
That’s why I think the S4 Honcho entering MSF training programs is a much bigger deal than simply adding another motorcycle to the fleet.
E-bikes have introduced millions of people to electric two-wheelers, including plenty who never considered themselves “motorcycle people.” Some of those riders are inevitably going to want more speed, more range and more capability.
Small electric motorcycles are the obvious next rung on that ladder.
And if riders can take their training and testing on the same type of clutch-free electric motorcycle they actually intend to ride, that ladder just became considerably easier to climb.
That could be a big boon for LiveWire, sure. But more importantly, it could help welcome an entirely new generation of riders into motorcycling – riders who might never have bothered if their first assignment was learning to feather a clutch on a gas bike.

title: Lucid's $50,000 Cosmos spotted testing in California after 2027 delay
content:
Lucid Motors
lucid cosmos
Fred Lambert
| Oct 5 2026 - 7:34 am PT
Credit: u/always_trolled on Reddit
The Lucid Cosmos is out testing in California traffic. A camouflaged prototype of the midsize SUV was photographed on Highway 101 in Morgan Hill, about 40 miles south of Lucid’s headquarters in Newark.
The four photos show the sub-$50,000 SUV from the rear and the side. They come two months after Lucid pushed the Cosmos launch back to the second half of 2027.
Lucid Cosmos prototype spotted on Highway 101
Reddit user
u/always_trolled
the photos on the Lucid subreddit
. Highway signs in the shots for downtown Morgan Hill, East Dunne Avenue, and Cochrane Road put the prototype northbound on US-101, heading toward San Jose.
A Lucid Cosmos prototype on US-101 in Morgan Hill, California (Credit:
u/always_trolled on Reddit
The car wears California plates and a black, white, and grey wrap made of jumbled letters. Not that the wrap hides much.
The roofline drops sharply toward the back, a spoiler sits at the base of the rear glass, and thin red light strips peek out from a covered panel that runs the width of the tailgate. That lines up with
the Cosmos design Lucid registered in Europe in June
The Cosmos prototype from the side, with flush door handles and a green light on the B-pillar (Credit:
u/always_trolled on Reddit
a Cosmos prototype was photographed next to a Tesla Model Y
near Lucid’s factory in Casa Grande, Arizona.
announced the Cosmos in March
with a 69 kWh battery pack, 300 miles of range, and a starting price under $50,000. The company claims efficiency of 4.5 miles per kWh and 200 miles of range added in 14 minutes. It uses Atlas, Lucid’s new drive unit, which has 30% fewer parts and costs 37% less than the current one.
Lucid Cosmos launch slips to late 2027
Production was supposed to start in late 2026. In August, new CEO Silvio Napoli
pushed the Cosmos to 2027
, “most likely the second half.”
“We’re not going to make the mistake of the past where products, great cars, were in fact tainted by launching before things were ready,” Napoli said.
Lucid needs this car. The company
laid off 18% of its staff in June
, its second deep cut in four months, and
its stock crashed 40% in July on a bankruptcy report that Lucid denied
. It says it has enough liquidity to last well into 2027.
And the competition isn’t waiting. Rivian started building the R2 in April, and
its $45,000 base version is due in late 2027
, the same window Lucid is now targeting for the Cosmos.
Electrek’s Take
A wrapped prototype on a highway isn’t big news by itself, but we are keeping a close eye on this program as it will make or break Lucid in our opinion.
We think Napoli made the right call on the delay. When we
reviewed the Gravity earlier this year
, the hardware was excellent and the software wasn’t ready. Lucid can’t repeat that with a car that has to sell in volume to buyers who are a lot less forgiving than early adopters.
The problem is the timing. Lucid says its liquidity lasts well into 2027, and the Cosmos comes in the second half of 2027. So the car that’s supposed to turn Lucid into a volume automaker shows up around the time its current cash is supposed to run out. That means another check from Saudi Arabia’s PIF, or maybe Uber, before the first customer delivery.
And the product is worth saving. Lucid claims the Cosmos is 10% more efficient than its closest competitor, and efficiency is how you get 300 miles out of a 69 kWh pack and a price under $50,000. Lucid’s powertrains are the most efficient in the business, and we’d love to see what they can do with a more mass-market vehicle.

title: Toyota gets the green light for a new EV built to take on China
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 5 2026 - 8:57 am PT
will invest around $1.3 billion, the largest in Argentina’s automotive industry to date, to produce a new electric vehicle at its site in Buenos Aires.
Toyota plans to build a new EV in Argentina
Toyota Argentina announced it had received approval from the Evaluation Committee to join the RIGI (Incentive Regime for Large Investments) to produce a new electric vehicle at its plant in Zárate, Buenos Aires province.
The project will cost around $1.3 billion, Toyota said, making it the largest investment in Argentina’s auto industry ever.
Toyota has been producing vehicles at the facility since 1997. The new investment will create around 3,600 jobs during the initial construction phase and about 2,600 once the upgrades are complete.
The site currently produces Toyota vehicles, including the Hilux pickup, SW4 SUV, and Hiace commercial van.
Toyota said it will announce more details shortly, including production plans. According to
Automotive News
, Toyota’s all-electric pickup, the Hilux BEV, is a likely candidate for production in Argentina.
Toyota Hilux BEV (Source: Toyota)
Toyota currently builds the Hilux EV in Thailand and exports it to Europe, Asia, Australia, and other overseas markets.
The announcement comes as Chinese brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery dominate EV sales in Latin America with lower-cost vehicles.
Toyota Hilux BEV pickup models (Source: Toyota Australia)
BYD sold 85,800 vehicles in Latin America through July, according to MarkLines. That’s nearly 60% of the region’s 147,493 electric vehicles sold in the same period.
Argentina’s Minister of Economy, Luis Caputo, said Toyota’s plant would generate around $1.28 billion in annual exports, with about 70% of production dedicated to foreign markets.
Electrek’s Take
Toyota’s “multi-pathway” strategy calls for offering all powertrain options, including gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, battery electric, and fuel cell electric vehicles.
As Chinese brands like BYD gain market share in key global markets such as Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Europe, Toyota is being forced to adapt.
Breaking with its traditional approach, Toyota, like many global OEMs, is
increasingly relying on Chinese batteries
, software, and other vehicle components to compete globally.
Toyota broke ground on a new Lexus EV manufacturing plant in Shanghai last summer. The facility, set to open in 2027, will move at “Lexus speed,” the company calls it, using advanced manufacturing methods, including gigacasting, to cut costs and speed up output.
Its top-selling electric vehicle in China, the bZ3X, reportedly uses nearly 90% locally sourced parts.
After introducing several new or updated all-electric vehicles globally, Toyota has sold considerably more EVs this year.
Through August, Toyota sold 267,649 EVs globally, more than double the number it sold in the same period in 2025.

title: Mazda’s New EV SUV Can Tell Pedestrians Whatever You Want—Even Naughty Words
content:
The automaker had good intentions with the feature, but it forgot to put some guardrails in place.
Photo by:
4:33am ET
The Mazda CX-6e is the automaker’s latest electric SUV.
Based on China’s Deepal S07, it has an external speaker that can deliver audio messages to pedestrians and cyclists.
The driver can input custom text, and there are no banned words.
Mazda’s last EV effort in the United States was short-lived and quite unimpressive. The 100-mile
MX-30 crossover
was very quirky and couldn’t quite offer the kind of driving range expected in the U.S., so it was discontinued after just 600 units reached customers in California.
But despite the lackluster performance stateside,
’s electric portfolio is in full swing overseas, with some help from its Chinese partner Changan. The Japanese automaker, known for the fun-to-drive Miata, recently debuted its latest all-electric crossover in Australia, and it comes with an unexpected and unfiltered feature.
, which is roughly the same size as the Tesla Model Y, is a rather handsome machine, but as
car journalists in Australia
very quickly found out, its standout feature is that it can shout at pedestrians and other road users through its external speaker while driving.
The functionality has been carried over from the Chinese market, where the technically similar Deepal S07 is sold, and the reasons for its existence are likely well-intentioned. Through the “External Announcement” feature, drivers can select prerecorded messages like “Hey, buddy, I’m here,” or “Please look up and focus on the road, stay safe.”
That’s all expected and quite tame, but custom messages can also be written on the massive, 26.45-inch display, and nothing will stop the driver from putting in anything they want, including profanities. It can be quite fun, to be honest, and a future software update will probably fix this little mess.
Until that happens, the Mazda CX-6e can make quite an entrance when going into the supermarket parking lot or when you’re passing by your neighbors. That’s if you happen to live in a country where Mazda’s new EV is sold, like Australia or Europe.
Where it is available, the CX-6e comes with a 78-kilowatt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery pack that can be charged at up to 200 kW and delivers up to 300 miles (484 kilometers) of range on a full charge on the WLTP cycle. There’s just one powertrain configuration, with a 255-horsepower (190 kW) motor powering the rear wheels.

title: The BMW M3 EV Is Almost Done Hiding
content:
The BMW M3 EV Is Almost Done Hiding
The latest teaser shows the electric M3 in its lightest camouflage yet, giving us our clearest look at the production-bound sports sedan.
- BMW’s latest teaser gives us our clearest look yet at the electric M3.
- It tones down the concept’s styling but keeps its muscular stance and distinctive lighting.
- The quad-motor M3 EV is expected to debut in 2027, with production starting that year.
BMW has published new images of the upcoming electric M3, and they are the most revealing yet. This is the car with its finished production body and lights, and even with camouflage, you get a clear idea of where it’s going.
And it’s going somewhere reassuringly close to the M Concept Neue Klasse BMW revealed in June, although it’s predictably less extreme. The production car appears to keep the concept’s muscular stance, but with toned-down aero elements, no ducktail spoiler, and conventional side mirrors replacing the concept’s sculptural, supercar-style items.
The flared wheel arches and the cool ventilated hood remain. So do the yellow headlight graphics and distinctive squared-off lighting elements lower down. Its bulging arches give it a noticeably broader stance than the recently shown i3 M60. Nobody should have trouble telling the full M car apart from the regular i3.
Under the camouflaged body is a version of the Neue Klasse platform with four independent motors, one for each wheel. Final output remains unconfirmed, but rumors suggest some variants could push 1,000 horsepower.
The horsepower number will surely be impressive and higher than in any previous combustion M3, but what will make the first-ever electric model unique is how its quad-motor setup puts that power down. We expect advanced torque vectoring that should let it adjust power at each wheel independently, helping the car rotate through corners, find traction on the way out, and drift as fans expect it to.
The electric M3 won’t be a silent EV. However, unlike Mercedes-AMG, which is trying to imitate its V-8, BMW M has taken a different approach. Engineers studied combustion engine sounds from the most iconic M cars to understand their emotional appeal, then used the electric motors’ own sounds as a foundation. The aim is to provide speed and acceleration cues alongside the drama, not trick you into thinking you’re in a gas-burning M3.
BMW also intends to give buyers a meaningful choice when picking which M3 to buy. Its M division has said the electric and combustion M3 models should sit in the same price ballpark, with a gas-powered successor to today’s G80 on the way.
The bigger question is whether the electric M3 will be good enough to win over fans of the combustion car. Matching it probably won’t cut it. To make enthusiasts truly embrace the switch, it needs to be substantially better—and that advantage has to show up in corners, through the steering wheel and in the urge to take the long way home. The new teaser certainly suggests it will at least look the part.
The electric M3 is expected to be revealed in 2027, with production beginning in Munich that year. BMW hasn’t announced when customer deliveries will start, but it could be before the end of 2027.

title: The Jeep Recon EV Went Just 160 Miles In A Highway Range Test
content:
The Recon’s boxy body and stubby wheels are made for off-roading, but drivers still need to drive on the highway to get to trails.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
5:23am ET
The 2026 Jeep Recon is one of the most inefficient EVs in the U.S. today.
It has an official EPA-estimated combined range of 222 miles.
At highway speeds, that figure drops dramatically, as discovered by
Car and Driver
It’s no secret that the
Jeep Recon loves to eat electricity
with a big spoon every time it hits the road. It was designed to take you where no other electric car can, so it had to have a boxy body, bumpers that aren’t exactly aerodynamic, and big, chunky wheels.
is hungry for energy, and owners will need to understand that they’re trading long-range convenience for off-road capabilities. Now, though, customers can get a rough idea of how far they can go on a full charge when they’re not on the trails.
Gallery: 2026 Jeep Recon: First Drive Photo Gallery
Car and Driver
drove a brand-new Recon on the highway at a constant 75 miles per hour and managed just 160 miles with a full battery. That’s 62 miles less than the combined EPA estimate, and it’s also 36 miles shorter than the EPA estimate for highway-only driving.
Considering that the Recon is powered by a rather generous 94-kilowatt-hour (100.5 kWh total) battery pack, the efficiency is one of the worst of any EV on sale today in the United States. According to
Car and Driver
, Jeep’s off-road-ready electric model averaged about 1.7 miles/kWh, which is a smidge better than the outrageous 1.4 miles/kWh achieved by the
GMC Hummer EV
Mercedes-Benz G 580 Electric
It’s worth noting that here at InsideEVs, we test cars at a constant 70 mph on the highway, and the Recon is expected to travel further at a lower speed. For drivers who like to go faster, though, they now have a point of reference—as long as they’re comfortable driving from 100% state of charge to zero.
When sticking to the 10-to-80% rule of thumb, just 70% of the car’s battery is available, which, in the Recon’s case, means a real-world range of 112 miles at a constant 75 mph. It gets better when cruising at low speeds, though. During our short time with the Recon, the instrument cluster showed around 2.5 miles/kWh.
All of this means plenty of charging on the road, and probably at trailheads, with
claiming a 10-to-80% time of 23 minutes. That's more than decent, but the bills will be higher than on most other EVs, simply because the electric off-roader needs more of it.

content:
Toyota’s New Hydrogen Bus Has 50% More Range
That’s despite having less hydrogen on board than its predecessor.
- Toyota and Isuzu have unveiled a new hydrogen fuel cell bus.
- The second-generation Sora bus needs less hydrogen to travel further.
- Its three tanks can be refueled in as little as ten minutes, while the range is quoted at over 186 miles.
Toyota is still keeping the hydrogen dream alive, though at a scale that’s not even close to the automaker’s hybrid vehicle might. We all know about the slow-selling Mirai and the refueling nightmare that the few American owners have to go through to keep their cars running, but now there’s a new kid on the block.
This is the second-generation Toyota Sora urban and regional bus, which is powered by the Japanese giant’s latest hydrogen fuel cell stack. A fuel cell stack mounted on the roof generates electric power, which is then sent to an ordinary electric powertrain built by Isuzu.
Toyota Sora (2026) FCEV bus
In fact, the whole vehicle—except for the roof-mounted hydrogen powertrain—is a rebadged Isuzu ERGA EV, which debuted in 2024, and Isuzu is now cashing in on the partnership by launching its own ERGA FCV variant.
Under the skin, there’s a pair of 110-kilowatt electric motors making a combined 295 horsepower and 715 pound-feet of torque. The motors draw power from an 88-kilowatt-hour lithium-ion battery that enables a driving range of over 186 miles (300 kilometers), which is roughly 50% more than the first-generation Sora bus that debuted in 2018. The fuel cell stack can deliver up to 113 kW of power.
The 471-liter tanks on the roof can be refilled in about ten minutes, but Toyota claims that future filling stations will be able to cut the refueling time in half. Just like the first-gen Toyota Sora, the new FCEV people hauler can export power from its high-voltage battery through an external power supply, transforming it into an emergency power source for disasters or other situations where the grid goes down for long periods of time.
Inside, the bus has a fully flat floor and an optional one-touch securement system, making life easier for wheelchair users. Four versions are available, with two styles reserved for urban use and two for suburban routes, each with different seat layouts.
Gallery: Toyota Sora (2026)
On the tech side, the new Sora comes with the Emergency Driver Stop System (EDSS) and the Driver Status Monitor (DSM), which can bring the bus to a complete stop if they detect that the driver is no longer able to drive.
The second-generation Toyota Sora is expected to go into production in the 2026 fiscal year that runs from April 2026 to March 2027. The bus will be built by J-Bus, a 50:50 joint venture between Isuzu and Hino Motors, at the Utsunomiya Plant in Japan’s Tochigi Prefecture.

title: OpenAI 将在 ChatGPT 中推出全新图片广告形式，不会影响生成结果
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 5 日消息，OpenAI 今日宣布，将在 ChatGPT 中推出全新的图片广告形式，扩充广告效果衡量工具与合作生态，并研发新方案用于评估品牌适配性。
IT之家从官方介绍获悉，
ChatGPT 每周覆盖 12 亿用户
，是全球规模最大的原生 AI 消费平台。这款全新图片广告形式，能够帮助用户想象产品与服务如何融入日常生活。广告图片可以展示产品灵感、使用场景或是产品带来的体验，让用户认识新品牌、了解产品的独特优势，辅助消费决策。对广告主而言，这也创造了借助图片讲述品牌故事的新机会。
团队会在 ChatGPT 的图像生成功能中测试该广告样式
。广告会做清晰标注，和用户正在生成的图片相互独立。和我们其他广告形式一样，广告内容不会影响 ChatGPT 给出的回答。本次测试将于本月晚些时候在美国启动，首批会邀请部分广告主参与。
OpenAI 提到，全新图片广告形式，助力用户发掘产品服务、想象产品如何融入生活，也让广告主拥有更直观的视觉化品牌叙事方式。整体来看，ChatGPT 广告新增的效果衡量能力、品牌适配评估能力，帮助企业评估广告活动效果，对广告投放场景建立信心。以上所有功能都遵循广告原则：
ChatGPT 的回答保持独立客观，用户对话隐私受保护，用户掌握自身使用体验的控制权
OpenAI 表示会持续迭代广告平台，推出新广告样式与能力，帮助企业以贴合用户需求的有效方式触达客户，为各类规模的企业创造增长机遇。

title: OpenAI 将在欧盟为 ChatGPT 和 Codex 文本输出添加隐形水印
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 5 日消息，OpenAI 今日宣布，为配合《欧盟人工智能法案》的内容透明要求，未来几周将在欧盟地区符合条件的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 文本输出中加入机器可识别的隐形水印。
据介绍，文本水印技术名为
textGrain（文本粒水印）
，会在模型选词过程中嵌入不可见的统计信号。检测器通过识别该信号，判断一段文本是否带有 OpenAI 水印。
IT之家注意到，OpenAI 下一步将在欧盟推广文本水印。未来几周，团队将仅在欧盟所有计划中向符合条件的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 用户引入文本水印功能。值得一提的是，OpenAI 不会在发布时将文本水印设为全球默认。
OpenAI 将为 API 客户启用选择加入的水印功能。从今天起，全球的 API 客户将能够选择为部分模型添加水印文本输出。这让客户能够决定水印如何符合其透明度义务以及为用户提供的体验。团队还在与云合作伙伴合作，在未来几周内为通过其服务访问的 OpenAI 模型输出提供水印功能。
OpenAI 还将为研究人员和专家组织提供探测器访问，获批的研究人员和专家组织可以申请从今天开始。根据行为准则访问最初将根据具体情况逐案授予，以支持文本来源的评估和改进。该工具会报告是否检测到 OpenAI 水印，但不会透露用户身份或提示内容或对话内容。

title: 卡普空开源 RE:Dox 结构化数据引擎，JSON 反序列化最高提速 2.84 倍
content:
IT之家 10 月 5 日消息，卡普空宣布，将旗下最新的数据处理及序列化基础库“RE:Dox”以开源软件（OSS）形式公开。该项目是卡普空次世代游戏引擎计划 REX（RE neXt ENGINE）的基础技术之一，开发者可以自由使用。
卡普空早在 2023 年 10 月便公布了 REX 引擎计划，目标是针对 RE ENGINE 长期使用后逐渐出现的问题进行改进，通过阶段性更新推动引擎迈向下一代。例如先前卡普空于 10 月 2 日在东京举办的技术展示活动“CAPCOM Open Conference RE:2026”中便介绍了 REX 计划的未来规划，并同步公开构成 REX 的基础技术之一“RE:Dox”。
据介绍，RE:Dox 本身是一款针对 .NET 的 Token-based 结构化数据引擎，主要用于将不同数据转换为统一格式和规则，从而提高数据处理、编辑及读取效率。
卡普空在 GitHub 的 README 中提供了实际使用示例。以玩家数据为例，原本以 JSON 格式记录的角色数据可以通过 RE:Dox 提供的类进行处理，例如创建一名 42 级、持有手枪和绿色药草的里昂，随后读取数据并将角色名称修改为“克蕾儿”，甚至追加“小刀”等道具。
根据官方公布的基准测试，在并行处理 JSON 反序列化（deserialization）时，RE:Dox 相较 .NET 标准的 System.Text.Json，理论最高可实现约 2.84 倍的处理速度。不过，实际运行表现仍可能受到数据结构、运行环境以及 CPU 等因素影响。
目前 RE:Dox 已按照 Apache-2.0 许可证开源。开发者只要符合许可证要求，即可自由使用和修改，甚至将其应用于商业项目。IT之家附项目地址（https://github.com/CAPCOM-TD-OSS/REDox/tree/main）。

title: 海外消费者网购下单两次 AMD 锐龙 7 9850X3D 处理器，均被调包成十年前的酷睿 i3-3000 系列产品
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 5 日消息，近日一名海外网友在亚马逊连续两次购买 AMD 锐龙 7 9850X3D 处理器，结果其购买的处理器均遭到调包，被换成了酷睿 i3-3000 系列处理器，引发社区热议。
据报道，Reddit 网友 BitProfessional3792 最初通过亚马逊官方商店购买了一颗 AMD 锐龙 7 9850X3D，但收到商品后发现处理器疑似遭到调包。商品外包装看起来正常，封条也没有破损，但盒内真正的处理器却被替换成了距今约 10 年的英特尔酷睿 i3-3000 系列产品。
对此，该网友认为“可能只是运气不好”，于是再次通过亚马逊下单购买一颗锐龙 7 9850X3D。为了防止再次出现问题，其在收货时全程进行录像。然而打开包装后，他发现商品竟然再次遭到调包，而且手法完全相同，盒内依旧是一颗英特尔酷睿 i3-3000 系列处理器。
最终，该网友对亚马逊失去信任，选择直接驾车前往当地 Best Buy 线下门店购买处理器。
该网友表示，两次购买总计花费约 1,600 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 10,737 元人民币）
，目前亚马逊正在处理相关退款事宜。不过，两次订单都以相同方式遭遇调包，也让部分网友怀疑问题可能出在仓储或物流环节，甚至不排除有人能够在官方发货流程中对商品进行替换。
还有网友注意到，两次商品包装盒上都贴有 LPN 标签。这类标签用于标记亚马逊退货商品，因此有观点认为，问题可能与退货商品重新进入库存的流程有关。例如有人截取退货商品包装，再放入其他处理器，以此绕过后续重新上架时的检查；也不排除商品在装箱或发货前遭到替换的可能。
目前尚无法确认具体的调包环节及责任方。不过，如果类似情况确实发生在仓储或物流环节，意味着相关流程存在较为严重的漏洞。由于 SSD、内存等小型且价值较高的电脑硬件同样容易被替换，此类问题也可能对其他高价值商品造成影响。至于亚马逊内部自动化系统是否存在可被利用的漏洞，目前同样没有确凿证据。

title: 玩家“魔改”12V-2×6：引入额外 2 组 8Pin 分流供电，减负效果显著
content:

10 月 5 日消息，Reddit 网友 @DallasGrave 近日展示了其 12V-2×6 的修改方案：该玩家
为显卡的 12+4 Pin 接口补充了 2 组 PCIe 8Pin 供电
，达成分流减负的效果。
▲ 该卡为微星 GeForce RTX 5090 32G VENTUS 3X OC
@DallasGrave 在原始 12V-2×6 接头的触点上焊接了一块拥有 2 个 PCIe 8Pin 接口的 PCB 小板，与 12V-2×6 一道
实现“三路”同时供电
根据其描述，这种改装后所有导线的功耗和温度都大幅降低，电流仅为 3A 左右。该显卡在 550W 满载下运行了 28 小时，即使在接头处，线缆温度也从未超过 40℃。
值得注意的是，这种改装需要一定的知识和技巧，
原则上无法彻底消除 12V-2×6 的过热风险
还可能引入新的隐患
，IT之家的小伙伴切勿轻易尝试。

content:
IT之家 10 月 5 日消息，香蕉派 (Banana Pi) 上月末推出了 BPI-CM7。这一核心板基于全志 (Allwinner) H618 芯片，拥有 4 个 Arm Cortex-A53 CPU 核心、Arm Mali-G31 GPU。
