title: INTERVIEW: Hithium’s sodium-ion storage push, where it could win, where it won't, and path to bankability - Energy Storage
content: After Chinese manufacturer Hithium launched its new 4 MWh sodium-ion BESS alongside its new 785Ah cell for energy storage, in response to questions, Leb Lan, senior product manager, Hithium , spoke with ESS News to discuss not only the technology developments but also where and when a sodium-ion BESS cabinet will better suit the market than LFP-based battery cell technology. ESS News: Your company has progressed rapidly in sodium-ion cells and energy storage systems. Is this the major step the technology needed, or do you expect advances of this significance to continue at a similar pace? Leb Lan, senior product manager, Hithium: We see this launch as an important step in moving sodium-ion energy storage from technology validation toward large-scale deployment. As materials, manufacturing processes and the supply chain continue to mature, we expect further improvements in both performance and economics. The motivation goes beyond introducing another battery chemistry. As global energy storage deployment expands, the industry is paying closer attention to the concentration of lithium resources, cyclical lithium carbonate prices, and the availability and predictability of materials over the 20- to 30-year life of energy infrastructure. Sodium is abundant and widely distributed. This can reduce dependence on concentrated critical resources. Sodium-ion technology also has strong potential for long cycle life, which can reduce replacement and augmentation requirements over the project lifetime and lower the cost of delivered energy. This supports energy equity by making reliable storage more accessible and affordable across different markets. Further progress will come from coordinated improvements in materials, cells, manufacturing and system design. We expect continued gains in energy density, manufacturing consistency, system efficiency and supply-chain scale. However, the most important measure of progress is not the size of each technology announcement. The real measure of progress is our ability to translate laboratory performance into energy storage products that can be manufactured consistently, validated thoroughly and deployed at a bankable scale. How much of the new cell and system has been validated outside the laboratory and in real-world conditions? We separate validation into two levels. Our first-generation sodium-ion platform allowed us to complete the engineering chain from materials and cells to system integration. This work included safety testing, manufacturing-process validation and real-world project application. It also gave us practical experience in system integration, thermal management, BMS control, manufacturing consistency and supply-chain coordination. Some project details and operating data remain subject to customer confidentiality agreements. For the new-generation product, we are planning a staged validation program covering the cell, module, system and real-world operating environment. The validation work will progress in line with product development and demonstration-project schedules, providing a basis for future customer evaluations and large-scale deployment. Regarding fire-safety standards, what tests have you completed? For our first-generation ∞Cell N162Ah sodium-ion cell, we completed the relevant safety tests under GB/T 44265. These included drop, crush, external short circuit, overcharge, over-discharge and thermal-runaway testing. At the material level, we use a polyanion cathode chemistry with high thermal stability. We have also optimized the separator, electrolyte, pressure-relief design and gas-generation characteristics. However, material stability alone does not justify an absolute safety claim. Safety must be verified at the cell, module and system levels. Building on the validation of our first-generation product, we are now conducting further safety testing on the new cell and system. The current work focuses on thermal propagation, gas release and pressure relief, fire-protection coordination, thermal management and transportation safety to verify reliability under practical energy-storage operating conditions. How does pricing compare with your LFP products? What would the capital expenditure (CAPEX) look like for a theoretical ‘Project A’ 100 MW / 200 MWh BESS using LFP versus sodium-ion? Giving a single price without defining a common project boundary could be misleading. The CAPEX of a 100 MW / 200 MWh project includes much more than the batteries. It also includes the PCS, medium-voltage equipment, civil works, grid connection, fire protection, installation, commissioning and any planned augmentation. At today’s industrial scale, mature LFP supply chains will generally retain an initial CAPEX advantage for a conventional two-hour project. The economic value of sodium-ion should not be assessed only by the initial purchase price. The comparison also needs to consider cycling frequency, project life, efficiency, degradation, augmentation, operating costs and exposure to raw-material price volatility. For projects with frequent cycling, long operating lives or a strong need for predictable long-term costs, sodium-ion has the potential to deliver a competitive LCOS through higher lifetime energy throughput. Its initial cost can also decline as the material ecosystem and supply chain scale. For a theoretical ‘Project A’, we would prefer to provide a transparent CAPEX and LCOS comparison using the same assumptions for PCS, grid connection, EPC scope, operating profile and project life, rather than offering a headline number without those conditions. Do you expect sodium-ion to beat LFP for utility-scale customers in certain scenarios? If so, which ones? We do not position sodium-ion as a technology that will replace or defeat LFP across every application. The two chemistries will serve different customer needs. LFP has a mature industrial base, higher energy density and significant economies of scale. It will continue to serve a large share of mainstream storage projects. Sodium-ion is more likely to create value first in projects with frequent cycling, long operating lives, or a strong focus on material availability and long-term cost stability. For a utility-scale customer, the most important comparison is not simply cell price or energy density. It is the amount of energy the system can reliably deliver over the project lifetime and the total cost of delivering that energy. If sodium-ion can reduce LCOS through longer life, potentially lower augmentation needs and more predictable material costs, it can become the better choice for those specific operating profiles. Our role is to match the technology to the project’s operating conditions and economic model, rather than claiming that one chemistry is universally superior. Is sodium-ion bankable? Have you worked with insurers to demonstrate that? For an emerging technology such as sodium-ion, bankability needs to be established for each product and project. It depends on independent testing, long-term operating data, manufacturing consistency, warranty terms and long-term service capability. Our first-generation product has provided a foundation of evidence at the cell, manufacturing and system-engineering levels. For the new generation, we are building the technical basis required for future third-party evaluation, project application, warranties and service support. We do not publicly comment on discussions with individual insurers or financial institutions. Our focus is to build a complete body of evidence that customers, technical advisers, lenders and insurers can assess independently. What still needs to happen before customers will order sodium-ion systems at scale? Large-scale sodium-ion deployment requires technology, manufacturing capacity and the supply chain to scale together. First, the industry needs to further expand the stable, large-scale supply of key materials, including hard-carbon anodes, so that material availability can grow alongside sodium-ion production capacity and support large-scale cell and system production. Second, cells and systems need continued testing and real-world project experience to build further evidence of performance, safety and reliability. Manufacturing capability, supplier quality management, product certification, warranty structures and long-term service capabilities also need to develop alongside production capacity. Finally, customers, technical advisers, lenders and insurers need sufficient, verifiable data to assess technical risk and lifecycle economics. As material supply expands, manufacturing capability improves, project experience accumulates and economic performance is validated, sodium-ion technology will be increasingly ready to support larger customer orders. title: Origin plans 4.9 GWh battery expansion in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Australia’s biggest energy retailer is seeking federal environmental approval to build an eight-hour battery energy storage system (BESS) that will add 500 MW of capacity to the battery precinct being built next to the Eraring power station on the New South Wales (NSW) Central Coast. Origin is seeking approval under the federal Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (EPBC) Act for the Eraring BESS North project that proposes the construction of a battery with a discharge capacity of 500 MW and an accessible energy storage capacity of about 4,942 MWh. In its EPBC referral, Origin says the project responds to “structural shifts in the National Electricity Market (NEM) as the electricity sector transitions from coal-fired generation toward variable renewable energy, supported by dispatchable firming capacity such as electricity storage.” “The development of large-scale BESS projects is critical to the ongoing transition to renewable energy,” Origin said. “The NSW Electricity Infrastructure Roadmap targets at least 12 GW of renewable generation and 2 GW of long-duration storage by 2030, while the Australian Energy Market Operator’s 2024 Integrated System Plan forecasts that the NEM must triple grid-scale variable renewable energy by 2030, creating a firming gap that this project will help address.” The Sydney-headquartered utility said the Eraring BESS North would operate in conjunction with the existing Eraring BESS precinct that is being built in stages. The 460 MW / 1,770 MWh first phase of the Eraring BESS was connected to the National Electricity Market (NEM) at the start of 2026 and construction is continuing on the 240 MW / 1, 390 MWh second stage that is due to come online early in 2027. While the public numbers don’t add up, Origin said in its scoping report that once complete, the Eraring BESS will comprise an energy storage capacity of approximately 3,658 MWh. Together, the existing and proposed BESS facilities would provide a combined maximum registered active power capacity of about 1,200 MW and a combined accessible energy storage capacity of approximately 8,600 MWh. “This dispatchable capability decouples the project’s output from weather-dependent generation profiles, allowing it to serve periods of high demand independent of wind and solar conditions, particularly during evening peak hours,” Origin said. Construction of the Eraring BESS North project is planned to be launched in 2028, with commercial operations scheduled for early-to-mid 2031. Origin said the Eraring North BESS will contribute to its commitments to achieve net zero by 2050 and support its shift away from coal . The 2.88 GW Eraring power station, the nation’s largest coal-fired generator, is scheduled to close in April 2029. title: Poland unveils significant new home storage subsidy - Energy Storage
content: Poland’s Ministry of Climate and Environment has announced a $257.9 million (PLN 1 billion) subsidy scheme for home battery and heat storage, aimed at increasing self-consumption from residential solar and other renewable energy installations. The program is open to individuals with grid-connected home solar or other small renewable electricity systems. It will subsidize batteries with at least 10 kWh of capacity and heat storage tanks holding at least 100 liters. Batteries must provide at least 2 kWh of storage per kWp of the accompanying solar installation. The scheme will cover the costs of purchasing and installing home storage systems. Battery grants will cover up to 30% of eligible costs, capped at approximately $206 (PLN 800) per kWh. Prosumers in the net-billing system can receive up to approximately $4,126 (PLN 16,000), while those in the net-metering system can receive up to approximately $2,063 (PLN 8,000). Applicants can receive up to 30% of eligible costs for EU-manufactured heat storage systems, capped at approximately $258 (PLN 1,000). An additional bonus of up to approximately $516 (PLN 2,000) is available for an EU-manufactured battery or a necessary replacement EU-manufactured hybrid inverter. Total support is capped at approximately $4,900 (PLN 19,000) per electricity supply point. The scheme is financed through the Modernization Fund. Applications will open on October 20 and close on October 1, 2027, or when funds are exhausted. Poland’s Minister of Climate and Environment, Paulina Hennig-Kloska, said equipping residential solar installations with energy storage is a ministerial priority. “The program has two main goals: increasing the efficiency of renewable energy use and strengthening energy security,” she added. According to the ministry, the number of home energy storage systems in Poland rose from more than 10,000 in the first quarter of 2024 to around 150,000 in June 2026, supported by subsidies and market growth. The ministry is targeting more than 200,000 home storage systems by the end of 2027. Sławomir Ćwik, deputy minister of climate and environment, said eligible battery installations must include an energy management system and backup power capability. “This allows households to maintain power even during grid outages,” Ćwik said. An initial phase of support financed through Poland’s National Recovery Plan allocated approximately $28.9 million (PLN 112 million) to support the installation of more than 5,000 home battery systems, according to the ministry. Poland’s Agency for Restructuring and Modernization of Agriculture recently announced a renewable energy subsidy scheme aimed at farmers. It opened for applications on October 5. Following Australia In Australia, the Federal government similarly offered a 30% subsidy on home installations of residential batteries , without a monetary or kWh cap, or need for existing solar installation, though some restrictions were added to cap the total installation sizing. The scheme has been budgeted to approximately AU$7.2 billion (US$4.68 billion or PLN 18.15 billion), and has seen more than 500,000 households add storage, or some 13 to 14 GWh of behind-the-meter storage capacity. title: BMW's new iX4 leaks days ahead of its debut [Images]
content:

is expected to reveal the new iX4 this week. Ahead of its debut, images of the new iX4 leaked online, offering an early look.
Leaked images reveal the new BMW iX4
The all-new iX4 is almost here. BMW said the new electric coupe-SUV will go on sale by the end of 2026.
Following the iX3 and i3, the iX4 will replace the current X4 with BMW’s updated Neue Klasse design and technology.
The 2027 BMW iX4 will be available in two versions: the 40 xDrive and 50 xDrive. Both are all-wheel drive (AWD), but will offer different performance and range options.
It will essentially be a sportier, more crossover-like sibling to the new iX3 SUV. Like the iX3 and i3, the iX4 will use BMW’s sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive and a 108.7 kWh battery.
The 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive offers a WLTP range of up to 500 miles (805 km). In the US, it uses a 112.2-kWh battery, providing an EPA-estimated range of up to 434 miles.

While BMW has yet to confirm a specific debut date, we know the iX4 will make its first appearance this fall. With its debut just around the corner, leaked images of the new iX4 by
@Kero_Wolf
apparently reveal the interior and exterior.
The images show a design similar to the
disguised prototypes
spotted testing over the past several months.

With a rakish roofline, BMW’s new iX4 looks more like a grand tourer than a traditional SUV like the iX3. It trades the boxy SUV look for a sporty, fastback-like silhouette.

title: Kia EV3 first drive: the affordable EV we have been waiting for
content:
The Kia EV3 starts at $29,890 in the US, and after a day of driving it around Vancouver Island, I think it’s the best-packaged affordable EV you can buy right now.
It comes with up to 321 miles of range, two battery sizes, and available all-wheel drive, which is more choice than anything else at this price. But there’s a catch: that $30,000 price tag climbs fast.
Kia brought me to Vancouver Island last week to test the EV3 as it launches in North America.
The Korean automaker took its time. The EV3 has been on sale overseas since 2024, and it quickly became one of the most popular EVs in Europe and won the 2025 World Car of the Year award before Kia finally decided to bring it here.
Now it’s here. US sales started in mid-August, and Kia told us it has about 1,300 units in dealer stock. According to the company, dealers love it because it’s bringing more shoppers into showrooms.
A Bolt EV with more options
Kia sees the EV3 as a competitor to the Chevy Bolt and the Nissan Leaf. Those are pretty much your only other choices if you want a new EV around $30,000 in the US.
The 2027 Bolt starts at $28,995 with 262 miles of range, and the 2026 Leaf starts at $29,990 with up to 303 miles. The EV3 lands right between them at $29,890 before a $1,495 destination fee.
The way I see it, the EV3 is really a Bolt EV that’s better packaged and comes with more options. You get to pick between two battery packs, front-wheel or all-wheel drive, and five trims, so you can end up with something closer to what you really want. Neither the Bolt nor the Leaf offers AWD.
The base Light FWD comes with a 58.3 kWh pack that’s good for 221 miles. For $34,990, the Wind FWD gets the 81.4 kWh pack and the full 321 miles. All-wheel drive adds a second motor for 261 hp and brings range down to 280 miles. At the top, the $45,890 GT makes 288 hp and gets to 60 mph in 5.4 seconds.
The EV3 also takes over from the Niro EV, which started at $39,700 with 253 miles of range. So Kia’s entry-level EV just got about $10,000 cheaper.
Small footprint, big battery
The EV3 is a boxy-looking compact SUV with Kia’s “tiger face” front end and the same design language as the EV6 and EV9.
Boxy usually means bad aero. But Kia focused on aero optimization and got the drag coefficient down to 0.275.
That’s a big reason why the base version gets impressive range out of a relatively small pack. And Kia still managed to fit a big 81.4 kWh pack into a vehicle that’s just 169.3 inches long. According to Kia, the new pack has 22% higher energy density than the one in the Niro EV.
The EV3 rides on a 400-volt version of the E-GMP platform, so don’t expect EV6 charging speeds. Peak rates are about 100 kW and 127 kW depending on the pack, but peak charge rates aren’t the whole story. At virtually any DC fast-charging station, you’ll be able to charge to 80% in roughly 30 minutes. Kia says that’s about 30% faster than the Niro EV.
It comes with a NACS port and Plug & Charge, which Kia says gives you access to more than 40,000 DC fast chargers.
Inside, you get 26 cubic feet of cargo space behind the rear seats and about 56 cubic feet with them folded.
There’s also a 0.9 cubic-foot frunk. It’s small, but we often don’t see any frunk on a vehicle of this form factor, and Kia says it’s the only one in this segment. We appreciate Kia making the effort.
Kia says the EV3 has 99.7 cubic feet of passenger volume, which it claims is more than any of its direct competitors.
When I sat in the back seat, I felt I had plenty of legroom with the front seat at a normal position, but when sitting straight, my head was within 3 inches of the ceiling (I’m 6ft tall).
The tech is what you’d expect from a more expensive EV: over-the-air updates, Apple CarPlay, and apps like YouTube and Netflix. Highway Driving Assist is standard on every trim, and a head-up display is available on the GT.
One thing to watch: vehicle-to-load (V2L) isn’t available below the GT-Line. On the trims that have it, Kia includes the external adapter.
Driving the EV3
Kia sent us on a loop out of Victoria: north over the Malahat, west to Port Renfrew, and back along the coast. I drove the Wind FWD and the GT-Line AWD.
The driving experience is impressive for an entry-level EV. The FWD version makes 201 hp and the AWD makes 261 hp. I never felt like I didn’t have enough power in either of them.
The EV3 also felt planted on the road, even on the tough logging roads around Vancouver Island. For a vehicle in that segment, I was pleasantly surprised by the driving experience.
Every EV3 gets four-wheel independent suspension, and Kia adds acoustic laminated glass on the windshield and front windows from the Wind trim up.
Then there’s one-pedal driving, and it feels great. Kia’s new i-Pedal 3.0 gives you three regen levels, and you turn it on by pulling and holding the left paddle.
And Kia finally remembers your preferred setting between drives. If you’ve owned a Kia or Hyundai EV, you know how annoying it was to turn i-Pedal back on every time you got in the car.
The price goes up fast
My main concern is the “affordable” part.
It’s true that you can get an EV3 for $30,000. But the cheapest version I tested was still $41,000, and the GT-Line AWD starts at $43,490. The price goes up fast depending on the options, so be on the lookout for that.
The good news is that you don’t have to go that high. You can get the base version for $29,890, or the max range in a well-equipped Wind FWD for $34,990. That one looks like the sweet spot of the lineup.
Electrek’s Take
This is the affordable EV we have been waiting for.
To be fair, the bar isn’t high. The other choices around $30,000 are very limited, with just the Bolt EV and the Leaf. But the EV3 gives you more than either of them: two battery sizes, up to 321 miles of range, and AWD if you need it.
It’s a Bolt EV that’s better packaged, with enough optionality to get you closer to the vehicle you really want. And that’s from someone who likes the Bolt EV.
Top comment by OliveFries
We really wanted a Kia EV3 to replace our second car but after our first Kia EV9 ownership experience we're looking at different options. Our Kia dealership and more importantly Kia America experiences have completely turned us away from wanting to own another one. Our EV9 was down for 2 months after the rear motor failed with only a few thousand miles and somehow it wasn't available. After some time sitting at the shop I opened a case with Kia America to assist. They had a single phone call with me and one with the dealership then did absolutely nothing. Nobody could get ahold of the case manager until after I already had the car back (over a month).
They then told me they'd take care of the car payments as a "goodwill" gesture for the down time only to find out I had to completely waive my lemon law rights for this and any future repairs on the vehicle. This supposedly also includes a non-disparagement agreement. Nothing about it was "goodwill", it was purely to keep me silent about my experience.
Absolutely disgusting behavior.
My worry is the pricing. If most of the EV3s on dealer lots look like the $41,000 one I drove, a lot of buyers will never see the “affordable EV” Kia is advertising. The $30,000 and $35,000 versions are the ones that matter.
But I think this can be a popular vehicle in North America like it already is in Europe. Kia sold 514 of them in the first full month, and I expect that number to go up from here as long as the Korean brand is making them available.

title: Tesla sold under 1,000 cars in its first year in India, but it's ramping
content:
Tesla Model Y
Tesla Model YL
Fred Lambert
| Oct 6 2026 - 6:58 am PT
Tesla has registered just 993 vehicles in India since it started deliveries there in September 2025, according to registration data compiled by Indian EV publication
ElecTree
But 294 of those came in September 2026 alone. That’s a record month for Tesla in India, and it comes right after the automaker cut prices and launched the six-seat Model Y L.
Tesla needed nine months to sell 428 cars
launched in India in July 2025
with a Model Y priced at roughly $70,000, almost twice what it cost in the US at the time. We said the price didn’t make sense.
The numbers agreed. Tesla registered 69 cars in September 2025, its first month of deliveries, and it didn’t beat that figure for the next eight months. It finished 2025 with 226 registrations and added only 202 more between January and May 2026, per ElecTree’s count. February was the low point at 29 cars.
A note on the “first year” math. The data covers 13 calendar months, September 2025 through September 2026. Count only the first 12 and Tesla is at 699 cars.
These are also registrations, not deliveries. Tesla doesn’t report sales by country, so registrations are the closest thing we get.
A price cut and the Model Y L changed the trend
Tesla made two moves this spring.
On April 22, it launched the Model Y L in India at ₹61.99 lakh (about $65,000), with deliveries starting in June. The longer six-seater came in cheaper than the five-seat Model Y Long Range, which was listed at ₹67.89 lakh (about $71,000) and has since been dropped from the lineup.
Then in late May, Tesla cut the entry-level Model Y by ₹9 lakh, from ₹59.89 lakh to ₹50.89 lakh. That’s a 15% cut, and it brings the starting price to about $53,000.
Registrations took off from there:
Month (2026)
Model Y L
Entry Model Y
Tesla total
September
That’s 565 registrations in four months, more than the 428 Tesla managed in its first nine.
The Model Y L is doing most of the work. It has 425 registrations in four months, which is exactly what the entry-level Model Y has put up in 13. In September, the six-seater accounted for 81% of Tesla’s registrations in India.
Model Y L launched in the US in July at $61,990
. So before taxes and fees, Indian buyers are paying within about $3,000 of the US price for an imported car, in a country with import duties of up to 110%. A year ago, Tesla was asking them to pay almost double.
It’s still a lot more than the roughly $47,000 the Model Y L launched at in China, where Tesla builds it.
Tesla has also added locations. It started with showrooms in Mumbai, Delhi, and Gurugram, and ElecTree reports that it has since opened in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Noida.
Tesla is still a rounding error in India
India registered 35,995 electric cars in September, up 98% from a year ago, according to
Vahan registration data reported by Autocar Professional
. Tata alone did 14,769. Tesla’s record month works out to 0.8% of India’s EV market.
Tesla looks better in the luxury segment. The same data has BMW at 502 electric cars in September, Tesla at 291, and Mercedes-Benz at 125.
So Tesla is now the second-biggest luxury EV brand in India with about 30% of the segment, up from 69 cars in the same month last year.
The comparison that stings is VinFast. The Vietnamese automaker registered its first cars in India the same month Tesla did. But it assembles them at a plant in Tamil Nadu, and it prices its SUVs between ₹18 lakh and ₹23 lakh (about $19,000 to $24,000).
VinFast registered 2,963 cars in India in September. That’s three times what Tesla has done in 13 months, in a single month.
Different price class, obviously. But it shows what building locally gets you in India.
Electrek’s Take
In January, we wrote that you can’t sell a $40,000 car for $70,000 and expect volume. Tesla tried it anyway and got 40 to 60 cars a month.
Then it cut the entry price by 15%, brought in a bigger car for less than the old top trim, and now it’s at almost 300 a month.
It must be a bit confusing for the Indian consumer.
It’s also hard to tell how much price changes affect volume compared to expansions in other cities.
Either way, for now, it looks like Tesla is not giving up on the Indian market despite the lackluster performance.

title: This funky solar electric scooter could handle your commute without ever plugging in
content:
Electric Motorcycles
electric scooter
Micah Toll
| Oct 6 2026 - 6:11 am PT
There are plenty of ways to build a small electric vehicle. These days, the prevailing options have been to make it faster, give it more power, slap on bigger tires, or keep adding features until your humble little scooter has somehow turned into a 150-pound electric motorcycle.
Or you can be brave and go in the other direction to ask a simpler question: How much vehicle do people actually need for all those short trips around town?
That’s essentially the idea behind the Lightfoot, a wonderfully weird new solar-powered electric scooter from San Francisco R&D company Otherlab. The two-seat electric scooter tops out at just under 20 mph (32 km/h), carries a surprisingly large amount of cargo, and covers both sides of its body in solar panels capable of adding up to 18 miles (29 km) of range per day.
And as someone who has long argued that
we need more small electric vehicles
– not simply faster and heavier e-bikes and e-mopeds – I’m pretty intrigued.
The Lightfoot has actually been kicking around for a while, and I covered
the prototype’s unveiling
nearly two years ago. But now it’s finally available for sale and delivery. The first 100 Launch Edition scooters
are priced at $4,495 including delivery
, with a refundable $100 reservation required to get in line. Those initial scooters will be available in sky blue and solar orange. A bit on the nose, but I like it.
Sure, $4.5k certainly isn’t cheap for a 20 mph electric scooter.
But then again, there aren’t many other electric scooters that can recharge themselves while you’re buying groceries, or fit 45 liters (1.6 cubic feet) of those groceries inside their body panels on the ride home instead of wearing a hiking backpack full of grains and veggies.
Yes, those solar panels actually do something
The most visually obvious feature of the Lightfoot is the pair of 120W solar panels built directly into the sides of the scooter.
Together, the 240W system can add a claimed 3-4 miles (5-6 km) of range per hour in good sunlight, or as much as 18 miles (29 km) over the course of a day.
That’s actually a meaningful amount of solar charging for this type of vehicle.
The trick is that Lightfoot doesn’t require much energy in the first place. Its 52V and 1,560Wh battery is rated for up to 37 miles (60 km) of range. That means someone commuting 5 miles (8 km) each way and leaving the scooter parked outside all day could theoretically replenish most or even all of their daily energy from sunlight under favorable conditions.
Of course, let’s keep the solar thing in perspective. A 1.5 kWh battery isn’t exactly an electric Hummer battery pack. Lightfoot includes a 230W onboard charger and can be plugged into a normal wall outlet, with a full charge taking around four hours. So that means sunshine isn’t necessary to make the scooter practical; it simply gives owners another option.
But there’s something undeniably cool about owning a vehicle that you might rarely need to plug in if your daily trips are short enough.
Sure, there may be downsides. It looks like a strong crosswind could have you tacking back and forth across the lane like a sailboat, and I’m sure they’ve got a solution for locking up – but I can’t quite imagine what it would be with no exposed frame members. But hey, it looks like an engineer’s dream – and I’m an engineer.
More than just a solar science experiment
Fortunately, Lightfoot seems to have put some thought into the rest of the scooter, too.
Power comes from a pair of 750W nominal geared hub motors – one in each wheel – rated at 1,000W peak each. Lightfoot claims a whopping 160 Nm of combined torque, meaning most hills shouldn’t be a problem.
The important takeaway though is that this isn’t supposed to be a high-speed machine. All that motor is there to haul people and cargo up those hills while keeping the speed below 20 mph (32 km/h). Again, they’re pitching this as a bike lane solution, not an electric motorcycle.
There’s also full suspension, with a 70mm-travel inverted front fork and a 45mm-travel rear coil-over shock. Tektro hydraulic disc brakes with 160mm rotors provide stopping power, while chunky 14 x 3.2-inch tires should help soak up rough pavement.
And despite its scooter-sized footprint, this isn’t exactly a featherweight. The lightfoot weighs 141 lb (64 kg) and has a 48-inch wheelbase.
Some of that heft buys you a feature I really like, such as that 45 liter (1.5 cubic foot) lockable, weatherproof cargo compartment inside the body. Lightfoot says that’s enough for three grocery bags.
Even better, there’s room for a passenger. The long bench seat is designed for two riders, meaning this isn’t merely a funky commuter. It can handle a grocery run and then pick someone up on the way home without forcing you to choose between your passenger and your pasta.
Though I will say that the thin PU seat cushion looks roughly as plush as an extra-absorbent maxi pad. Perhaps it’s more comfortable than it looks. I’d certainly be fascinated to find out.
Lighting includes a 2,000-lumen headlight, accelerometer-activated taillight, and a rather serious 120 dB horn. There’s also a lockable center stand, Bluetooth-enabled display, and regenerative braking.
What about those bike lanes?
This is where things become slightly more complicated.
Otherlab pitches Lightfoot as a vehicle for both city streets and bike lanes and says it doesn’t require a license or registration.
But micromobility regulations vary significantly by state and municipality, so riders should check their local laws rather than assuming a sub-20 mph (32 km/h) top speed automatically makes Lightfoot legal everywhere a bicycle can go.
Conceptually, though, that’s clearly the territory Lightfoot is aiming for. This isn’t a 50 mph (80 km/h) Sur-Ron competitor masquerading as an e-bike. It’s a sub-20 mph seated scooter intended for the same sort of short urban trips already being made on electric kick scooters and other low-speed micromobility vehicles.
So as long as there aren’t some disqualifiers like the lack of pedals, it should be fairly easy to fit into the expanding definitions of micromobility vehicles in most places.
Electrek’s Take
I love this idea.
Not necessarily because I think everyone needs solar panels hanging off the sides of their scooter, but because I think we desperately need more experimentation in the space between an e-bike and a car.
There are millions of trips where a 4,500 lb (2,000 kg) automobile is ridiculous overkill, yet people still want weather-protected storage, the ability to carry a passenger, enough torque for hills, and something they can simply hop on and ride.
Lightfoot checks a surprising number of those boxes.
It’s admittedly expensive.
At $4,495
, you’re paying significantly more than many 20 mph (32 km/h) seated electric scooters, including machines like the Infinite Machine Olto. And unlike the Olto, which
can be unlocked
to around 36 mph (55 km/h), Lightfoot isn’t secretly offering you a faster vehicle underneath its low-speed settings. At least, not that I know of.
But speed isn’t really the point here.
You’re paying for the unusual design, the big enclosed cargo compartment, two-person capability, full suspension, dual motors, and – obviously – those giant solar panels.
If all you need is something with two wheels that travels 20 mph, I don’t think Lightfoot makes much financial sense. There are much cheaper ways to accomplish that.
But if your daily mileage is low enough that you could genuinely run largely on sunshine, you’ve got somewhere outdoors to park it, and you want a highly practical little vehicle that looks like absolutely nothing else on the road, then I can see the appeal.
The bigger question is whether enough people are willing to pay a premium for that appeal. Otherlab has built an interesting answer to the question of what a short-trip, self-sustaining vehicle could look like. Now we’ll get to find out whether there are enough buyers asking the same question.

title: Cheaper EVs Are Helping Fuel Europe’s Electric Car Boom
content:
Cheaper EVs Are Helping Fuel Europe’s Electric Car Boom
More affordable EVs are attracting buyers as electric car sales surge in the EU, but price isn’t the only driver of the shift.
- EU electric car sales rose 45% through August, with more affordable models helping drive growth.
- Five of Europe’s top 20 plug-in models offer electric versions below €30,000 in at least one market.
- Higher fuel prices are also pushing Europeans to switch to electric, although pricier EVs remain major sellers.
It turns out that giving people more electric cars they can afford is a very effective way of selling more of them. Europe’s EV sales have hit a new record this year, according to a new study, with smaller, cheaper models helping driving that growth.
According a new report from Transport & Environment, an advocacy group, electric car sales in the European Union reached 1.64 million units from January through August, up 45% year over year. They accounted for roughly 22% of new cars sold, while the choice of electric models expanded by 50% compared to a year ago.
Transport & Environment notes that this is happening alongside an influx of new affordable EVs that have hit the market due to tightening CO2 targets in Europe. Five of Europe’s top 20 best-selling EVs start below €30,000 ($33,600), based on their German price before incentives.
The organization forecasts that sales of electric models with starting prices below €25,000 will be seven times their 2024 level this year. It expects 16 models below that threshold to be available by the end of 2026. That’s twice as many as last year.
Renault seems to have figured it out: After launching the 5 E-Tech, the EU’s third-best-selling EV in 2025 and best-selling electric subcompact, it has now launched the even cheaper Twingo, which is already proving to be a hit. The French automaker saw EV sales rise 63.2% in the first half of 2026, following a 72.2% jump in 2025.
New arrivals are also starting to show up in the charts. In August, the Kia EV2 recorded 4,429 registrations, the Cupra Raval added 3,608, and the grown-up new Volkswagen ID. Polo contributed 1,876 in its debut month.
Improving affordability isn’t the only way to get more people to choose EVs. Higher fuel prices have also created an undeniable economic incentive, making buyers more willing to switch. Still, this EU EV boom includes larger, pricier vehicles. According to JATO’s August figures, the Tesla Model Y, Skoda Elroq, BMW iX1, BMW iX3, and Volkswagen ID.4 each notched over 6,000 registrations.
European manufacturers are supplying much of that expanding choice. T&E notes that they account for nearly 60% of available electric models, with 16 new additions in the first half of 2026. Chinese automakers hold 21% of the market and added 11 over the same period.
So while a handful of cheap hatchbacks haven’t single-handedly electrified Europe, they are helping. With an even broader selection of affordable models coming by the end of the year, we may start to see even more cheap EVs among Europe’s best sellers in 2027.

title: Gas Cars’ Dominance Is Fading: Global Sales Fall Below 50% For The First Time Since The 1920s
content:
Gas Cars’ Dominance Is Fading: Global Sales Fall Below 50% For The First Time Since The 1920s
EVs had the most to gain from the gas cars’ continued decline, with some experts estimating that electric cars will dominate by 2030.
- Traditional gas vehicles now make up less than half of new-car sales globally.
- Pure gas models went from having 73% of the world’s car market in 2021 to less than 50% now.
- Rising fuel prices and high maintenance costs are driving buyers toward EVs and hybrids.
After a century of dominance, gas-only vehicles now account for less than half of global new-vehicle sales. High oil prices triggered by the conflict in the Middle East have prompted more and more car buyers to ditch traditional combustion cars for EVs or hybrids.
Gas-only vehicles accounted for 49% of all new-vehicle sales around the world in the first half of the year, excluding hybrids and other electrified models, according to data from Mobility Global quoted by Nikkei Asia.
Affordable models like the Renault 5 E-Tech have boosted European EV sales.
It’s the first time that gas cars have had less than 50% of the global market share since the technology went mainstream in the 1920s, spurred by the widespread adoption of Tetraethyllead, the additive that created leaded gasoline. Despite the health hazards associated with the additive, it boosted combustion engines’ compression, which in turn led to more performance and increased fuel efficiency.
Pure gas vehicles held 73% of the global new-car market in 2021, but sales have tumbled since then. In the first half of the year, automakers sold 20.25 million units worldwide, 10% fewer than during the same period last year.
Most people who ditched gas cars went for EVs or hybrids. Despite what’s going on in the United States, electric cars are experiencing huge growth in popularity elsewhere. China buys half of all EVs globally, though the market has slipped 3% to 3.44 million units after incentives were scrapped in January. Closer to home, EV sales in North America went down 15%.
Meanwhile, Europe and Southeast Asia are leading the way in the electrification game. Europeans bought 1.81 million EVs through the first six months of the year, 32% more than last year, while Southeast Asian sales jumped 81% and reached 350,000. In Oceania, EV sales more than doubled to 110,000.
"EV adoption slowed [around 2024], and hybrids grew due to subsidy cuts and other factors, but higher oil prices have renewed appreciation for EVs' lower operating costs, and sales are now growing again," said Yoshiaki Kawano, Mobility Global associate director.
Overall, global EV sales reached 6.87 million, an increase of 12% over the same period last year, while hybrids rose 10%, reaching 7.27 million units.
According to Mobility Global, EVs accounted for 17% of all new-vehicle sales, which is still a long way from gas cars’ 49%, but analysts estimate that things won’t stay the same for long. By 2030, EVs are poised to exceed 30% of total vehicle production, overtaking hybrids and pure combustion-powered vehicles, including diesel.
“Few EV buyers return to gasoline vehicles or hybrids, and as prices continue to fall, demand driven by genuine consumer needs rather than subsidies is likely to expand," Kawano said.

title: Lucid Production Plunges As The EV Maker Tries To Clear Inventory
content:
Lucid Production Plunges As The EV Maker Tries To Clear Inventory
The American startup delivered fewer than 4,000 EVs in the third quarter, while production remains capped at a single shift.
- Lucid Motors’ third-quarter production and deliveries fell short of analysts’ expectations.
- The startup’s production fell 38% quarter-over-quarter as it tried to move inventory vehicles.
- Deliveries also fell compared with the same period last year.
Lucid Motors, the California EV startup that builds the Air sedan and Gravity SUV, delivered 3,806 cars and built 2,954 vehicles during the third quarter. That’s a 6.7% decrease in deliveries compared to the same period last year, and a 24% drop in production.
On the manufacturing side, it’s the lowest number since early 2025 and a 38% drop compared to the second quarter. That’s mainly because the company slashed one of the two assembly shifts at its AMP-1 factory in Arizona in June, and then tried to sell as many inventory vehicles as possible.
The Lucid Gravity GT-S joined the lineup earlier this year as America's most powerful three-row SUV, with over 1,000 hp.
Lucid deliveries and production during 2026
| Period | Production | Deliveries |
| Q1 2026 | 5,500 | 3,093 |
| Q2 2026 | 4,774 | 3,953 |
| Q3 2026 | 2,954 | 3,806 |
The third-quarter figures are not looking great, but it’s not all bad news. From the beginning of the year through September 30, Lucid built nearly 33% more cars and delivered 3% more EVs than last year, with 13,228 vehicles assembled and 10,852 total deliveries.
The company doesn’t break out sales for individual models, but the Gravity SUV is likely the winner here, as demand for electric sedans can’t quite keep up with buyers’ inclination to go for an SUV. Lucid said that “demand for the Lucid Gravity continued to regain momentum,” after the electric seven-seater was hit by a costly recall that halted shipments for nearly a month.
Earlier this year, the California company cut production and laid off 18% of its staff as part of an “operational reset” that targets $1.4 billion in cash flow improvements this year.
Lucid Motors brought in Silvio Napoli to steer the company in the right direction back in April. Napoli, an auto industry outsider, replaced interim CEO Marc Winterhoff and got the extremely tough task of turning a profit.
There are good signs ahead, along with a healthy influx of cash from Uber and the Saudi Public Investment Fund, but the results of these deals won’t be seen for months. The Cosmos mid-size crossover, which is bound to open the company up to a completely different client base, has been delayed to next year. Slated to cost around $50,000, the Cosmos EV will try to make inroads in the highly competitive segment where the Tesla Model Y reigns supreme.

title: Renault’s E-Space Concept Brings Back The Minivan With A 1980s-Inspired Twist
content:
Renault’s E-Space Concept Brings Back The Minivan With A 1980s-Inspired Twist
It’s an all-electric reinterpretation of the original Espace minivan, which was the vehicle of choice for countless European families.
- Renault wants to make minivans cool again.
- The E-Space Concept is a modern electric people carrier that harks back to the original Espace.
- The bold MPV will sit front and center at Renault’s Paris Motor Show booth later this month.
Minivans are somewhat of a dying breed, as SUVs have convinced families with kids that they’re the better choice. Well, France’s Renault begs to differ and wants to make minivans cooler than they’ve ever been.
Enter the E-Space Concept, a bold electric reinterpretation of the original 1984 Renault Espace that ferried countless families to soccer practice, ballet, and skiing lessons across Europe.
Renault E-Space Concept
Featuring a digitized front fascia with a wide U-shaped light strip that resembles the Espace’s squared-off face, the E-Space is billed as “a future-focused vision of the original” that will serve as a “reboot.”
There are no interior images or tech specs, with Renault saying that more will be revealed when the car goes under the spotlights at the Paris Motor Show on October 12. The marque insisted that the retro minivan is purely a concept, but said that it’s exploring “possible futures,” and that a production version of the electric people carrier would fit just right under its Futuready strategy.
The E-Space Concept is 185 inches (4,700 millimeters) long and features a nearly 360-degree glasshouse that includes a raked A-pillar quarter window, just like the original. At the rear, the D pillar wraps around the roof and seems like it’s floating a few inches from the main body.
1984 Renault Espace
Digital cameras take the place of conventional side-view mirrors, huge wheels shod in slim tires fill the wheelarches just like on a sports car, and there are no visible door handles.
The 1984 Espace was an exercise in good packaging. It offered up to seven seats and plenty of space for passengers in a surprisingly compact footprint. Developed in cooperation with Matra, the Espace had removable rear seats, while the front seats could swivel, enabling owners to transform their boxy car into a van or a cozy place to have lunch while camping.
Renault didn’t say how the E-Space’s interior can be configured, but it’s sure to come with a few cool party tricks. Building a minivan on top of a completely flat electric platform sounds like a match made in heaven—we’ll just have to wait and see if Renault is bold enough to put its concept into production.
What is clear, though, is that the French automaker has been on a roll lately, launching fabulous concepts like the 8 Gordini throwback and R17 restomod.

title: This Chinese SUV Was The UK's Best Selling Car Last Month
content:
The Jaecoo 7 SUV, available as a plug-in hybrid, was the best-selling new car in the UK in September.
Photo by:
2:16pm ET
The UK's best-selling car last month wasn't a small, European-made diesel hatchback or even a luxurious British SUV. Well, it kind of looks like the latter. The Jaecoo 7, a Chinese SUV widely known as the "Temu Range Rover," found over 10,800 buyers in September, according to the UK's Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders.
It's the model's second monthly sales crown this year. Last month, the 7 edged out the Tesla Model 3, Ford Puma, and Kia Sportage for the top spot.
Chinese vehicles are finding support in the UK, claiming 23% of September's market share, according to
Bloomberg
. Jaecoo took 4.3% of the market, Chery (which is Jaecoo's parent company but also sells cars under its own brand) claimed 2.8%, and
sold 5.75% of light-duty cars, according to the SMMT data.
Photo by: Chery
Chinese automakers are also seeing success as sales of electric vehicles more broadly boom in the UK. In September, battery-electric vehicles made up 28.3% of the UK car market, up five percentage points from September of last year. Plug-in hybrids came in at 17% of the market, an increase of 4.8 percentage points, SMMT says.
It isn't hard to see why the UK would be so fond of the the 7. It looks strikingly similar to a Range Rover Velar—hence the slightly rude nickname.
The Jaecoo 7 was the UK's best-selling car in September, edging out the Ford Puma and Tesla Model 3.
Photo by: Jaecoo
With a starting price of around £30,000, the Jaecoo 7 undercuts the Velar by about £26,000. With similar looks and a luxurious interior, the Chinese-made SUV is a no-brainer for many customers. It gives them the posh look and opulence they want, at normie prices. It also helps that the UK lacks the Chinese car tariffs the European Union has, so Chinese brands can offer attractive prices few other countries can match.
Additionally, the Jaecoo 7 comes as a plug-in hybrid, proving how popular such models have become in the UK. Plug-in hybrid sales increased by 55.7% in September, according to
, with a total of 59,563 new registrations. Affordable hybrids like the Jaecoo 7 are a big part of that.
Things aren't all sunshine and rainbows for the Chinese Range Rover lookalike, though. According to
What Car
, the Jaecoo 7 was among the 10 least reliable cars in the UK this year. Most of its issues seem to stem from non-powertrain electronics, and 65% of customers with issues saw repair times take longer than a week. So sometimes the cheaper route isn't always best.

title: R 星表态：《GTA6》不会过度聚焦特定人物、事件，系列游戏从未重点讽刺美国政治
content:
IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，Rockstar 叙事部门高级副总裁鲁珀特 · 汉弗莱斯（Rupert Humphries）近日接受采访时表示，《GTA6》游戏不会过度聚焦于某个特定的人物、事件或政治运动。
IT之家了解到，《侠盗猎车手》系列游戏经常会以辛辣的手段，讽刺某些现实事件。同时 Rockstar 从来不会避讳一些敏感议题，例如在《GTA5》就深入展示过酷刑、秘密拘留等事件。
不过 R 星一般不会指名道姓地讽刺某件现实事件。假如团队在开发阶段计划让《GTA6》出现名为“瓜斯克”的 NPC，他会发射火箭进入太空，而且行为有些古怪。那么等到游戏发售时，“瓜斯克”很可能无法准确对应原型角色近年来的举动。
鲁珀特 · 汉弗莱斯对此表示：“如果你们回顾此前的《GTA》作品，就能够发现我们从未将讽刺重点放在美国政治上。《GTA4》确实将国家安全和《爱国者法案》的兴起作为重要内容，但 9·11 事件后，纽约确实有着这些事件背景。”
“我们希望将发售的游戏联结时代背景，但与此同时，它又不能完全反映现实世界。因此我们不希望过度针对特定人物、事件、政治运动等。”
相较之下，Rockstar 更希望捕捉佛罗里达州的特质。开发团队曾调研过佛州的各种奇人怪事。
汉弗莱斯继续说道：“除此之外，我们还有很多方式来讲述这些故事，而不需要让玩家直接与角色面对面。你可能会看到一张选举宣传海报，接到竞选团队的自动电话，或者在收音机里听到广告。我们还加入了一些很棒的政治脱口秀节目，它们会在广播中讨论各种各样的问题。”

title: 《战争机器：事变日》游戏开发团队找到提升微软 Xbox Series S 主机性能的新方法：虚拟内存
content:
IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据游戏媒体 EuroGamer 今天报道，《战争机器：事变日》是微软 Xbox 第一方游戏，登陆 PC 和 Xbox Series X|S 平台。由于 XSS 相比 XSX 计算性能有限，开发团队必须做好优化才能确保两种主机能够流畅运行游戏。
如今，《战争机器：事变日》开发团队已经找到一种类似虚拟内存的机制，让仅有 10GB GDDR6 内存的 Xbox Series S 主机也能顺畅地运行游戏。团队选择与 Xbox 先进技术团队合作，将一些原本放在内存的数据，转移到超高速 NVMe 固态硬盘中。
IT之家注意到，NVMe SSD 本身是存储单元，可以在必要时充当额外内存使用。虽然它的速度无法和内存相提并论，但开发团队将其作为二级内存使用时，游戏引擎将能够更流畅地分配资源。本作会将当前需要使用的数据交换到内存中，而当这些数据暂时不再使用时，则会将其重新放回 NVMe SSD。
由于这套系统足够智能，因此可以将那些不受明显影响的数据暂存到硬盘中。只需要占用 SSD 上几 GB 的存储空间，就能获得大约 1GB 的可用系统内存。
随着 3A 游戏性能需求不断膨胀、当前世代游戏主机逐渐步入中后期，开发商需要更多的巧妙解法来维持游戏性能表现。这项技术可能会成为 Xbox 平台的重要技术发展，不过我们尚不清楚未来是否会有更多 Xbox 游戏采用。

title: 宣称“欧美最强开源模型”：Mistral AI 发布 Mistral Large 4 公开预览版，月底开放权重
content:
IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，当地时间 10 月 6 日，法国公司 Mistral AI 正式推出 Mistral Large 4 模型的公开预览版（Public Preview），简称 ML4，代号 le Chonk。
即日起，用户可以在 Mistral Studio 上体验预览版 API，模型权重将于本月底正式开放下载。
目前，官方正联合顶尖网络安全机构、受信任的合作伙伴及政府监管部门，在真实业务环境中对模型展开红队测试（Red-Teaming）。相关合作方将获得该模型的专项测试访问权限；该测试版本适当放宽了内容安全审查策略，并强化了网络安全攻防技术能力。
ML4 是一款拥有 1 万亿总参数、490 亿激活参数的原生多模态模型，Mistral 称其实测表现不仅足以媲美全球顶尖的开源模型，更大幅领先于欧美开发的所有开放权重模型。
在网络安全、金融与法律等关键企业级工作负载中，该模型在所有开源模型中均达到了 SOTA。
在某些特定领域（例如视觉定位），它的表现更进一步，甚至超越了当前的前沿闭源模型。
据介绍，ML4 是在 Mistral 位于欧洲的自建数据中心内，基于 3,800 块英伟达 Grace Blackwell GPU 从零开始训练完成的，其欧洲部署方案完全由 Mistral 实施端到端独立运营，严格遵循欧盟法律法规，不受制于任何其他第三方数字服务提供商。
ML4 的训练数据具备显著的多语言特性，语料覆盖超 160 种自然语言，全面囊括了欧盟的所有官方语言。
价格方面，ML4 每百万 tokens 输入 1.36 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 9.1 元人民币），每百万 tokens 输出 4.18 美元（现汇率约合 28.1 元人民币）。

title: 梅赛德斯-奔驰正式为 EQS 电动轿车提供线控转向选装，套件税前 2500 欧元
content:
IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，Mercedes‑Benz（梅赛德斯-奔驰）当地时间今日宣布，其新一代 EQS 纯电动豪华轿车正式支持选装线控转向系统。
该套件包含线控转向系统、后轴转向系统、集成创新安全气囊结构的扁平方向盘，在德国市场的定价为税前 2,500 欧元 / 税后 2,975 欧元（现汇率约合 18,822 / 22,399 元人民币）。
线控转向系统在日常驾驶中带来诸多优势。这项技术提升了车辆的动态性能，同时使操控和泊车更加轻松便捷。其从左到右仅需 170° 的转动角度，带来轻松流畅的转向体验；与后轴转向系统相配合，还消除了在颠簸路面行驶时传导至驾驶员手部的震动。
与此同时，更紧凑的方向盘显著提升了车内空间，改善了驾驶员显示屏的视野，并方便了上下车。
梅赛德斯-奔驰的线控转向系统采用冗余架构，配备高精度传感器、强大的控制单元和独立的信号通路。即使在系统完全失效的极端意外情况下，ESP 系统也能通过后轴转向和针对特定车轮的制动干预来维持车辆的横向控制。

title: 消息称成本压力迫使本田调整印度策略，与塔塔技术合作缩短一半研发周期
content:
IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据路透社今日消息，两位知情人士透露，来自竞争对手的压力迫使日本车企本田重新审视其长期坚持的“单干”自研路线。本田在印度与塔塔技术展开合作，旨在将成本最多削减五分之一，并将整车研发周期缩短一半。
在预计超过 120 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 805.74 亿元人民币）的电动汽车相关亏损的打击下，本田目前正全面转向油电混合动力技术并大力压缩开支。该公司正寻求在未来四年内削减超过 90 亿美元的成本。
今年 5 月，工程服务商塔塔技术曾宣布已获选为一家日本车企提供车型研发服务，但当时未指明合作方身份。据前述两位知情人士及另一名相关人士透露，该车企正是本田。
两位知情人士表示，根据该整车外包协议，塔塔技术将专门针对印度市场开发乘用车。通过此项合作，本田预计可最高降低 20% 的成本，并将目前长达约五年的整车研发周期缩短一半。
其中两位知情人士透露，本田之所以决定引入塔塔技术，根源在于其日本本土与印度本地的管理层陷入分歧 —— 双方在印度后续新车型的零部件供应商选用策略上始终无法达成一致。
本田在官方声明中表示，公司此前在印度未能构建起足够充实、能让消费者感到“物有所值”的产品矩阵。为此，本田正着手“重新调整”其在印度的产品线规划，并计划推出兼顾品质与价格竞争力的新车型。
同时，本田否认了日印两地团队在供应商甄选问题上存在争执。
在另一份单独声明中，本田印度分公司表示，产品开发涉及不同团队之间的密切合作，并补充称将协作讨论定性为分歧是不准确的。
塔塔技术方面则未对置评请求作出回应。

title: 特斯拉在印度市场交付超一年，仅注册不到 1000 辆汽车
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 6 日消息，据 electrek 报道，根据印度电动汽车刊物 ElecTree 汇总的注册数据，特斯拉自 2025 年 9 月在印度开始交付以来，
仅注册了 993 辆汽车
上述数据覆盖了 2025 年 9 月至 2026 年 9 月共 13 个自然月；若严格按前 12 个自然月计算，特斯拉交付第一年的新车总注册量仅为 699 辆。鉴于特斯拉官方并不按国家单独披露销售明细，注册量已是最接近真实销量的数据参考。
2025 年 7 月，特斯拉正式进军印度市场，旗下 Model Y 起售价约 70,000 美元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 47 万元人民币）
，几乎是当时美国本土售价的两倍。
2025 年 9 月是特斯拉在印度的首个交付月，当月新车注册量仅为 69 辆，且在此后的八个月中，其单月表现均未能超越这一水平。
根据 ElecTree 的统计，截至 2025 年底，特斯拉在印度的累计注册量仅为 226 辆；而在 2026 年 1 月至 5 月期间，该数字仅增加了 202 辆，其中 2 月更是跌入谷底，仅登记了 29 辆。
早在今年 1 月，特斯拉便已开始对其首批进口至印度但仍未售出的 Model Y 进行降价促销。到了 5 月，
印度重工业部部长证实特斯拉将不会在印度本土建厂
。这意味着，特斯拉在印度销售的所有车辆都将继续完全依赖整车进口，并需承担相伴而来的高额进口关税。
不过，2026 年 9 月一个月，特斯拉新车注册量达到了 294 辆，创下了特斯拉在印度的单月交付新高。也直接印证了其近期一系列举措的成效 —— 特斯拉全面下调了印度售价，并正式推出了六座版 Model YL。
4 月 22 日，特斯拉在印度正式推出六座版车型 Model YL，起售价为 619.9 万印度卢比
（现汇率约合 43.3 万元人民币）
，并于 6 月启动交付。
这款车身更长、空间更大的六座版车型，其定价反而低于此前在售的五座版 Model Y 长续航版，该车型售价 678.9 万印度卢比
（现汇率约合 47.4 万元人民币）
；目前该版本已被移出在印度销售的产品线。
5 月下旬，特斯拉再次对基础款 Model Y 进行价格调整，直接降价 90 万印度卢比
（现汇率约合 62,888 元人民币）
，售价由 598.9 万印度卢比
（现汇率约合 41.8 万元人民币）
降至 508.9 万印度卢比
（现汇率约合 35.6 万元人民币），
调幅达 15%。

title: 降本增效：宝马将提高通用零部件使用比例，减少定制零部件
content:
10 月 6 日消息，据 bmwblog 今日报道，为削减成本、提升效率，宝马计划在其整车制造中大幅提高标准化零部件的使用比例。
为提升自身竞争力，宝马正寻求借鉴中国汽车产业的发展策略。这家德国汽车制造商计划大幅提升标准化现货零部件的采用率，不再为每款车型单独开发专用零部件。其目标非常明确：在坚守宝马核心品牌基因的前提下，降低成本、加快研发周期并提高利润率。
该公司预计，到 2032 年，标准化零部件将在其约 800 亿欧元
（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6,023.16 亿元人民币）
的年度采购预算中占据最大份额。与此同时，宝马计划将专用零部件的使用比例削减一半。
各大汽车制造商早已在广泛共享零部件，涵盖传感器、电子控制模块以及变速箱等机械部件。其核心差异在于，
宝马计划更深度地依赖由供应商依据行业通用标准研发、并向多家车企同时供货的标准组件
宝马新任首席执行官米兰 · 内德利科维奇（Milan Nedeljković）表示：“市场上已经存在非常成熟且值得信赖的行业标准，弃之不用将是极其错误的决策。”
这绝不意味着旗下车型会突然退化成“乐高积木式的模块拼凑”
。该公司声明，扩大标准化零部件的采用率不会牺牲产品质量、机械性能或宝马固有的品牌辨识度。
零部件通用化仅仅是宝马更大规模降本增效举措中的一环。宝马近期公布了多项规划，包括精简车型衍生版本、停产 2 系多功能旅行车且不设后续迭代车型，并在 2027 年年中前将相关业务部门及管理岗编制精简 20%。
针对中国市场，宝马也推出了专门的提效方案。宝马计划到 2030 年，其在中国市场销售的车辆中，至少有 95% 实现本土化生产与专属适配研发。此外，该公司还在评估将中国工厂生产的车型出口至其他东南亚市场的可行性。

title: Der Faktor Zeit: Warum Pforzheimer Studierende am Auto hängen
content:
Der Faktor Zeit: Warum Pforzheimer Studierende am Auto hängen
Warum steigen Studierende in Pforzheim nicht auf den Bus um, obwohl die Hochschule direkt angebunden ist? Die Studie „Urban Student Mobility in Pforzheim“ von Studierenden der Hochschule Pforzheim liefert eine plausible Erklärung: der massive Zeitverlust. Auf Basis von über 1.000 anonymisierten Wohnadressen und automatisierten Reisezeit-Abfragen zeigt die Untersuchung, dass Busfahrten im Schnitt mehr als dreimal so lange dauern wie die vergleichbare Autofahrt – ein zentraler Befund für die Verkehrswende der Goldstadt.
Im Rahmen des Moduls „Ethik & Nachhaltigkeit“ werteten Maximilian Motz, Daniel Landes und Yusrea Valiyakath die Wohnadressen von 1067 Studierenden aus und berechneten für jede Adresse die Reisezeit zur Hochschule – einmal mit dem Auto und einmal mit dem Bus. Das Ergebnis zeigte eindrucksvoll: Während eine Autofahrt im Durchschnitt 8,7 Minuten dauert, benötigt der Bus 27,7 Minuten für eine vergleichbare Strecke. In Einzelfällen lag der Unterschied bei bis zu 48 Minuten. Eine Zählung von 487 Autokennzeichen auf den Hochschulparkplätzen bestätigte das Bild: Rund 40 Prozent der geparkten Fahrzeuge hatten ein Pforzheimer Kennzeichen, stammten also mutmaßlich von Studierenden, die in Pforzheim und der Region wohnten – und damit theoretisch direkten Busanschluss zur Hochschule hätten.
Mithilfe einer geografischen „Heatmap“ identifizierten die Studierenden strukturelle Ursachen für die langen Fahrzeiten. Die Flüsse Enz, Nagold und Würm teilen Pforzheim in vier Zonen, zwischen denen der Busverkehr meist über zentrale Knotenpunkte wie den Leopoldplatz umgeleitet wird. Besonders betroffen sind Stadtteile wie Südweststadt, Büchenbronn, Dillweißenstein sowie Huchenfeld und Würm: Hier dauern Busfahrten teils 40 bis über 60 Minuten, weil direkte Verbindungen fehlen und Umstiege in der Innenstadt nötig sind.
Die Ergebnisse fügen sich in die Herausforderungen ein, denen sich die Stadt Pforzheim mit ihrem Integrierten Mobilitätsentwicklungsplan (IMEP) stellt. Dieser sieht unter anderem eine Reduktion der verkehrsbedingten CO₂-Emissionen um 40 Prozent bis 2035 sowie eine Steigerung des Fuß- und Radverkehrsanteils von derzeit 28 auf 45 Prozent vor.
Was Pforzheim von Utrecht und Oslo lernen kann: Dort wurden ehemalige Hauptverkehrsstraßen zu Grün- und Wasserflächen zurückgebaut, in Oslo reduzieren autofreie Zonen und ein konsequenter Radwegeausbau den Innenstadtverkehr spürbar. Auch der Ausbau von Straßenbahnnetzen – wie ihn Verkehrsforscher der TU Berlin für Städte dieser Größenordnung empfehlen – wird als mögliche Option für Pforzheim diskutiert, auch wenn hierzu nach Einschätzung der Autor*innen weiterer Forschungsbedarf besteht.
"Unsere Daten liefern keinen Aufschluss zu individuellen Verhalten der Studenten, identifizieren jedoch beim Zeitfaktor einen erheblichen Mangel, der erklären könnte, warum trotz Busanbindung auf das Auto zurückgegriffen wird“, fasst Co-Autor Maximilian Motz zusammen.
Die Studierenden erhielten für Ihre gemeinsame Arbeit den Förderpreis des kommunalen Eigenbetriebs „WSP - Wirtschaft und Stadtmarketing Pforzheim“.

Das Startup xenko der Universität Ulm erhält eine EXIST-Förderung des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Energie in Höhe von 143 500 Euro für ein Jahr. Das Team entwickelt eine digitale Gesundheitsplattform, die mittels Virtueller Realität zu mehr Bewegung im Alltag am Arbeitsplatz anregen soll. Interessant ist das für Unternehmen mit einem Betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagement.
Das Startup xenko erhält eine EXIST-Förderung des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Energie in Höhe von 143 500 Euro. Das Gründer*innen-Team der Universität Ulm entwickelt eine digitale Gesundheitsplattform, die mittels Virtueller Realität zu mehr Bewegung im Alltag am Arbeitsplatz anregen soll. Interessant ist die Entwicklung für Unternehmen mit einem Betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagement und langfristig auch für die Physiotherapie-Branche.
Ein höhenverstellbarer Schreibtisch, der Obstkorb in der Büroküche und eine vergünstigte Mitgliedschaft im Fitnessstudio: Unternehmen haben erkannt, dass die Gesundheit ihrer Mitarbeitenden ein hohes Gut ist, und fördern deshalb bereits seit Jahren unterschiedliche Maßnahmen. Oft sind diese im Betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagement (BGM) gebündelt und werden als Anreize beispielsweise bei der Mitarbeitergewinnung beworben.
Das junge Ulmer Startup xenko setzt genau hier an: Es ermöglicht Unternehmen, Gesundheitsangebote digital und flexibel bereitzustellen, die die Mitarbeitenden unabhängig von Standort und Arbeitszeit nutzen können. Im Kern steht dabei die sogenannte Extended Reality (XR), also die Erweiterung der Umgebung durch Elemente in der Virtuellen Realität, die dann durch eine VR-Brille sichtbar sind. Das Angebot reicht von Mobilitätsübungen, Pilates und Yoga bis hin zu Meditationen und Regenerationseinheiten. Ein Trainingsplan, die virtuelle Umgebung und ein Avatar lassen sich individuell auf die Bedürfnisse der Nutzenden abstimmen. „Über Echtzeit-Ganzkörperfeedback werden die eigenen Bewegungen in die virtuelle Umgebung übertragen und mit denen eines Traineravatars verknüpft. Ein detailliertes digitales Muskelmodell kann zusätzlich veranschaulichen, welche Muskelgruppen bei einer Bewegung beteiligt sind. So wollen wir Bewegung nicht nur erlebbar, sondern auch verständlicher machen“, erklärt Geschäftsführerin Dr. Jana Funke. Funke hat an der Uni Ulm bei Professor Enrico Rukzio am Institut für Medieninformatik promoviert und ihre Begeisterung für Bewegung und Sport mit der zukunftsweisenden XR-Technologie verbunden. Sie erforschte, wie Bewegungsübungen für XR gestaltet sein sollten, und untersuchte deren Auswirkungen auf die Nutzer*innen, darunter Trainingserfolg, Akzeptanz, „Motion Sickness“ und Einfluss auf emotionale Zustände. Zusammen mit den anderen Gründer*innen Nadja Pirchheim (zuständig für Marketing und Produktdesign), XR-Entwickler Benjamin Bayer und Dr. Jessica Seyfried (Content Development) entstand 2024 die Idee zu xenko.
Alle Gründerinnen wurden bereits durch ein Woman-EXIST-Stipendium über den Entrepreneurs Campus der Universität gefördert und haben nun über das Gründungsnetzwerk erfolgreich ein EXIST-Gründungsstipendium des Bundesministeriums für Wirtschaft und Energie (BMWE) über drei Vollzeit-Stellen eingeworben. Das klare Ziel ist die Unternehmensgründung. „Wir suchen gezielt nach wissenschaftlichen Ergebnissen, in denen unternehmerisches Potenzial steckt, und befähigen die Menschen dahinter, daraus echte Anwendungen zu machen und den Weg zur Gründung zu gehen. Der Entrepreneurs Campus ist der Ort, an dem wissenschaftliche Exzellenz und unternehmerischer Mut zusammenkommen – und genau dafür sind wir da", so Melanie Kamrath vom Entrepreneurs Campus der Uni Ulm. Der Entrepreneurs Campus, der auch die Gründer*innen von xenko berät, ist die zentrale Anlaufstelle für gründungsinteressierte Menschen an der Universität und bietet neben Inspiration und Qualifizierung ein starkes Netzwerk für alle, die unternehmerisch handeln und Innovationen schaffen wollen.
Das Gründungs-Team von xenko erhält im Rahmen der EXIST-Förderung insgesamt 143 500 Euro – aufgeteilt auf drei Vollzeitstipendien für Dr. Funke, Pirchheim und Bayer – sowie 30 000 Euro Sachmittel und 5 000 Euro für Coaching-Ausgaben. Die Förderung läuft vom 1. September 2026 bis 31. August 2027.

Prof. Dr. Michael Pilgermann, THB-Professor für Angewandte Informatik, insbesondere IT-Sicherheit, leitet das neue Forschungsprojekt DHS-RS.

Mit einem virtuellen Kick-off-Meeting hat am Montag die Arbeit am neuen Forschungsprojekt „Digital Health Security Research Hub“ (DHS-RH) an der Technischen Hochschule Brandenburg (THB) offiziell begonnen. Das vom Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) geförderte Vorhaben bringt führende europäische Akteure zusammen, um die Cybersicherheit im Gesundheitssektor durch intensiven Wissensaustausch zu stärken. So sollen kritische Infrastrukturen wie Krankenhäuser mit Hilfe von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) effektiv vor Cyberangriffen geschützt werden.
Unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Michael Pilgermann kooperiert die THB in dem Projekt eng mit den Technischen Hochschulen Ingolstadt und Nürnberg sowie internationalen Partnern, unter anderem aus Griechenland, Norwegen, Großbritannien und Spanien.
Krankenhäuser und medizinische Einrichtungen zählen zu den kritischen Infrastrukturen und stehen zunehmend im Visier von Cyberkriminellen. Um dieser Bedrohung auf europäischer Ebene strategisch zu begegnen, ist am 15. September 2026 das Projekt DHS-RH an den Start gegangen. Das auf ein Jahr angelegte Projekt wird durch das BMFTR im Rahmen der Programmlinie „HAW-EuropaNetzwerke“ gefördert. Beim nun erfolgten Kick-off-Meeting haben die beteiligten Akteure die operativen Weichen gestellt.
Die Projektleitung liegt bei THB-Professor Michael Pilgermann, der an der bran-denburgischen Hochschule bereits seit 2021 die Forschungsgruppe „MedSec – IT-Sicherheit in der medizinischen Versorgung“ leitet. Zu den zentralen Partnern auf nationaler Ebene gehören die Technische Hochschule Ingolstadt, vertreten durch Prof. Patrizia Heinl, sowie die Technische Hochschule Nürnberg, vertreten durch Prof. Dr. Andrius Patapovas. Zwischen den Institutionen und der THB besteht mit dem Arbeitskreis für Digitale Sicherheit in der Gesundheitsversorgung der Gesellschaft für Informatik e.V. (GI) bereits seit mehreren Jahren eine enge und erfolgreiche Zusammenarbeit, die nun international erweitert wird.
Zentrales Ziel des DHS-RH ist es, die wissenschaftlichen Aktivitäten und die an-wendungsorientierte Forschung im Bereich der KI-gestützten Healthcare-Cybersicherheit europaweit zu verzahnen. Da die aktuelle Forschung auf diesem Gebiet bislang meist isoliert stattfindet, erfordert die zunehmende Bedrohungslage eine konsequente Bündelung von Ressourcen und Wissen. Das Hub dient hierbei als zentrale Anlaufstelle zur Vernetzung von Forschenden und Praxispartnern sowie als Plattform für den kontinuierlichen Wissens- und Methodenaustausch.
„Die Cyberbedrohungslage macht auch für Gesundheitseinrichtungen nicht an Landesgrenzen halt. Mit dem Digital Health Security Research Hub schaffen wir eine nachhaltige Plattform, die europäische Expertise bündelt und der Praxis zugänglich macht. Wir binden aktiv Expertinnen und Experten sowie Ergebnisse aus laufenden und vergangenen Forschungsprojekten ein, um das Rad nicht zwei Mal zu erfinden. Über Wissenschaft und Industrie hinaus laden wir auch die Policy-Maker auf EU-Ebene herzlich zur Mitwirkung und Zusammenarbeit ein. So ermöglichen wir einen umfassenden Blick auf die Herausforderungen und Lösungspotentiale für sichere digitale Gesundheitsinfrastrukturen“, betont Projektleiter Michael Pilgermann.
Das so aufgebaute Netzwerk soll bewusst über die Projektlaufzeit hinaus aktiv bleiben und nachhaltige Synergien schaffen. Ein erklärtes Ziel ist es, innerhalb des Netzwerks ein schlagkräftiges Konsortium aufzubauen, um sich bei der EU um weiterführende Fördermittel zu bewerben. So soll auch in Zukunft die europäische Cybersicherheit im Gesundheitswesen dauerhaft gestärkt werden.

Wird die spezielle Polymerhülle mit Licht bestrahlt, verändert sie ihre Struktur und wird wasserdurchlässig. Der Wirkstoff kann austreten und die Wunde desinfizieren. Wird das Licht abgeschaltet, verschliesst sich die Hülle wieder.

Chronische Wunden belasten Betroffene und das Gesundheitssystem gleichermassen. Forschende der Empa arbeiten deshalb an einem innovativen Material, das bei Bestrahlung mit sichtbarem Licht Wirkstoffe freisetzt. Als Bestandteil eines Pflasters könnte diese Technologie die Wundbehandlung verbessern und den Weg für eine neue Generation intelligenter Wundtherapien ebnen.
Der menschliche Körper besitzt die faszinierende Fähigkeit, sich selbst zu heilen. Dazu ersetzt er jeden Tag Millionen von alten Zellen durch neue. Einige Krankheiten können diese Heilungsmechanismen jedoch behindern: so etwa Diabetes Mellitus, eine Krankheit, die allein in der Schweiz über 500'000 Menschen betrifft. Wird eine Diabetes-Erkrankung nicht oder ungenügend behandelt, schädigt der hohe Blutzuckerspiegel Blutgefässe und Nerven, wodurch die Füsse schlecht durchblutet werden. Dies wiederum kann das diabetische Fusssyndrom auslösen: Nur schon durch eine Druckstelle im Schuh können Wunden an den Füssen entstehen. Während eine solche Wunde bei gesunden Menschen innerhalb von 1-2 Wochen verheilt, kann sie bei Betroffenen chronisch werden – also trotz Pflege länger als vier Wochen nicht verheilen.
Um die Behandlung chronischer Wunden kümmert sich in der Regel ein Behandlungsteam aus den Disziplinen Dermatologie, Chirurgie und Pflege. Die Wunde erfordert engmaschige Kontrollen und einen Verbandswechsel mindestens alle drei Tage. Und das häufig bis zu einem Jahr. Aufgrund dieses grossen personellen Aufwands stellen chronische Wunden eine ernstzunehmende ökonomische Belastung für das Gesundheitswesen dar.
Wirkstoffabgabe mit Licht steuern
Um diese Kosten zu reduzieren und das Gesundheitspersonal zu entlasten, arbeiten Forschende der Empa an neuartigen Behandlungsmethoden für chronische Wunden. Das Team um Luciano Boesel und Giorgia Giovannini aus der Abteilung «Biomimetic Membranes and Textiles» in St. Gallen hat ein Material entwickelt, das unter Lichteinstrahlung kontrolliert Wirkstoffe abgibt und dadurch die Wirksamkeit der Behandlung verbessern sowie ihre Nebenwirkungen reduzieren könnte.
Dafür haben die Forschenden Siliziumdioxid-Nanopartikel mit dem gängigen Wunddesinfektionsmittel Chlorhexidin beladen. Anschliessend haben sie diese mit einem Polymermantel beschichtet, der mit speziellen molekularen Fotoschaltern versetzt ist. Werden diese Fotoschalter mit sichtbarem LED-Licht bestrahlt, verändern sie ihre Struktur, wodurch der Polymermantel anschwillt und seine Wasserdurchlässigkeit erhöht. Dadurch kann das Chlorhexidin aus dem Siliziumdioxid-Kern austreten. Wird das LED-Licht ausgeschaltet, ziehen sich die Polymer-Moleküle zusammen und nehmen wieder ihre ursprüngliche, wasserdichte Form an. «Eingebaut in ein Pflaster, ermöglicht dieses System eine kontrollierte Wunddesinfektion», erläutert Luciano Boesel. «Der Zeitpunkt und die Dosis des freigesetzten Wirkstoffs lassen sich steuern, indem man die Dauer oder Intensität der Bestrahlung und die Wellenlänge des Lichts variiert.»
Personalisierte Wundbehandlung ermöglichen
Das System gibt den Wirkstoff kontrolliert ab. Damit hat es gegenüber anderen Pflastern den Vorteil, dass es das Medikament genau dosiert – damit vermindert es die Gefahr, dass die Bakterien in der Wunde Resistenzen entwickeln. «Am besten wäre es, wenn wir dieses neue System der lichtgesteuerten Wirkstoffabgabe mit einem Wundsensor kombinieren könnten, der laufend die Anzahl und Art der Bakterien bestimmt, die in der Wunde vorhanden sind», ergänzt Luciano Boesel.
Ein Wundsensor, wie etwa derjenige, den die Empa 2025 entwickelt hat, würde eine zusätzliche Weiterentwicklung des Pflasters ermöglichen: Denn Siliziumdioxid-Nanopartikel lassen sich nicht nur mit einem Wunddesinfektionsmittel aufladen, sondern auch mit anderen therapeutischen Wirkstoffen, und der Polymermantel lässt sich mit unterschiedlichen Fotoschaltern ausstatten. Je nachdem, welche Wellenlänge das Licht hat, mit dem man das Pflaster bestrahlt, aktiviert dieses unterschiedliche Fotoschalter. Die Wunde liesse sich somit gezielt mit genau dem Wirkstoff behandeln, der aufgrund des registrierten Bakterienbefalls zu dem Zeitpunkt nötig wäre. «Das wäre ein wichtiger Schritt in Richtung einer personalisierten Wundbehandlung», betont Boesel. Er sieht nämlich einen grossen Nachteil des heutigen Wundbehandlungs-Standards darin, dass die Wunde immer ungefähr gleich versorgt wird, egal mit welchen Bakterien sie besiedelt ist.
Vom Reagenzglas in den klinischen Alltag
Wie und wann dieses System der lichtgesteuerten Wirkstoffabgabe tatsächlich in der Praxis zum Einsatz kommen kann, ist derzeit noch nicht klar. Luciano Boesels Team hat es im Labor entwickelt und bisher ausschliesslich im Reagenzglas getestet. In einem nächsten Schritt muss es nun auf den klinischen Bedarf angepasst werden. «Wir sind in Kontakt mit verschiedenen Kliniken, die grundsätzlich interessiert wären an einem solchen System», sagt Boesel. Er ist derzeit auf der Suche nach interessierten Doktorierenden, die das System in ihrer Doktorarbeit weiterentwickeln könnten. Danach wird das System mehrere Phasen von klinischen Studien durchlaufen müssen, bevor es als Teil eines medizinischen Produkts in der Schweiz eine Zulassung erhält.
Selbst wenn also alles gut läuft, werden Menschen mit dem diabetischen Fusssyndrom noch einige Jahre warten müssen, bis sie von dem Hightech-Pflaster mit lichtgesteuerter Wirkstoffabgabe profitieren können. Sollte es jedoch erfolgreich sein, würde es ihnen zahlreiche Spitalbesuche ersparen. Nicht zuletzt würde es auch das Gesundheitssystem entlasten: Selbst wenn die Herstellung der Pflaster teurer wäre als die herkömmlicher Pflaster, würden sie diese Kosten durch den geringeren Personalbedarf mehr als ausgleichen.
Das Projekt wurde von der OPO-Stiftung (Projekt «STERILISE») und dem Schweizerischen Nationalfonds unterstützt.

Am Montag, 14. September, war eine Delegation der malaysischen Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman (UTAR) für einen Tag an der OTH Regensburg. Innerhalb von sechs Stunden unterzeichneten beide Hochschulen zwei Verträge. Am Vormittag setzten OTH-Präsident Prof. Dr. Ralph Schneider und UTAR-Präsident Ir. Professor Dato' Dr. Ewe Hong Tat ihre Unterschrift unter ein Memorandum of Understanding, das den bestehenden Kooperationsvertrag verlängert.
Seit 2012 sind die beiden Hochschulen verbunden, seit 2014 bieten sie im Master Electrical and Microsystems Engineering (MEM) einen Doppelabschluss an: Wer das Programm durchläuft, erhält am Ende ein Zeugnis aus Regensburg und eines aus Malaysia. Unterrichtet wird auf Englisch, inhaltlich verbindet der Studiengang Elektrotechnik und Mikrosystemtechnik mit einem Schwerpunkt in der Halbleitertechnologie.
„Wir verknüpfen englischsprachige Studiengänge mit gezielter Sprachförderung, interkultureller Begleitung und Kontakten zur Industrie", sagt Prof. Dr. Oliver Steffens, Vizepräsident für Forschung und Internationalisierung der OTH Regensburg. „Wer bei uns den Master macht, soll danach in einem deutschen oder internationalen Halbleiterunternehmen arbeiten können.“
Genau dieses Feld wollen beide Hochschulen weiter ausbauen. Mit dem Letter of Intent, den beide Seiten am Nachmittag unterzeichneten, kommt zum bestehenden Doppelabschluss ein zweites Kooperationsprojekt hinzu: das DAAD-Projekt G-Step.
„Malaysia gehört zu den zentralen Standorten der globalen Halbleiterindustrie. Das macht die UTAR für uns interessant: Wer dort seinen Bachelor macht, kennt dieses industrielle Umfeld bereits", sagt OTH-Präsident Prof. Dr. Ralph Schneider. „Gleichzeitig suchen die Unternehmen in Ostbayern genau solche Fachkräfte. G-Step bringt beides zusammen – für die Absolventinnen und Absolventen eröffnet das eine Perspektive in Forschung und Industrie, für die Region qualifizierten Nachwuchs.“
G-Step: vom Bachelorabschluss bis zur Promotion
Die Förderzusage des DAAD kam im Juni 2026. „G-Step“ (Global Semiconductor Excellence – International Graduate Talent Programme) läuft bis 2029 und wird aus dem Programm „Academic Horizons – Attracting Global Minds“ finanziert. Das Projekt richtet sich an internationale Bachelorabsolventinnen und -absolventen, die in der Mikrosystem- und Halbleitertechnologie einen Master und anschließend eine Promotion anstreben. Die beteiligten Partnerhochschulen liegen in Malaysia und Singapur. Dahinter steht auch ein regionales Interesse: Die ostbayerische Halbleiterbranche sucht qualifizierten Nachwuchs, das Projekt fügt sich in die Ziele der Hightech Agenda Bayern ein.
Vereinbart ist eine Summer School, die künftig jedes Jahr an der OTH Regensburg stattfinden soll. Studierende aus Malaysia und Singapur arbeiten sich dort in die Halbleitertechnologie ein und bekommen einen Eindruck davon, wie Studium und Alltag in Deutschland aussehen. Über Unternehmensbesuche sollen erste Kontakte in die deutsche Wirtschaft entstehen.
„Wir pflegen seit vielen Jahren eine erfolgreiche Partnerschaft mit der OTH Regensburg. Nun möchten wir die Verbindung zwischen Hochschule, Forschung und Industrie noch weiter stärken“, sagt UTAR-Präsident Ir. Prof. Dato' Dr. Ewe Hong Tat. „Unser Ziel ist es, den Studierenden nicht nur eine hochwertige Ausbildung zu bieten, sondern ihnen auch internationale Forschungserfahrung und frühzeitige Karrierechancen in der Halbleiterindustrie zu eröffnen.“

Die Studierenden haben sich unter anderem mit dem alten Klinikareal in Darmstadt-Eberstadt beschäftigt, mit dem Pallaswiesen- und Mornewegviertel oder auch mit Brennpunktorten wie dem Frankfurter Bahnhofsviertel. Hierbei sind sie oft in Kontakt mit Institutionen und Partnern vor Ort getreten. Einige Entwürfe wurden im Rahmen des World Design Capital Frankfurt Rhein-Main 2026 umgesetzt. Roboter-Teams für die Baustelle - Doppel-Erfolg für die Universität Stuttgart bei der EIC Pathfinder Challenge
