South 8 Technologies Signs 3-Year Supply Agreement with Galvion to Power Arctic SoloPack
SAN DIEGO–(BUSINESS WIRE)–
South 8 Technologies
, a U.S. manufacturer of lithium-ion battery cells for extreme environments, has signed a multi-year master supply agreement with Galvion, a defense technology company specializing in integrated head systems and soldier power and data solutions. South 8’s AE35 cell will power SoloPack™ Arctic, Galvion’s new extreme cold weather soldier power solution that will make its debut at AUSA 2026 in Washington, D.C., October 12–14
The agreement converts a
Letter of Intent
signed by the companies in July 2025 into a commercial supply framework and marks another step in South 8’s transition from technology development to scaled production and customer delivery.
The agreement comes as South 8 moves its ARCTIC™ AE35 18650 cell into commercial production at its San Diego headquarters. The company’s new manufacturing line has begun production, scaling toward 5 MWh of annual production capacity in 2027, equivalent to approximately 450,000 AE35 cells per year.
The AE35 is South 8’s first high volume 18650 cell. Powered by the company’s proprietary LiGas® electrolyte technology, the AE35 will charge and discharge from −60 °C to +60 °C (−76 °F to +140 °F) and uses the familiar 18650 form factor. Cells will be produced at South 8’s San Diego facility, providing customers with a domestically manufactured battery cell and a defined pathway toward meeting applicable National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) sourcing requirements once those rules are finalized.
Jungwoo Lee,
CEO of South 8 Technologies, said:
Partnering with Galvion to bring LiGas technology into the field is an important commercialization milestone,
“This multi-year supply agreement demonstrates that our technology is moving beyond development and into mission-critical applications where reliable power in extreme cold can make a real difference. Galvion’s proven SoloPack platform is an ideal application for AE35, and we’re proud to help deliver the performance and resilience warfighters need in the world’s most demanding environments.”
SoloPack Arctic extends Galvion’s soldier power portfolio into extreme cold environments at a time of increasing focus on Arctic readiness. As the system advances toward broader deployment, evaluation of SoloPack Arctic will be happening in field exercises in Alaska, where reliable power in extreme cold is a critical operational requirement.
Jonathan Blanshay,
Founder and Executive Chairman of Galvion, said:
When we began working with South 8, we saw an opportunity to combine their innovative cell technology with our proven SoloPack battery to address a very real challenge for operations in extreme cold,
“SoloPack Arctic is the result of that collaboration, and this agreement marks an important next step as we move from development into field evaluation and commercialization.” For South 8, SoloPack Arctic represents the next stage of commercialization: bringing the AE35 into production, seeing the cell integrated into a customer product, and converting an earlier LOI into a commercial supply agreement supporting market launch.

The Wait Is Over: AuroraCell RESS Now in Stock in Poland
After a long wait, we are delighted to announce that AuroraCell Residential Energy Storage Systems are now in stock at our warehouse in Poland. Our sodium-ion RESS is here, bringing long-life energy storage closer to European homes and installation partners.
Thank you to everyone who has followed the development, asked questions and waited for this arrival. Having stock in Poland is an important step: homeowners, installers and distributors can now talk to us about a system from the available batch and plan their next project with our team.
Why NCO is ideal for residential energy storage
A home battery works quietly in the background, storing energy and releasing it when the household needs it. That makes
durability, daily cycling and safety
central to the choice. Sodium Chromoxide (NCO), the sodium-ion chemistry behind AuroraCell RESS, is a strong fit for exactly these priorities.
Built for years of everyday energy storage
Residential storage should be considered over decades. With an expected service life of
25–30 years
, AuroraCell’s NCO platform is intended to serve as a lasting part of the home’s energy system. Longer useful life can reduce the need for battery replacement and spread the initial investment over more years of use.
Cycle it daily. Make more of your solar energy.
Store surplus solar electricity during the day and use it later, when household demand rises. A projected cycle life of
more than 30,000 cycles
makes NCO especially compelling for frequent charge-and-discharge operation. The goal is a battery you can use every day as part of a correctly sized and configured home energy system.
Our NCO cycle-life update explains the ongoing cell tests and the projections behind this long-life approach.
Safety at the heart of the system
For equipment installed at home, safety deserves as much attention as capacity. AuroraCell RESS combines
NCO sodium-ion chemistry, an integrated battery management system and passive thermal design
. Together, these form our ultra-safe design approach: chemistry, monitoring and protection developed for residential storage. Correct installation and operation within the specified limits remain essential.
European stock. A practical next step.
With RESS now at our Polish warehouse, we can discuss availability, delivery arrangements and the right configuration for your project. Whether you are a homeowner planning solar storage or an installer preparing a customer installation, our team can help check the battery, inverter and operating settings together.
Long life, frequent cycling and an emphasis on safety make Sodium Chromoxide a compelling choice for residential energy storage. We are excited to see the next installations take shape.

title: Volt Harbor to Showcase Software-Defined Energy Platform at The Battery Show North America 2026 - Batteries News
content:
Volt Harbor to Showcase Software-Defined Energy Platform at The Battery Show North America 2026
The company will demonstrate MAC-BESS™, its battery-agnostic technology that cuts battery project costs by half and optimizes how power flows through data centers and the grid
ANN ARBOR, Mich., October 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ —
Volt Harbor
, the Ann Arbor–based software-defined energy startup that
publicly launched in May
, will exhibit at
The Battery Show North America 2026
hosted at Huntington Place in Detroit, October 12–15. Volt Harbor will be at Booth #6212, demonstrating how its MAC-BESS™ platform is a solution for the entire front-end power stack, from the grid to the data center, in a single battery-agnostic system.
Grid resilience depends less on how much storage gets built than on how intelligently power moves through it, and the layer with the most untapped potential is the power electronics. Unlike traditional energy infrastructure, which requires expensive hardware overhauls to adapt to new needs, Volt Harbor’s platform uses software changes to adapt Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) dynamically. This supports any input or output, including new battery chemistries and “second-life” EV batteries, inside a single unified system. The result is roughly 40-50% lower capital and operating costs, 50% less physical footprint, and ultrafast energy response with no single point of failure.
This year’s Battery Show comes at a pivotal moment for storage project economics. Today, a storage project is a fifteen-year asset bought through a day-one procurement process, and the architecture chosen determines almost everything that follows. Systems that manage their batteries as a single block age at the pace of their worst modules. This is why most projects that hold up, and those that get written down, were effectively decided long before commissioning. MAC-BESS™ takes a different approach: it manages every battery module independently, extending usable life while needing fewer batteries and letting operators augment or replace with whatever supply is available at the time, and making units swappable without taking the system offline.
Dr. Al-Thaddeus Avestruz,
CEO of Volt Harbor, said:
The Battery Show is where the people actually building the next generation of battery supply, infrastructure, and end-use storage systems come together, which makes us excited to be on the show floor,
“The industry has spent a decade optimizing the batteries themselves. The layer that almost nobody has really touched is the power electronics architecture, and that is where the next step-change in cost, flexibility, and project life actually comes from.”
Volt Harbor’s platform is deploying a utility pilot in 2027 with DTE Energy, Michigan’s largest utility, where second-life EV batteries will buffer high-power EV charging events that exceed local grid capacity. The same architecture is being readied for data center deployments, where AI loads swing energy facilities from 30% to full rated capacity within milliseconds and back. The legacy power stack was never designed to absorb this pattern, and it’s part of why grid interconnection queues in major data center markets now run past four years. Storage and power electronics that absorb those spikes let the grid supply the average, which means more compute for every megawatt of existing interconnection, or a smaller interconnection that clears the queue sooner.

cylib appoints Roland Harings as chairman of its Advisory Board
Roland Harings, former CEO of Aurubis AG, has joined cylib’s Advisory Board and will serve as its chairman.
With his leadership experience, Roland Harings will support cylib in building an end-to-end battery recycling chain at industrial scale.
Aachen, Germany, 1 October 2026
– cylib, a German battery recycling company, has appointed Roland Harings to its Advisory Board and named him its chairman, effective October 1, 2026.
‍Experience across industrial value chains
Harings currently serves as CEO of Elsewedy Electric’s Metals Recycling Sector in Cairo, Egypt. He brings extensive international experience, including from his tenure as CEO of Aurubis, a leading multimetal recycling company. In addition, he has deep expertise in building and scaling industrial recycling solutions for complex materials, as well as in integrated value chains and all aspects of the circular economy.
Dr. Gideon Schwich,

Roland Harings brings strategic expertise in scaling circular economy businesses, expanding value chains and building long-term partnerships,
“His experience will be highly valuable to cylib as we ramp up our industrial operations in Wernberg-Köblitz and develop our hydrometallurgical facility in Dormagen. His appointment further strengthens our governance and strategic direction as the company enters its next phase of growth.”

Harings has been a member of cylib’s Industry Advisory Council since May 2025. His appointment as chairman of the Advisory Board builds on this existing relationship and strengthens cylib’s strategic positioning in its next phase of development.

title: Battery Show: Ford, GM Pivot to Grid Energy Storage
content:
Market Analysis
Automotive & Mobility
Stationary Batteries
Battery Manufacturing
Interviews
As EV demand stabilizes, Ford and GM are converting battery assets to address grid energy storage needs, a trend Pacific Northwest National Laboratory's Ted Miller will explore in his Battery Show keynote.
October 7, 2026
4 Min Read
PNNL's Grid Storage Launchpad
A tempering of the EV market has helped automakers and energy storage providers meet rising grid energy storage demand in the US—but more work remains to stay ahead of the curve. That includes finding domestic alternatives to Li-ion batteries.
That’s the expert perspective of Ted Miller, senior principal advisor for batteries and energy storage at
Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
(PNNL) based in Richmond, Washington.
Miller will share the next steps in progress to meet continued energy storage demand in his keynote “From Concept to Commercialization: Bridging the Domestic Battery Gap” at Informa’s
Battery Show North America
in Detroit from Oct. 12-15.
Ted Miller, senior principal advisor for batteries and energy storage at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. Credit: PNNL
EV market slowdown creates grid storage opportunity
Estimated Li-Ion battery demand for 2026 is nearly 1.5TWh for electric vehicles and almost 500GWh for stationary grid energy storage, he noted. While the outlook during the next decade anticipates growth in the EV and the stationary energy storage market, forecasts generally expect the EV market to dominate battery demand.
Related:
Data Centers Highlight AI-Related Sessions at The Battery Show
“Global battery supply is thus far meeting the demand. In some respect, a tempering of the EV market has been beneficial in meeting rising grid energy storage demand. Ford, GM, Volkswagen and other automakers have answered the call to action by converting existing EV battery manufacturing assets to address pressing grid energy storage needs.”
Miller will spotlight current efforts to create the scaleup and validation road map to meet demands for both segments.
PNNL's $75M Grid Storage Launchpad
“The Department of Energy Office of Electricity invested $75M at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory to create the Grid Storage Launchpad, a 93,000-square-foot facility to scale up and validate energy storage technology. GSL has extensive energy storage testing capability as well as advanced characterization technology and pilot prototyping, including a new prismatic cell production line. GSL supports more than 200 staff across PNNL working on energy storage and 90 ongoing projects.”
PNNL's new prismatic cell production line. Credit: PNNL
The Li-ion dilemma: Flexibility vs. critical material dependence
A key challenge to building an energy storage approach that satisfies both legs of this demand for renewable energy is developing and proving out new battery technologies. Miller noted that though there are many potential options for stationary grid energy storage — for instance, sodium-ion and flow batteries — Li-ion batteries “are the preferred choice for EVs and grid energy storage due to their demonstrated reliability and affordability.
Related:
Battery Makers Pivot from EV to Grid Storage, Defense & AI as Demand Landscape Changes
“The good news is that Li-ion technology has proven extremely flexible and suited to a range of applications and power and energy demands. The bad news is that Li-ion’s success has placed increasing demand on critical materials. Lack of U.S. domestic availability and processing at scale of some materials used in Li-ion batteries also contributes to concern. Developing and validating domestic alternatives to Li-ion batteries for grid energy storage may be one of the keys to growing both markets.”
Bridging the concept-to-commercialization gap
Another critical element to meeting domestic energy storage demand will be partnerships between industry and national labs to accelerate energy storage technology development and validation for domestic production at scale, Miller continued.
“The Department of Energy Office of Electricity and Transportation Technology Office have supported domestic battery research and development, including such organizations aa the United States Advanced Battery Consortium. The result has been development of battery technology used in Ford, GM and Stellantis electrified vehicles. The DOE has also supported battery materials development and testing at the national laboratories.
“What has been missing is the link from concept to commercialization. PNNL aims to bridge that gap by partnering with industry and employing facilities such as GSL to validate energy storage technology for domestic production.”
Related:
AGM Batteries Dominate Modern Cars as Electronics and Start-Stop Systems Drive Market Shift
How automaker expertise can transform grid energy storage
Miller will also address how the know-how of top US automakers Ford and GM can be leveraged to influence buildout of a robust domestic energy storage ecosystem.
“They can establish a new standard of design and validation process efficiency for grid energy storage systems,” he advised. “Lessons learned in the development of battery cell and system technology for automotive applications will inform stationary energy storage system designs.
PNNL prismatic cell. Credit: PNNL
“Conversely, as they grow their expertise in grid energy storage, those learnings can be applied to future mobile battery designs. Automakers have a compulsive and natural concern about ensuring battery safety. Similar concerns exist with grid energy storage systems and leveraging automotive industry best practices will enhance reliability and could even lower total system cost.”
Validation standards: Lessons from the USABC model
Validating complete energy storage systems and subsystems such as DC blocks is a critical step.
“The USABC played a key role in the early days of electric vehicles to establish standards and performance and safety measures. This again is where PNNL and other national laboratory partners can assist by collaborating on energy storage standards and test procedure development, as well as facilities and personnel to conduct the validation.”

title: Honeywell battery tech catches hidden defects
content:
Testing & Safety
Stationary Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
Battery News
The system uses electrochemical testing and ultrasound to inspect every cell, identifying problems that could cause failures or safety issues later.
October 7, 2026
3 Min Read
Inbound cell recieving solution diagram
Honeyell
Honeywell Technologies
will feature its recently launched Autonomous Cell Finishing technology at The Battery Show North America. Autonomous Cell Finishing (ACF) is designed for incoming inspection of battery cells. These battery evaluations are targeted for pack and module manufacturers producing EVs, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and space, aerospace, and defense applications.
With the Autonomous Cell Finishing solution, Honeywell can answer the question, "If a globally supplied cell is labeled as 'good,' is it really defect-free?" The solution is designed to save battery modules and packs from utilizing defective cells. One defective cell can cause module and pack imbalance, degradation, warranty claims, and even safety issues.
Detecting latent battery defects before production
There's a particular danger from latent defects, explains Alec Falzone, Battery Industry Leader – North America, Honeywell Technologies. "Batteries expand and contract over their life cycle. And when you have a very small out-of-spec situation, it becomes worse over time as things expand and contract."
Related:
Advanced Battery Safety and Testing with ARC Technology
Alec Falzone, Battery Industry Leader – North America, Honeywell Technologies. Credit: Honeywell
Latent defects can include contaminants, separator misalignment, and other issues that can show up with vibration, temperature, fast-charging, and other uses, Falzone said.
The core of the solution is high-speed, 100% in-line inspection and evaluations utilizing electrical, electrochemical, and 3D internal ultrasound characterization to thoroughly check every battery.
Three-pronged battery cell inspection technology
The first "leg of the stool" is electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), according to Falzone.
"Historically, it takes a long time to get a full-sweep EIS of good quality. However, with Honeywell's system, you can do every cell doing a multi-frequency sweep."
The second leg of the stool is looking at parasitic current, he said. "A cell may have a micro-short that's not a complete short circuit. When you short circuit [completely], your voltage goes to zero. But let's say there's metal particulates or electrode overhang where there's contact, but not enough to cause a safety event. There will still be parasitic current, but it's very small. We hold the voltage constant and measure current, and are able to extrapolate and identify problem cells very quickly."
The final leg of the stool is ultrasound inspection. "Working with our partner at Titan AES, we deploy their proprietary ultrasound technology—a non-destructive way to look inside the cell."
And the objective is to look at every cell, he said. "Not just one percent or 10% of the population, but every cell."
Related:
Battery Safety Testing and Monitoring Methods Explained
Honeywell then utilizes intelligent methods that enable closed-loop defect identification for removal of bad cells and provide real-time upstream feedback and resolution.
This is all orchestrated by Honeywell's Battery Manufacturing Excellence Platform (Battery-MXP). This system is fast, efficient, and not only catches obvious problems, but also identifies those latent defects. The platform also provides insights into the cycle-life of individual cells.
Honeywell's solution is able to catch these latent defects and provide what the company terms "Informative Defect Identification" to return the cells and provide feedback to the supplier for corrective action and preventative action (CAPA). This not only helps the pack and module manufacturer, but also helps the global battery supplier address issues for better future product and implement cost savings by reducing scrap costs.

title: How Carbon-Aware Scheduling Can Cut Data Center Emissions
content:
Data centers are often described as having fixed carbon footprints tied to their size and grid mix. In practice, operators can lower emissions by aligning flexible workloads with periods and locations where electricity is cleaner.
This “carbon-aware” approach complements long-term
renewable procurement
and efficiency programs, creating a practical pathway to reduce Scope 2 emissions and to demonstrate progress toward 24/7 carbon-free energy objectives. It also helps address growing regulatory expectations and stakeholder scrutiny of digital infrastructure’s electricity demand.
What Is Carbon-Aware Computing?
Carbon-aware computing is the practice of scheduling compute-intensive but time-flexible tasks – such as data backups, batch analytics, AI model training, report generation, and non-urgent patching – during windows when grid carbon intensity is lower or when on-site renewable or stored energy is available.
Related:
After the AI Rush, Can Data Centers Reclaim Sustainability?
The core idea is to compare the emissions profile of running a workload at one time or place versus another, and then choose execution options that minimize emissions within operational constraints.
How Carbon-Aware Scheduling Works
Electricity grids are dynamic. Solar production peaks during daylight, wind output varies seasonally and hourly, and some regions benefit from geothermal, hydro, or nuclear baseload. Grid conditions change by the hour based on demand, transmission constraints, and market dispatch. As a result, the emissions intensity of a kilowatt-hour can swing significantly across a single day.
Carbon-aware computing takes advantage of this variability by aligning flexible workloads with periods when low-carbon energy is most available. Operators assess which workloads can shift in time or location without violating service-level agreements (SLAs), latency requirements, data residency constraints, or change-control policies. The outcome is a set of scheduling policies that favor cleaner windows while maintaining service objectives. That way, compute-hungry tasks can run without forcing incremental demand at higher-emitting hours.
Implementation Realities: Data, Forecasts, and Constraints
The principles behind carbon-aware computing are simple enough. In a data center context, however, implementing carbon-aware strategies can be challenging for a few key reasons. Common hurdles include limited observability into tenant workloads (particularly in
colocation facilities
), difficulty predicting workload power draw due to dynamic CPU/GPU utilization and I/O patterns, and uncertainty in renewable forecasts.
Related:
Do Data Centers Cause Air Pollution? It Depends on Power.
Additionally, not all workloads are flexible. Mission-critical, latency-sensitive applications may be fixed in time and location.
A practical approach starts with cataloging workloads by flexibility class, power profile, and compliance constraints. From there, operators can pilot carbon-aware scheduling on clearly deferrable tasks.
What Operators Can Do Today
Effective carbon-aware programs typically include:
Instrumentation and metering.
Enhance power telemetry at the rack and cluster level to identify high-draw, schedulable workloads and measure realized emissions impacts.
Behind-the-meter resources.
On-site renewables
improve certainty that incremental workload energy is low-carbon. Generic utility grids typically can’t guarantee that the energy they supply comes from any particular source. However, data centers with their own solar, wind, or geothermal energy supplies can do this. When paired with
batteries
, operators can time-shift energy and shave peaks. While few sites can economically size batteries to cover full facility load, modest storage can be sufficient to power energy-intensive, deferrable tasks during clean windows.
Reduce Emissions, Keep Reliability
Perfect optimization is unrealistic for most data center environments. Even so, carbon-aware computing can deliver real reductions by capturing the “clean hours” that already exist on many grids. Over time, it becomes another reliability-minded tool – one that lowers emissions while respecting the operational realities that keep data centers running.

title: Australia home battery installs hit 966.5 MWh in September - Energy Storage
content: The latest report from energy industry data analyst SunWiz shows 311.8 MW of small-scale solar (0-100 kW) was registered across Australia in September 2026, a 7.29% increase on the 290 MW installed during the previous month. The September tally is one of the highest monthly totals of the year, eclipsed only by the 505 MW registered in April 2026 and the 320 MW installed in July. The September 2026 total is well clear of the approximately 240 MW registered in the same month last year. SunWiz Managing Director Warwick Johnston said the market continues to benefit from the federal government’s Cheaper Home Batteries Scheme, that requires residential batteries to be installed alongside new or existing solar systems to qualify for the rebate. “Courtesy of the battery rebate driving PV installations, there is now more sub-100 kW PV installed in 2026 year-to-date than in the entirety of 2025,” he said, noting that the January-September tally is 43% ahead of the same point in 2025. Image: SunWiz Johnston said five of the eight states and territories had increased installations last month with Queensland leading the way with 91.8 MW of new solar registered, a 14% increase on the August 2026 tally. New South Wales added 90.1 MW, an 11% increase on the previous month. The 10-15 kW bracket “remains the clear backbone of the market,” said Johnston, with 105.94 MW added in September, a 13% increase on the previous month and more than double the 6-8 kW band which was next-largest with 53.04 MW, and well ahead of the 15-20 kW bracket (43.41 MW). The national average system size edged up to 9.98 kW from August’s 9.86 kW, well clear of May’s 12-month low of 9.35 kW but still well below December’s high of 12.07 kW. Home batteries installations reached an estimated 966.5 MWh in September 2026, up 12.5% on the 859 MWh registered in August and the strongest month since April’s 3,262 MWh peak. “The battery market has stabilized near to 1 GW a month, Johnston said, adding that the average battery size continues to grow, with 45% of the market now exceeding 30 kWh. The 20-30 kWh bracket remains the largest segment with 368 MWh of capacity registered last month, a 13% increase on the previous month, while the 40-50 kWh band delivered 250 MWh and 30-40 kWh 190 MWh. The installation of smaller batteries slowed with the 10-20 kWh bracket easing 2% to 148 MWh and 0-10 kWh band dropping 13% to 11 MWh. The national average system size rose to 26.30 kWh, its fourth consecutive gain. title: Chile approves 158 MW solar project with 1.3 GWh BESS - Energy Storage
content: Chile’s Environmental Assessment Service (SEA) has approved the environmental impact statement for the Sidon Solar photovoltaic project, which will include 158.17 MWdc of solar generation and 1,296 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity. Sidon Solar SpA, established by Trina Solar Systems (Chile) SpA in July 2023, will develop the project across the municipalities of Cabrero in the Biobío region and Pemuco in the Ñuble region. The approved configuration comprises 218,160 solar modules rated at 725 W, installed on 4,040 single-axis trackers. The panels will cover two areas totaling 185.44 hectares and will be supported by 18 transformer stations. The project’s DC capacity is lower than the 162.55 MWdc included in the configuration submitted for environmental assessment in 2025. That version specified 150 MWac of generation, which also appears as the project’s net capacity in a June 2025 project report from Chile’s Ministry of Energy. Sidon Solar will also include 324 Huawei Luna2000 battery units across a 30,967-square-meter site. The environmental approval sets total storage capacity at 1,296 MWh, with an injection capacity of 150 MW for five hours. The batteries will shift part of the solar generation for injection into Chile’s National Electricity System (SEN) after dark. Electricity will be evacuated from the project substation through a 220 kV transmission line to the Entre Ríos substation, which is already connected to the SEN. The 5.7 km line will have a single circuit and a nominal capacity of 170 MVA. Construction of the transmission infrastructure is expected to take 17 months. The project will occupy 275.31 hectares, including the solar plant and transmission line. The declared investment is $100 million, while the project is expected to operate for 33 years. Construction is scheduled to take 24 months and is expected to employ an average of 350 workers, with a peak workforce of 600. The operational phase is expected to require 12 workers for maintenance. Sidon Solar has also committed to promoting the hiring of workers from Cabrero and Pemuco through the municipalities’ employment offices. title: Nala Renewables starts construction on 250 MWh Finland BESS - Energy Storage
content: Global renewable energy investment platform Nala Renewables has issued a notice to proceed (NTP) for the construction of its 125 MW / 250 MWh Nala Vuolijoki battery energy storage system (BESS) in Finland. The company stated the NTP marks the project’s transition from development into the construction phase, describing Nala Vuolijoki as “one of the largest BESS projects in Finland to start construction.” Nala Renewables acquired the standalone Vuolijoki BESS from Swiss developer Fu-Gen in February 2026 as a ready-to-build (RTB) asset. Along with Nala Vuolijoki, the company recently energized its 50 MW / 100 MWh Kauhava BESS and acquired the 100 MW / 200 MWh Kärppiö BESS from Fu-Gen in September 2026. In total, the three projects bring Nala Renewables’ pipeline to 275 MW / 550 MWh in Finland. Inside BESS manufacturing: Maxxen’s utility-scale storage factory in Europe Nala Renewables is developing and will own the Nala Vuolijoki project. Finnish engineering firm Despro has been appointed as engineering, procurement, and construction management (EPCM) contractor and will also provide local engineering support. Destia Oy will serve as balance of plant (BOP) contractor, while Sungrow will supply the battery energy storage technology. “By combining in-house expertise across development, financing, construction and operations with close partner collaboration, we are well positioned to navigate the evolving complexities of the energy transition and deliver high-quality projects that support both grid resilience and renewable energy growth in Finland and our other focus markets,” said Remy Verot, interim CEO at Nala Renewables. The project secured long-term financing from Rabobank. “We are pleased to support Nala Renewables with the long-term financing of the Nala Vuolijoki 125 MW / 250 MWh battery energy storage project. This transaction builds on our relationship with Nala and its owner, IFM Investors, a key institutional client of Rabobank,” said Gijs Hofman, executive director at Rabobank. Finland’s reserve markets are changing, and Fingrid’s annual auction prices for upward and downward frequency containment reserves fell for 2026, while the grid operator shifted more procurement toward hourly markets. It makes Nala Vuolijoki’s intended revenue mix and trading arrangements worth watching as the project moves through its build. Recently, Swedish energy infrastructure company Ingrid Capacity secured €65 million from investment firm Mirova for two BESS projects in Sweden and Finland. The 45 MW / 90 MWh Pedersöre BESS in Finland will be developed, operated, and optimized by Ingrid Capacity under a strategic agreement. title: BMW's new iX4 has 428 miles of range, but it starts at north of $66,000 [Images]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 8 2026 - 8:02 am PT
revealed the new iX4, its new electric coupe-SUV that can drive up to 428 miles on a single charge.
Meet BMW’s newest EV, the iX4
The iX4 arrives as a sportier, coupe-like sibling to the new iX3 SUV. Following the iX3 and i3, the iX4 is the third EV from BMW’s Neue Klasse lineup.
Earlier this week,
images of the iX4 leaked online
with reports claiming it would make its official debut on October 8.
The rumors proved true. BMW unveiled the all-new iX4 on Thursday, an all-electric replacement for the X4. Like the iX3 and i3, the new iX4 features BMW’s Neue Klasse minimalist design and technology.
The 2027 BMW iX4 will go on sale in March 2027 as the iX4 50 xDrive, with a range-topping M60 xDrive version set to launch shortly after.
Both feature a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The standard 50 xDrive delivers a combined 468 hp and 475 lb-ft of torque, which BMW says is good for a 0 to 60 mph sprint in 4.7 seconds.
The iX4 M60 takes it up a notch, packing a combined 603 hp and 645 lb-ft of torque with a 0 to 60 mph time of just 3.9 seconds.
Prices, driving range, and a look at the interior
BMW said the iX4 50 xDrive boasts an estimated range of up to 428 miles using a 112.2 kWh battery and its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system. On the WLTP cycle, it gets up to 828 km (514 miles).
Thanks to its 800V architecture, both models can add up to 184 miles of range in just 10 minutes with charging speeds of up to 400 kW. BMW says charging from 10% to 21% takes 21 minutes.
BMW iX4 M60 xDrive (Source: BMW)
With a rakish roofline, the iX4 adopts more of a grand tourer, or “coupe-SUV”-like silhouette, rather than the traditional boxy SUV design like the iX3. The sportier design helps it achieve a drag coefficient of 0.23.
Inside, the new iX4 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse interior. As such, it features a 17.9″ central infotainment screen and 43″ Panoramic Vision that stretches across the base of the windshield.
BMW iX4 interior (Source: BMW)
Buyers can upgrade to the optional BMW 3D Head-Up Display, positioned above the Panoramic Vision.
The M60 model comes with an exclusive M Sport steering wheel with a red marker at the 12 o’clock position, colored stitching, and shift paddles. It also includes two exclusive buttons to activate Boost Mode and M Mode.
BMW iX4 interior (Source: BMW)
Measuring 188.3″ long, 74.6″ wide, and 63.3″ tall, with a 114.1″ wheelbase, the new BMW iX4 is about the same size as the iX3, but slightly lower thanks to its sloped coupe roofline.
Like all BMW Gen6 models, the new iX4 supports bidirectional charging, letting it serve as a mobile power bank.
It will also offer SAE Level 2 driver assistance systems with Highway Assistant, enabling “attentive hands-free driving” on the highway at up to 85 mph.
BMW iX4 M60 (left) and 50 xDrive (right) (Source: BMW)
BMW iX4 50 xDrive
will go on sale in March 2027, starting at $66,200, not including the $1,495 destination fee, or $4,700 more than the iX3 50 xDrive.
We will learn prices for the range-topping M60 variant closer to launch, but it could cost upwards of around $85,000 to $90,000.
In comparison, the Tesla Model Y Performance is even cheaper than the base BMW iX4 50, starting at $57,990 in the US.

title: Tesla files permit for Semi service center in Las Vegas as ramp begins
content:
Tesla Semi
Fred Lambert
| Oct 8 2026 - 8:20 am PT
Image: Tesla
Tesla is preparing a dedicated Tesla Semi service center in Las Vegas, according to a new building permit filed with Clark County, Nevada.
It’s one of the first concrete signs of the service network Tesla needs to support its electric Class 8 truck, which only entered volume production two weeks ago.
What the permit shows
The Clark County record (BD26-39451) describes the project in plain terms: “Tesla Semi Service Center. Tenant Improvement in new shell building.”
The site is 3780 N Las Vegas Blvd, part of the LV Logistics One industrial development on the northeast side of the valley, between I-15 and Nellis Air Force Base. The property owner is listed as L V Logistics One Property Owner LP, a Dallas-based entity, so Tesla is a tenant here and not building from scratch.
The application lists Tesla as the tenant and classifies the use as a “Repair Garage,” with the work type marked as a remodel under the 2024 building code. Its status is “Awaiting Plans,” which means the application is in but Tesla hasn’t submitted its construction drawings yet. So this isn’t opening next month.
The neighboring building in the same development, at 3790 N Las Vegas Blvd, gives a good idea of what Tesla is moving into. It’s a 152,256-square-foot logistics building completed in 2024 with 32-foot clear height, 20 dock-high doors, and a 122-foot truck court, according to its lease listing. That’s the kind of space you need to pull Class 8 tractors in and out all day.
Why Las Vegas
Las Vegas sits on the I-15 corridor, one of the busiest freight routes in the West, linking the Southern California ports and warehouses of the Inland Empire to Las Vegas and on to Salt Lake City. The run from the Inland Empire to Las Vegas is roughly 230 to 270 miles, well within the 325-mile rating of the Standard Range Semi.
It also fills a gap. When Tesla
added 64 planned Megacharger sites to its map in February
, Nevada got only two, and the only operating Nevada site is at Giga Nevada in Sparks, about 440 miles north.
launched volume production of the Semi
at its new Sparks factory late last month, claiming capacity for 50,000 trucks a year. Customers at the event included PepsiCo, DHL, US Foods, and ABF, and Einride ordered 500 trucks in August.
But trucks need to be fixed somewhere. Tesla has shown plans for about 20 dedicated Semi service locations across the US, and this is the first one we’ve found in a public permit filing.

title: Tesla leaned on Dutch regulator to ease its FSD review, emails show
content:
Tesla Autopilot
Fred Lambert
| Oct 8 2026 - 6:57 am PT
Tesla spent months pushing the Dutch vehicle regulator RDW to scale back its review of “Full Self-Driving (Supervised),” including disputing a €365,000 bill, according to emails obtained by Reuters. RDW later approved the system and is now asking the EU to do the same.
That Dutch approval is the foundation of Tesla’s entire FSD push in Europe. Eight EU countries now allow the system, and a bloc-wide vote could come as early as December.
What the emails show
Reuters’ investigation
, published yesterday, is built on hundreds of pages of correspondence between Tesla and regulators in seven European countries, obtained through public-records requests.
The Dutch exchanges are the most telling. In November 2024, a Tesla staffer told RDW that starting vehicle tests by the end of that month was “mission critical for our leadership,” and that leadership would “measure the goodwill” of the regulator by whether it hit that date.
Then came the money. European rules make automakers cover the regulator’s costs for these reviews, which isn’t the case in the US. In April 2025, Tesla called RDW’s €365,000 invoice for five months of work an “extremely high cost” and said it would hold payment until it got an hour-by-hour accounting of every RDW employee on the project. It also objected to paying for five RDW staffers to visit Giga Berlin.
A week after the invoice complaint, an RDW staffer invited Tesla to suggest how the regulator “might adjust or reduce the required effort moving forward.”
Other concessions followed, according to the documents:
Tesla argued its own test reports should be enough instead of having an RDW inspector travel to witness tests. RDW offered to monitor part of them remotely.
Tesla pushed back on a meeting about its over-the-air software updates. An RDW staffer replied that it didn’t want to “dive too deep in technical details” and didn’t “question the quality and process for OTA’s.”
Tesla demanded advance notice of exactly what tests RDW would run on its cars, plus the names of the safety drivers. RDW agreed and stressed its “shared goals and objectives” with Tesla.
RDW told Reuters that its engagement with manufacturers “does not compromise the independence or thoroughness of our assessment.” But it redacted large parts of the emails, and it still won’t publish its own FSD test data, citing Tesla trade secrets.
That last part matters. It’s a regulator asking 26 other countries to trust a review that the public isn’t allowed to see.
The safety data doesn’t support the “lives saved” claim
Tesla’s other pressure lever is its own safety research. It shared an “evidence dashboard” with EU member states in April and posted its European study on X last month, calling it “one of the key pieces of evidence” behind the Dutch approval.
Seven traffic-safety researchers who reviewed the methodology for Reuters found the FSD sample was too small, in the tens or hundreds of thousands of miles, to compare against hundreds of millions of miles of manual Tesla driving in Europe. Instead of crashes, Tesla measured “surrogates” like honking, blinker usage, hard braking and hard cornering, and the FSD cars were driven by Tesla’s own professional test drivers rather than regular owners.
Tesla’s own fine print says the comparisons can’t be read as “causal estimates.” So the study doesn’t show FSD prevents crashes, let alone deaths.
And yet that’s exactly what Tesla is telling the public. When it posted the study, Tesla said Europe’s average of 53 road deaths per day are “largely preventable with technology we have today” and that the benefit “remains locked behind bureaucracy.” When French transport minister Philippe Tabarot said in July that France couldn’t back FSD, Musk replied that “delaying the approval of FSD in France will cost lives.”
“When you start getting into ‘lives saved,’ that’s where it gets nonsensical,” Marco Benedetti, a former NHTSA statistician now at the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute, told Reuters.
This isn’t new. In the US, Tesla compared airbag-deployment crashes on FSD against every crash in federal data where a car had to be towed to claim FSD was 10x safer than human drivers, later revised down to 7x. Reuters reports Tesla sent that same US research to European regulators too.
Fans as a lobbying arm
Musk asked for this part out loud. At last year’s shareholder meeting, he said “pressure from our customers in Europe to push the regulators to approve would be appreciated,” and a Tesla account on X later linked owners to RDW’s contact form.
It worked, in the sense that regulators got flooded. Public-records requests show Tesla owners sent dozens of emails to regulators in Sweden and Norway, many repeating the life-saving claims, and Tabarot’s X account filled up with posts holding him personally responsible for road deaths.
Norway’s Stein-Helge Mundal warned Nordic counterparts in an email that regulators would “need to use a lot of effort to answer misled consumers.” His statement to Reuters is the best line in the whole story: “We do not approve systems because they are popular, and we do not reject them because they are controversial.”
The pressure is paying off
France is the clearest example. Two months after saying no, Tabarot posted a photo of a video call with Musk last month, describing a “constructive exchange” and “working closely” with Tesla on changes “that will enable France to support its approval.”
reported last month
, the EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles didn’t vote on FSD on October 6, despite Tesla pointing to that date. Approval needs 15 of 27 member states representing 65% of the EU population. Croatia has since become the eighth country to allow FSD after the
Netherlands, Lithuania
, Denmark, Belgium, Estonia, Slovenia and Czechia, but those are mostly small markets. Germany, Italy and Spain still haven’t signed on, and Sweden wants the EU to reject FSD unless Tesla removes the ability to set speeds above the limit.
There’s some irony in RDW’s role here. In 2025, it
publicly corrected Tesla
when the automaker claimed RDW had “committed” to a February approval, saying “for the RDW, (road) safety is paramount.” Behind the scenes, it was offering to reduce its effort after Tesla complained about a bill that’s a rounding error on $95 billion in annual revenue.
Electrek’s Take
None of this proves FSD is unsafe in Europe. But it shows the approval process isn’t the independent, data-driven review Tesla fans like to point to whenever someone questions it.
The pattern is the same one we’ve seen in the US for years. Tesla won’t publish the one number that would settle the debate (miles between critical disengagements by customers on FSD), so it substitutes proxies, cherry-picked comparisons and big “lives saved” claims. Then it points its fan base at anyone who asks for more. In the US, there was no approval to win. In Europe, there is, and Tesla is clearly treating the regulator as an obstacle to manage rather than a safety check.
And there’s a real commercial reason for the rush. Tesla’s European sales fell 28% last year, and FSD is one of the few things it can sell that BYD, Volkswagen and others can’t yet match on European roads. We get why Tesla wants it badly. That doesn’t make it RDW’s job to help.
If FSD is as safe as Tesla says, the fix is simple. Publish the European customer data, let RDW release its test results, and let independent researchers check the work. A regulator that offers to “reduce the required effort” after a billing dispute shouldn’t be the one deciding for 450 million people.
The EU vote is now expected in December at the earliest. The question is whether Germany, Italy and Spain ask for that data first, or follow France and fold.

title: VinFast plans US electric buses – and it’ll handle more than the ride
content:
Electric Buses
Michelle Lewis
| Oct 8 2026 - 8:40 am PT
Photo: VinFast
wants to put electric buses on US streets, and its pitch goes beyond the vehicles: charging, maintenance, and operations bundled into one package. Deliveries of buses approved for US use are expected to begin in Q1 2028.
The Vietnamese EV maker announced the plan at the APTA TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago. It signed an initial agreement with NexMove, a joint venture between passenger transportation company Transportation Management Services and commercial EV charging provider Zeem Solutions.
For transit agencies and fleet operators, the appeal is having one provider handle the buses and the services needed to keep them running. NexMove plans to offer a service agreement promising 97% uptime.
VinFast says around 2,000 of its electric buses already operate in Vietnam. Its buses feature LFP batteries, fast charging, and camera and radar driver alerts, but the announcement doesn’t specify US models, range, prices, or charging speeds.
NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem charging depots so fleet operators and transit agencies can go check them out. Those vehicles won’t have US approval yet. The partners also aim to develop US manufacturing that meets Federal Transit Administration requirements, although no location or production schedule was announced.
Paul Gioupis, Founder and CEO of Zeem Solutions and cofounder of NexMove, said:
In late July, our team visited VinFast’s manufacturing operations and was impressed by the number of buses in daily service and by the scale and quality of production. This is a proven product with real operating history. We look forward to working with VinFast toward US manufacturing that meets Federal Transit Administration requirements, so public transit agencies can put these buses to work.

title: 200MW/400MWh！亿纬锂能惠州日盛独立共享储能电站正式并网
content:
9月29日，惠州日盛200MW/400MWh独立共享储能电站并网仪式隆重举行。惠州市政府党组成员、副市长曲维震，市人工智能和机器人发展局（惠州市能源和重点项目局）党组成员、副局长庆伟，博罗县委常委、县政府副县长黄剑波，亿纬锂能董事长刘金成博士，联合创始人、总裁刘建华及核心管理层、合作伙伴、媒体代表共同出席见证。
惠州日盛200MW/400MWh独立共享储能电站占地25,333平方米，装机200MW/400MWh，以220千伏接入电网，搭载公司自研储能电芯逾45万颗，年均充放电超1亿度，预计年减排二氧化碳约8万吨。作为亿纬锂能首个并网的电网侧独立共享储能电站，将为广东电网提供调峰调频支撑，平抑新能源出力波动。
该电站实现核心产品自研自产、工程建设自主管理、运营能力自主搭建的"三个自主"首次落地，完整验证了从规划设计、部署施工到电网调度适配与运维的全链条能力。广东亿纬数字能源技术有限公司副总经理唐俊明介绍，自研电芯具备长寿命、高能效、高安全、易运维等优势，公司将以此沉淀更适配的系统解决方案，为客户提供更优的产品与整站增值服务。
惠州市博罗县委常委、县政府副县长黄剑波表示，该电站是博罗深入贯彻"双碳"战略、发展新质生产力的重要成果。"项目投运后不仅能够充分发挥调峰调频、顶峰保供的能源保障作用，还将持续产生稳定产值与税收，实现生态效益、经济效益、社会效益的有机统一。"
亿纬锂能董事长刘金成博士表示，当前世界格局深刻变革，粮食与能源问题是全球核心议题。光伏、风电作为新能源主力，源自太阳能，但天然存在出力波动的短板；保障电网稳定，是新能源发展的必由之路。而电网稳定技术不能只停留在实验室，必须经受高温、暴雨、严寒等实战考验，该电站正是亿纬锂能面向亚热带高温高湿场景的实战试验场。当前亿纬储能业务稳步拓展，产品已落地欧美大型储能与数据中心项目。这座电站的并网，是亿纬锂能储能事业的重要里程碑，公司将持续深耕储能技术，打造面向全球的千亿级储能产业，助力双碳战略落地。
未来，亿纬锂能将继续以技术创新服务能源转型，为构建新型电力系统、实现碳中和目标贡献力量。

title: 天赐材料通过港交所聆讯
content:
近日，港交所披露天赐材料通过主板上市聆讯，摩根大通、中信证券、广发证券担任联席保荐人。这标志着又一家锂电产业链龙头企业距离“A+H”两地上市更进一步。
据了解天赐材料成立于2000年，于2014年在深交所上市，此次赴港上市，天赐材料曾于2025年9月22日首次递表，后申请失效。2026年3月27日二次递表，并于8月19日获得中国证监会境外发行上市备案批复，拟发行不超过4.13亿股境外上市普通股。
作为全球电解液领域的绝对龙头，天赐材料自2016年起已连续十年位居全球电解液出货量第一，2025年全球市场份额约36%。同时，公司还是全球最大的六氟磷酸锂及双氟磺酰亚胺锂（LiFSI）供应商，2025年六氟磷酸锂出货量占全球市场份额38.2%，LiFSI出货量占全球份额47.2%。
业绩方面，招股书显示，2023年至2025年，公司营业收入分别为154.05亿元、125.18亿元和166.50亿元，期内利润分别为18.42亿元、4.78亿元和13.44亿元。
进入2026年，公司业绩大幅增长，上半年实现营业收入147.10亿元，同比增长109.28%；归母净利润28.61亿元，同比大增967.91%；扣非净利润28.07亿元，同比大增1096.69%；综合毛利率大幅提升至33.55%。

title: 宁德时代拟向西班牙电池项目提供5000万欧元贷款
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月30日，宁德时代发布公告称，旗下全资子公司卢森堡时代新能源科技有限公司拟向控股子公司时代星曜新能源科技有限公司提供5000万欧元（约合人民币3.81亿元）股东贷款承诺，资金将用于西班牙合资电池工厂的建设投资及日常经营。
根据公告，时代星曜可根据实际需求分一笔或多笔提取贷款，借款年利率为3.55%，期限自每笔提款日起至协议约定的到期日止。贷款本金及利息在满足相关合规程序的情况下，可转换为时代星曜股份。
时代星曜是宁德时代与Stellantis在西班牙成立的合资公司，也是双方合资建设西班牙电池工厂的投资建设主体。宁德时代通过卢森堡时代间接持有时代星曜50%股权，Stellantis旗下Stellantis España、Stellantis Auto SAS分别持股40%和10%。
该公司成立于2025年1月31日，注册资本1.72亿欧元（约合人民币13.11亿元），主要负责机动车辆的电池电芯、模组及零部件的制造、销售和供应，并建设、运营相关生产设施。
此次贷款期限最长为12个月，即自借款协议签署之日起满12个月，或全部本金及应计利息偿还完毕、按照协议转换为时代星曜股份之日，以较早者为准。时代星曜其他股东也将按照各自出资比例提供同等条件的财务资助。
宁德时代表示，本次资金支持主要用于满足时代星曜的运营资金需求，支持西班牙合资电池工厂建设。由于时代星曜属于宁德时代合并报表范围内的控股子公司，公司能够对其业务、财务及资金实施风险控制。

title: 德赛智储与威思顿电气达成战略合作
content:
9月29日，惠州市德赛电池有限公司（以下简称“德赛电池”）的全资子公司——惠州市德赛智储科技有限公司（以下简称“德赛智储”）与烟台东方威思顿电气有限公司（以下简称“威思顿电气”）在山东烟台举行战略合作框架协议签约仪式。德赛电池董事长曾剑云、德赛电池高级副总裁郭庆明、德赛智储副总经理李勤峰，与威思顿电气方面代表共同出席并见证签约。
根据协议，双方将建立为期两年的战略合作关系，围绕离网储能、微电网、独立电站、重卡换电等应用场景展开全面合作，并在主动安全电芯应用与海外市场拓展上深度协同。合作期内，双方力争完成储能系统规模不低于500MWh，其中约一半规模将优先采用搭载AI主动安全电芯的储能系统。
惠州市德赛智储科技有限公司是专业从事储能电池、储能机柜及储能系统产品研发、生产与供应的企业。公司围绕储能电池、储能机柜与储能系统集成等核心环节，持续构建研发、制造与供应能力，现已具备储能产品生产、交付及技术服务能力，可为项目落地提供从产品到服务的系统化支撑，多年来，德赛智储以安全、可靠、高效的储能产品与服务，助力客户推进多场景储能应用规模化落地。
威思顿电气成立于2003年，是东方电子集团旗下国家级重点高新技术企业。公司深耕数字电力、智慧能源、数智工厂三大领域，聚焦用电、配电、发输变、综合能源、微电网等八大业务方向及海外市场，是能源计量与管理、电网配用电整体解决方案的领先提供商。今年年初，威思顿电气已成立专门的微电网部门，将储能列为重点发力方向，与德赛智储的业务布局高度契合。
未来两年，双方将依托德赛在电芯与系统集成环节的制造能力，叠加威思顿电气在海内外电力市场的渠道与项目经验，共同推进储能产品在微电网、独立电站与重卡换电等场景的规模化应用，并同步探索海外市场的联合拓展。

title: 江西、湖南两大固态电池项目落地
content:
近期，多家固态电池企业持续推进产能及项目布局。9月29日，纯锂新能源江西湖口1GWh固态电池智造基地正式投产；9月30日，恩力动力固态电池华中区域总部暨生产基地项目落地湘潭经开区，项目总投资约20亿元。
纯锂新能源1GWh固态电池智造基地投产
“湖口县融媒体中心”消息显示，9月29日，纯锂新能源湖口基地投产暨产业合作峰会举行，纯锂新能源江西湖口1GWh固态电池智造基地正式投产。
据了解，2024年1月，北京纯锂新能源科技有限公司与湖口县金砂湾工业投资集团有限公司共同成立湖口纯锂新能源有限公司，专注于全固态电池研发与制造，产品可应用于小动力、储能、船舶动力、低空经济、机器人及特种装备等领域。
2025年，湖口纯锂新能源年产1GWh固态储能电池生产建设项目完成环评审批。2026年7月，项目进入设备安装及调试阶段，并计划于9月底试生产，最终于9月29日正式投产。
今年5月，纯锂新能源披露，其500MWh量产线已经达产，并正推进GWh级产线建设。同月，其完成数千万元Pre-A+轮融资，资金将主要用于产品研发、市场拓展及产线落地。
在产品及应用方面，纯锂新能源今年2月表示，将推动固态电池产品从小批量测试生产迈向规模化市场布局，并开发第二代固态电池产品，重点拓展机器人、无人机、乘用车、电动船舶等应用场景；同时扩大亦庄电动自行车换电项目试点规模。
恩力动力20亿固态电池项目落地湘潭
9月30日，湘潭经开区新发展集团有限公司与北京恩力动力技术有限公司签订项目合作协议，恩力动力固态电池华中区域总部暨生产基地项目正式落地湖南湘潭经开区，项目总投资约20亿元。
根据协议，恩力动力将在湘潭建设集研发、生产、销售于一体的固态电池华中区域总部暨生产基地，并配套建设智能仓储等设施，引进自动化生产装备，完善固态电池产业链布局。
恩力动力主要布局硫化物固态电池技术路线，产品包括软包电芯等，覆盖无人机、机器人、电动摩托等应用场景。据介绍，恩力动力高比能软包电池覆盖3.5Ah至100Ah规格，能量密度达到270Wh/kg至600Wh/kg。
目前，恩力动力已在安徽滁州建设2GWh半固态电芯生产基地，并在江苏无锡布局电池Pack智造基地，业务覆盖电芯制造及系统集成。
今年以来，恩力动力持续推进固态电池产业化及应用布局。1月，恩力动力与恩捷股份签署战略合作协议，双方将在隔膜及固态电解质等领域开展合作。
4月，恩力动力与丰翼科技联合研发的物流无人机专用电池取得阶段性进展。据介绍，该产品已具备50公斤载重、百公里航程的常态化运营能力。双方计划未来三年推动480Wh/kg电芯量产，并进一步提升电池循环寿命。
同月，恩力动力与均胜电子共同出资成立宁波均恩新能源有限公司，布局具身智能领域动力能源市场，重点开展固态电池研发、生产与销售。
在产品规划方面，恩力动力此前表示，2026年重点推出1—20Ah全固态电芯，主要面向无人机、机器人等非车用市场；2027年进一步拓展至电动摩托车及小型电动车领域，并计划到2030年实现车规级全固态电池规模化应用。

title: 海博思创包头储算一体化项目暨词元工厂开工
content:
9月29日，海博思创在包头举行“算电协同能智互融——海博思创包头储算一体化项目暨词元工厂开工仪式”，打造储算一体化创新载体，通过储能电站与分布式智算中心协同建设，推动算力基础设施与能源系统协同发展，实现从储能赛道向词元领域的跨界整合。
面向智能化发展新时代，算力产业规模持续扩大，对电力供给的稳定性、灵活性和适配性提出了更高要求。为积极响应国家算电协同新基建战略部署，海博思创在包头打造储算一体化项目，通过电网侧储能与分布式智算中心的一体化统筹规划、就近布局、协同运行，探索绿色算力发展新路径，全力打造全国算电协同标杆工程。
中国计算机行业协会算电协同工委会副秘书长刘京娟表示，算电协同已从行业共识上升为国家战略部署，此次开工的项目正是一个很好的样本：通过电网侧储能与分布式智算中心统筹规划、协同发展新模式，构建“源网荷储”闭环；以词元工厂形态组织算力生产，将算力产出对应到可计量、可定价的词元服务，为算电协同从提供算力资源向提供算力服务的价值转化提供实践场景，也为行业提供先行先试的样本。
海博思创董事会秘书、首席财务官高书清表示，当前，人工智能产业快速崛起，算力已成为数字经济的核心生产力。此次创新建设的词元工厂，依托一体化能源算力底座，将对外输出优质算力云服务，打通能源供给、储能调峰、算力调度全链条，实现源、储、算高效协同。通过储能平抑新能源发电波动，将间歇性绿电转化为稳定可控的优质电能；同时，依托算力的柔性负荷特性，项目主动适应电网波动，真正实现“算随电走、电随算调”，构建可持续、可复制的算电协同商业模式，不断拓展储能产业高价值应用场景。
针对高端算力严苛的电能质量需求，此项目将采用自主可控的核心技术体系，依托海博思创自研HyperPTU电力方舱和HyperSST固态变压器，实现高效电能变换、精准调压、灵活调控，全面提升区域能源系统调控能力。
产业新赛道的蓬勃发展，离不开开放协同、生态共建。海博思创将依托此项目，建立并深化与并行科技、华为数字能源、广东水电二局等伙伴的合作。并行科技领跑高端算力服务，华为数字能源深耕电力电子与数字技术，广东水电二局拥有雄厚工程建设实力，海博思创聚焦储能技术研发与场景落地。各方优势互补、资源互通，共同探索产业新模式，共建算电协同产业新生态。
北京并行科技股份有限公司董事、副总裁、AI云创始人赵鸿冰表示，本次项目聚焦算电协同、能智互融，直面当前智算中心供电稳定性、绿色消纳两大行业难题，是极具探索价值的工程示范。并行科技期待与海博思创深化合作，围绕储、算一体化场景，联合验证算力与储能联动的工程落地路径，把风光资源优势转化为稳定可用的绿色算力。
广东水电二局集团有限公司集团党委委员、副总经理徐城彬表示，基于与海博思创合作落地的多个GWh级储能项目的良好基础，本次项目开工是双方合作的进一步深化，期待未来与海博思创深耕合作，打造更多标杆项目，为国家新型电力系统及内蒙古绿色智能产业发展贡献更大力量。
开工仪式同期，海博思创与并行科技举行了合作签约仪式。双方将在算电协同、词元工厂及算力云服务等领域携手开拓市场，围绕技术研发、商务合作、高质量交付、售后服务等环节，推动产业协同创新，为全国乃至海外客户提供高质量的词元服务。海博思创董事会秘书、首席财务官高书清与北京并行科技股份有限公司董事、副总裁、AI云创始人赵鸿冰共同签署合作协议。
能源革新与数字化、智能化浪潮正在重塑产业格局，数能融合已成为行业主流趋势。海博思创将坚持创新、深耕算电协同赛道，与各方伙伴合力推动新能源与数字经济融合发展，为行业绿色高质量发展贡献力量。

title: 超1GWh！阳光电源、阿特斯等5企披露储能订单及项目动态
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，阳光电源、阿特斯、华为数字能源、禾迈、国润储能等企业相继披露储能订单及项目动态，涉及柬埔寨、芬兰、澳大利亚、菲律宾、匈牙利及国内市场。
阳光电源获815.6MWh海外储能项目
近日，阳光电源在柬埔寨、芬兰相继披露储能项目进展，涉及储能规模合计超过815MWh，
在柬埔寨，阳光电源参与建设的EDC干丹斯登储能电站（GS79）已完成并网及全部验收测试。项目规模为108.4MW/215.6MWh，位于干丹省达克茂，采用集中式构网型储能技术，配置516台构网型PCS，具备黑启动及孤岛运行能力，可与当地水电、火电协同运行。
在芬兰，阳光电源与瑞士储能开发商Delta Capacity此前签署的1GWh储能框架协议已有600MWh进入项目实施阶段，涉及卡皮奥（Kärppiö）和AKKU One两座储能电站，规模均为125MW/300MWh。其中，卡皮奥项目已启动建设，计划2027年第四季度并网投产；AKKU One项目同样已开工。阳光电源将为两座项目提供储能系统技术，采用PowerTitan 2.0液冷储能系统。
阿特斯获200MWh澳大利亚储能订单
近日，阿特斯旗下e-STORAGE与瑞典可再生能源开发商OX2达成合作，将为澳大利亚新南威尔士州Muswellbrook光储一体化项目提供100MW/200MWh储能系统，负责设备交付、系统集成及并网调试等工作。项目将采用e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0储能电池舱及EQ-S能源管理系统。
Muswellbrook项目位于新南威尔士州Hunter-Central Coast可再生能源区，利用废弃煤矿用地建设，规划包含光伏和储能。项目已于2026年5月开工，储能系统计划于2027年Q3开始发货，预计于2028年Q3投入商业运营。
华为数字能源与Solarion签署储能合作
10月6日，华为数字能源菲律宾公司与Solarion Energy在马尼拉签署合作备忘录，双方将围绕漂浮光伏与光储一体化（PV+ESS）开展合作。
根据协议，华为数字能源将为Solarion的水上光伏项目提供逆变器、智能储能系统，以及水上抗腐蚀和运维等技术支持。
禾迈匈牙利落地32MWh光储项目
近日，禾迈携手GNX及EPC合作伙伴KKS，在匈牙利落地16个光储场站，合计部署32MWh储能。
项目分布于Kalocsa、Solt、Békés及Bácsalmás四个地区，每个场站配置500kW光伏电站及0.48MW/2MWh禾迈HoyUltra 2000M储能系统，项目已于2026年7月并网。
项目中，禾迈提供储能系统及技术支持，GNX负责SCADA监控系统与EMS联调，KKS承担现场施工及配套建设，三方共同完成设备部署、系统接入与调试，并提供本地化服务。
国润储能签订40MWh液流储能订单
9月30日，山西国润储能科技有限公司与内蒙古国天建设发展有限公司签订储能系统设备采购合同。
根据合同，国润储能将为国天能源二连浩特市200MW/800MWh电网侧独立新型储能电站项目中的10MW/40MWh全钒液流储能部分提供系统设备及配套技术服务。

title: 隆基绿能、晶科能源、阿特斯纪要：披露光伏储能业务进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，9月30日，阿特斯、晶科能源、隆基绿能三家光伏头部企业同步披露投资者关系活动记录表。
阿特斯：美国2GW高效HJT电池工厂投产
针对即将落地的能效强标，阿特斯表示，新规将抬升行业准入门槛，加速低效产能出清，行业竞争逻辑也将由单纯价格战转向效率、质量与可靠性综合比拼。
阿特斯披露，目前公司已实现高效N型产品量产销售，可以匹配新标准。现有N型电池产线具备技改升级潜力，后续将结合市场需求、投资回报节奏有序推进产线改造。
对于行业盈利修复节奏，阿特斯判断，伴随国内政策消化、海外需求回暖，明年全球光伏需求有望重回稳步增长。但短期行业供需仍处于再平衡过程，产能出清尚需时间，行业底部修复是渐进过程，公司目标在行业周期波动中维持相对稳健的盈利水平。
海外产能方面，阿特斯美国一期2GW高效HJT电池工厂7月正式投产，预计10月实现满产，二期扩产工作持续推进。美国制造业务由合资公司承接，架构满足当地补贴资格。工厂租赁业务上，组件工厂租金已于上半年确认，随着电池工厂量产，三季度起新增电池工厂租金收入，后续相关收益可参考定期报告披露。
储能业务方面，阿特斯认为海外大储竞争不只是价格竞争，核心在于全生命周期服务价值。依托垂直一体化端到端交付能力，阿特斯业务可以延伸至EPC、运维、资产管理，叠加海外本地化团队与服务网络，形成差异化竞争力。
此外，面对欧美储能进口政策趋严，相关细则尚未落地，公司将持续跟踪评估，依靠全球化布局、本地产能、合规调整来对冲地缘政策风险。
晶科能源：严打海外假冒组件
需求端，晶科能源判断，受136号文影响，国内市场出现阶段性扰动，但沙戈荒大基地、光伏治沙提供需求基本盘，分布式市场打开增量空间，全年国内组件需求落在200-230GW区间。
晶科表示，后续光伏将有望从传统并网周期逻辑转向场景化刚需驱动，海外市场在中东地缘、光储融合带动之下，预计明年全球光伏增速维持10%左右。
此外晶科也特别提到，近期海外市场不断出现冒用晶科品牌的假冒伪劣光伏组件，对品牌与国内光伏出海形象造成损害。晶科表示，公司已经联动海关、市场监管部门，对这类侵权产品开展查处行动。晶科唿吁行业共同抵制假冒侵权、低质低价的恶性竞争行为，维护中国光伏品牌海外口碑，推动行业高质量发展与反内卷落地。
隆基绿能：上半年储能签约订单已超3GWh
围绕行业反内卷进程，隆基绿能表示，国内已经陆续出台多项政策，引导行业重构竞争规则。2027年1月正式实施的光伏新国标覆盖全产业链环节，将显着抬升能效准入门槛，有望加快低效产能出清。
在当前价格承压的环境下，BC产品全球渗透率持续走高，分布式场景溢价表现尤为突出，隆基表示，BC产品也带动了公司经营修复，2026上半年综合毛利率实现同比转正。
据隆基披露，2026上半年其海外组件销量同比提升超26%，海外收入占比已经超过65%。分区域来看，美洲销量增长36%，欧洲销量增长34%，亚太销量增长20%，此外，在拉美、东南亚、阿联酋、巴基斯坦等市场也占据领先地位。
储能业务方面，隆基披露，上半年累计签约的储能订单量已经突破3GWh。围绕LONGi ONE全栈光储融合战略，隆基陆续推出多款储能产品，可适配大型地面储能、工商业储能以及离网微网等不同场景，多个海内外重点项目也已经落地推进。

title: 'Magnificent' Or 'Hideous?' People Are Divided On Jaguar's $130,000 EV
content:
'Magnificent' Or 'Hideous?' People Are Divided On Jaguar's $130,000 EV
Jaguar's first electric car post its controversial rebrand has arrived. It's just as polarizing as you'd expect.
- Jaguar unveiled the Type 01, the brand's first vehicle since its controversial rebrand two years ago.
- It's brutalist, boxy, and it's dividing the internet.
- Reactions online ranged from calling the $130,000 electric sedan "magnificent" to "hideous."
When Jaguar first launched the Type 00 Concept in December 2024, its brutalist styling and funky new badge had car enthusiasts foaming at the mouth. I'm not sure I've ever seen a concept car met with so much vitriol. Jaguar fans were livid that the brand was changing its iconic leaping cat logo for something far more minimalist and modern. They were also pretty pissed that Jag traded its typically gorgeous, sweeping, muscular designs—consider the legendary E-Type—for something so angular and square-jawed.
Now the concept has become reality. The new Jaguar Type 01 made its debut on Tuesday in New York, looking a whole lot like the off-the-wall concept car from close to two years ago. The web is pretty divided on whether this $130,000 electric sedan is a work of art—or a design that never should've left the drawing board.
Jaguar Type 01
Some People Love The Jaguar Type 01
A quick scan of reactions online shows that the Type 01 is actually seeing much more positivity than its predecessor did.
The reveal post on the Jaguar subreddit shows a very healthy mix of opinions, from people who love it, to those who hate it, to some people who might not be thrilled with this new direction from Jag but understand it.
There seem to be a surprising number of longtime Jaguar owners who actually seem to like both the car's design, and the idea of it. One Redditor who claims to have owned four Jags over the years said that while they don't love the interior, "The exterior, though... That's magnificent. It's the best looking EV I've seen. It's brutally handsome and purposeful."
One commenter on Jaguar's Instagram post about the Type 01 said that, like most Jags, it's ahead of its time. "It looks great as an EV. People will only start appreciating it after it’s discontinued," they wrote. "That’s typical for Jaguars: few people buy them while they're available, but once they're gone, everyone calls them a masterpiece."
There are a bunch of comments that hint at it looking like the '90s cartoon Batmobile, which is hard to argue with. It does indeed have an art-deco vibe you don't see in car design much these days. "The designer liked the Batmobile from Batman the Animated Series in the 1990’s," said one commenter on Auto Trader's YouTube video of the car.
Some People Hate It
One common opinion seems to be that the exterior looks good, with its ultra-boxy design, but that its interior is boring. And I couldn't agree more. The cabin is not only incredibly generic, but it looks claustrophobic.
Jaguar Type 01
"The interior doesn't really say 'Nice materials, pleasant place to be' does it?," one Redditor said. And they're right. With basic designs, very little trim, and a color palette like a Swedish crime-drama morgue, the Type 01 lacks the warmth Jags have always had.
That's not where the criticism ended, though. Haters are still very much active on the good ol' internet.
Below a post from one Redditor claiming to love the new Type 01, one commenter disagreed: "It’s an armored car with a fastback roof. Being inside it looks like an exercise in claustrophobia. Jaguars always gave that hemmed in feeling. But this looks uncomfortably extreme."
Jaguar Type 01
Even an Instagram post featuring Florence Pugh couldn't save the Type 01 from internet hate. "Put more people in front of the car or it’ll be still visible," one commenter said. "Goodness me it’s hideous, but I give you that, while the whole world told you don’t do it… you plowed on. That’s commitment. Self destructing… but still commitment."
The lack of classic Jaguar imagery, like the famous logo or hood leaper, still bothers many. One YouTube commenter posted about it on Jag's intro video: "The new logo makes Jag seem like a hipster stationary store that sells fresh cold pressed juices on the side. Wasn’t expecting them to still make cars. Who knew?"
One Redditor even used Jag's own famous catchphrase against it. "Christ on a Bicycle it's even more ugly and ungainly in motion. No Grace, No Space..." Hey, at least you know Jag isn't paying for social media bots to spam high praise. And if it is, it needs to get its money back.
Car magazines and online publications seem mostly pretty positive. And anyone who's interested in design seems to comment on what Jaguar calls the "Impossible Panel," which is the rear quarter panel that runs the length of the roofline. It's all one pressed aluminum panel that even Jaguar's software said was impossible to create. So a human with a pen and paper figured out how to do it, taught the computer a thing or two, and then Jag made it. That alone is a win in my book, even if I suspect that slightly denting it would total the car.
Overall, the reaction to the Type 01 seems far more positive than the reaction for the Type 00 concept. Fans are still upset about the logo change and the lack of leaper, but that's more to do with the brand itself and not the car. The reactions seem to be about a 50/50 split.
But then again, does it even matter? We're talking about low-volume, six-figure, ultra-luxury electric sedan. It doesn't need to appeal to everyone. And as Jaguar's top boss told us, the brand's most vocal haters probably aren't its customers anyway.

title: 1 In 4 New Mercedes Cars Sold Last Quarter Had A Plug
content:
Mercedes-Benz's EV sales skyrocketed in the third quarter, increasing 61% year-over-year.
Photo by:
Mercedes-Benz
4:32pm ET
Mercedes-Benz's overall sales are down, but that's only a snapshot of the story.
Its EV sales are up—way up—with 16.8% of passenger cars sold last quarter being fully electric.
And if that wasn't enough, Mercedes says that one in four cars sold had a charging port.
If you picked four brand new
Mercedes-Benz
cars sold between July and September at random, one of them would have a charging port.
Statistically speaking, of course, according to the automaker's global sales figures it shared on Wednesday. The company's latest delivery report shows a huge leap in its electrification efforts despite a down quarter for vehicle sales overall.
Photo by: Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
Mercedes says it sold 407,200 passenger cars globally last quarter, an 8% year-over-year drop. It largely blamed "challenging market conditions" in China for the decline, noting that its sales outside the country grew by 6%. Mercedes is far from the only European car company struggling in the world's biggest car market.
And yet, Mercedes says it sold 68,400 battery-electric vehicles last quarter, up 61% year-over-year and 29% from the second quarter. While the Mercedes pie got smaller, electric cars accounted for a record share of sales: 16.8%. That's an increase of 7.2 percentage points from the same quarter last year, Mercedes said. Add in plug-in hybrids, and 25% of the company's sales had a plug.
A lot of the heavy lifting is happening in Europe, with the main growth driver being the
electric GLC
. In Europe, nearly one-in-three cars Mercedes sold were fully electric thanks to sales that rose 78% year-on-year. Its electric variants of the CLA, GLA, GLB, and GLC are all sold out in the EU for the remainder of 2026.
Mercedes also says that the sales of its electric vans have increased, albeit not nearly as much as its passenger cars. About 11% of all vehicles sold across its van arm were electric, with Europe seeing as high as 15% share.

Will this electric wave hit the U.S.? Sales probably won't boom as much as they are in Europe. But the company does have a product offensive coming in the form of a whole bunch of new EVs, like the C-Class, GLC, and GLB.

title: How Tesla Is Pressuring European Regulators To Approve FSD
content:
How Tesla Is Pressuring European Regulators To Approve FSD
Elon Musk and his online army of fans said delayed FSD approval in Europe will cost lives. Scientists say they have no evidence to back those claims.
- A new investigation revealed how Tesla was pressuring European authorities to approve its Full-Self Driving (Supervised) system.
- The automaker reportedly presented flawed safety data, which had no independent third-party reviews, to safety regulators in Europe.
- Dozens of Tesla fans emailed regulators in Europe, claiming the authorities would be responsible for deaths if FSD roll out was delayed.
Tesla is pressuring European regulators to approve its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) advanced driver-assistance system, claiming that delays in rolling out FSD across the continent are costing lives. But scientists said there was no evidence to support that claim, according to an explosive new investigation by Reuters.
The outlet reviewed internal emails between Tesla and the Dutch regulator RDW, interviewed agency staffers, and sought the views of seven independent traffic-safety researchers, who identified significant flaws in safety reports Tesla submitted to European authorities. As part of its campaign, Tesla also rallied its fans to pressure European regulators to approve FSD speedily, according to the investigation.
FSD is kind of a big deal for Tesla right now. CEO Elon Musk has bet the company's future on autonomy, AI, and robotics unlocking its next phase of growth. A version of FSD also powers Tesla's Cybercab and Model Y robotaxis in the U.S., although the rollout of that has been notably slow. For Tesla's passenger cars, expanding FSD into Europe could also open up a huge new market worth millions in additional subscription revenue.
However, there are no publicly available independent or peer-reviewed studies showing that FSD is actually safer than a human driver. Which means authorities have to take Tesla's word for it before conducting their own tests.
According to the investigation, Tesla couldn't make a meaningful case for FSD’s improved safety over human drivers in an “Evidence Dashboard” submitted to European regulators in April. The data reportedly covered far fewer FSD test miles than the hundreds of millions of miles covered by Tesla drivers. Instead, Tesla pointed to “behavioral surrogates” such as horn use, sudden acceleration and deceleration, low turn-signal usage, and automatic emergency braking to demonstrate that FSD was safer.
Researchers told the outlet that some of these measures are poor proxies for actual crash risk. More importantly, none of the seven researchers interviewed by the outlet believed the study demonstrated that FSD prevents fatal crashes.
What’s perhaps more jarring is that internal emails showed Tesla repeatedly pushing the Dutch RDW to reduce the scope or intensity of its evaluation. After Tesla complained about the cost and extent of the review, an RDW staffer offered to discuss ways to “adjust or reduce” the required scrutiny, according to the report. That raises an obvious question: How independent can a safety assessment be if the company being evaluated is negotiating with the regulator over how rigorous that evaluation should be?
The RDW pushed back on that characterization. In response to the investigation, it said the exchanges with automakers were “a routine part of the assessment process and does not compromise the independence or thoroughness of our assessment.”
The Netherlands ultimately approved FSD, and several other countries followed, including Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, Lithuania, Czechia, Slovenia, and Croatia. France and Norway have taken a more cautious approach, while Germany appears to be on track to approve the system and has said it will advocate for EU-wide approval. Tesla also agreed to rename FSD “Tesla Assisted Driving” in Germany after authorities objected to the original name.
Tesla and Musk also used X, the social media platform the trillionaire CEO owns, to mobilize Tesla fans to pressure European regulators to approve FSD. Officials in Sweden and Norway received dozens of emails from Tesla fans asking for a speedy roll out of the technology in the countries, Reuters said. And in some emails, Tesla fans essentially told regulators that they would be responsible for deaths if FSD wasn't approved.
There are few things worth remembering here. Despite its misleading name, FSD isn't a fully autonomous driving system. Tesla says drivers remain responsible for crashes and must be ready to take over at all times. Users say the system has grown more capable over the years, as it gathers data from millions of Teslas on the road to train and improve its behavior. FSD can help Teslas steer, accelerate, brake and even park on their own, but the driver must continuously supervise.
As of the second quarter, Tesla said FSD had about 1.5 million subscribers worldwide, and many drivers appear to be happy with the system. But social media videos also regularly show FSD making questionable decisions, including flouting traffic rules, exceeding speed limits, and failing to recognize obstacles. Fatal crashes involving Teslas with FSD are also under investigation by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration here in the U.S.
Now an EU-wide vote on FSD is pending. The automaker needs support from 55% of member countries representing at least 65% of the bloc's population. What remains to be seen is whether European regulators independently scrutinize Tesla's claims before giving FSD the green light, or if the company's pressure campaign will make them buckle.

title: Tesla FSD Just Got The Green Light From Germany. But It Might Need A New Name
content:
Tesla FSD Just Got The Green Light From Germany. But It Might Need A New Name
German regulators support approving FSD for use throughout Europe. But they want Tesla to drop the "Full Self Driving" name.
- German regulators support EU-wide FSD approval with a speed offset capped at 10% above the limit.
- Tesla has offered to rename FSD “Tesla Assisted Driving” to make clear that drivers remain fully responsible, the statement claims.
- FSD is available in eight European countries, but EU-wide approval remains pending.
An October 6 statement from Germany’s Federal Ministry of Transport details September talks between Transport Minister Steffen Bilger and Tesla about the future of its "Full Self-Driving" technology suite. They reached agreement on technical and liability issues, prompting Bilger to push for timely EU-wide approval, the office announced.
The ministry says they agreed to allow speeds up to 10% above the limit, conceding that small excesses can sometimes smooth traffic flow. That tackles a major concern regulators had about excessive speeding, as the U.S. version of FSD includes a "Mad Max" mode that drives far over the speed limit in some circumstances.
Regulators were also concerned about the technology's long-controversial name. German regulators consider the FSD name to be misleading. Tesla will reportedly address this by calling it “Tesla Assisted Driving” instead, according to the German account of the discussion.
The ministry praises the system’s urban capabilities, too, noting that it rarely requires driver intervention to handle steering, acceleration, and braking. In general, though, the statement notes it is supporting European regulatory approval for the tech, not actually approving its current form.
FSD’s European rollout has been a patchwork, but approval in Germany might smooth adoption throughout the rest of the European Union. When it debuted in the Netherlands in April, the decision to allow it on public roads followed more than 18 months of assessment. Other countries can recognize that authorization individually, while EU-wide acceptance requires a separate vote by member states.
FSD also differs between the U.S. and Europe. One difference is how the speed offset feature works, and another is that the European version approved by Dutch regulators excludes the more aggressive ‘Mad Max’ driving mode available in the U.S.
Early FSD demonstrations in Europe have put it in a very positive light. It had no trouble navigating incredibly tight cobbled streets in downtown Aarhus, Denmark, where cyclists, pedestrians and cafe customers left precious little room for a car to pass. The drive showed impressive spatial judgment with only minor mistakes.
FSD passed 1.48 million subscribers in July. It introduced FSD subscriptions in the U.S. in July 2021, initially charging $199 a month alongside an outright purchase option. In February 2026, it dropped the upfront purchase for new U.S. customers, making FSD subscription-only. Today, it costs $99 a month in the U.S. and €99 in European markets.
Drivers already have access in the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Lithuania, Estonia, Slovenia, the Czech Republic, and Croatia. With Germany now supporting wider approval, how much longer will it take for FSD to spread to the rest of Europe?

title: The BMW iX3 M60 Gets 603 Horsepower And Yellow Lights
content:
BMW's new electric crossover is getting the M treatment thanks to a redesigned electric motor and other sporty upgrades.
Photo by:
3:07am ET
The BMW iX3 M60 packs 603 hp and hits 62 mph in 3.9 seconds, a full second quicker than the 50 xDrive.
Its 468-mile maximum WLTP range is only about 6% lower than the 50 xDrive’s.
The i3 M60 could be quicker still, while BMW’s more extreme four-motor M cars remain in development.
BMW has revealed the specifics of the M60 powertrain for
, and i3 electric models. It adds another 140 horsepower and extra torque over the 50 variant, but it still isn’t the most extreme electric BMW the M division has planned.
Announced alongside the new BMW iX4, the M60 becomes the most powerful iX3 variant revealed so far. Its two motors produce 603 horsepower and 645 pound-feet (875 Nm) of torque, enough for a claimed 0–62 mph (100 km/h) sprint of 3.9 seconds and a 149-mph top speed (240 km/h). That’s a full second quicker to 62 mph than the iX3 50 xDrive. The iX4 M60 has the same performance figures as the iX3.
Photo by: BMW
The extra power comes from a revised rear motor and a more powerful inverter, and it comes standard with adaptive M suspension, M-tuned variable-ratio steering, M Sport brakes, and an electronically controlled rear differential. BMW has also added front-end bracing and revised chassis tuning to make the extra power useful beyond straight-line driving.
The M60 also looks the part, with optional yellow daytime running lights, standard 21-inch M wheels, a black rear diffuser, and an M-specific roof spoiler with two aerodynamic blades.
Official U.S. market press materials say the iX3 M60 battery pack has more usable capacity: 112.2 kilowatt-hours versus 108.7 kWh in Europe. Whether that reflects different hardware, a different usable buffer, or a documentation error is unclear. It supports 400-kilowatt charging and has a WLTP range rating of 468 miles (754 km). That’s around 32 miles (51 km), or 6%, less than the 50 xDrive’s 500 miles (805 km).
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
BMW has also confirmed and shown the M60 version of
the i3 sedan
. With its lower and lighter body, it should be even quicker than the iX3. It’s around two-tenths quicker to sprint, so we can expect the i3 M60 to go from a standstill to 62 mph in around 3.7 seconds.
It’s worth noting that while these won’t be the highest-performance variants of their respective model lines, BMW considers them true M models. However, BMW plans more extreme, full-fat M versions, with crazy four-motor setups and a predisposition to go sideways.
The first of these true Neue Klasse-based M cars is the electric M3, which has already started
shedding camouflage
ahead of its full reveal sometime in 2027. An iX3 M is also in the works, but we haven’t seen spy photos of an iX4 M, though that doesn’t mean it isn't coming.
