title: Tesla drops 'Full Self-Driving' name in Europe after Germany pushback
content:
Tesla’s driver-assistance package is now called “Tesla Assisted Driving” in Europe. The company’s German website no longer mentions “Full Self-Driving,” and the old address now redirects to a new “Tesla Assisted Driving” page.
The rename follows Germany’s Transport Ministry calling the FSD name misleading, and it’s part of a deal that has Berlin backing Tesla’s push for EU-wide approval.
Germany wanted a new name, and Tesla offered one
In a statement published October 6, Germany’s Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV) wrote that the name of the system formerly sold as “FSD – Full Self-Driving Supervised” is misleading because the system doesn’t take over the full driving task. The driver has to pay attention at all times and remains fully responsible for the car.
Tesla offered to rename it “Tesla Assisted Driving” during talks with Transport Minister Steffen Bilger in September, according to the ministry.
They also agreed on speed. Germany says the system can go up to 10% over the speed limit, and it will back that position in the EU approval process. Tesla will need to change FSD to make that happen as it often goes way beyond 10% of the limit.
That’s a real concession from Tesla. Reuters reported that the version approved in the Netherlands allows speeds up to 50% over the detected limit.
In return, Bilger says he wants Tesla drivers to be able to use the system across the EU as quickly as possible. Musk thanked Germany on X with a “Danke schoen.”
Same pitch, new name
The rebrand is mostly a find-and-replace job. Not much else changed.
Tesla’s new German page is a translation of its US FSD page with the product name swapped out. It still says the car will drive you “almost anywhere” under your active supervision with minimal intervention. It still claims the system is “7x safer” than human drivers, a figure Tesla’s own footnote says is measured against the estimated US average. And it still ends with a section titled “Die Zukunft ist autonom” (“The future is autonomous”) that promotes Robotaxi and Cybercab.
Back in the US, tesla.com/fsd is still selling “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” for $99 a month.
Tesla’s page lists eight EU countries where the system is approved: the Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia and Croatia. Germany isn’t on the list yet. As we reported last month, the EU vote has slipped to December at the earliest, and bloc-wide approval needs 15 of 27 member states representing 65% of the EU population. France and Sweden have both raised concerns about speeding.
Electrek’s Take
This should be the name everywhere, and Tesla knows it.
“Full Self-Driving” was an aspiration when Tesla started selling it. In October 2016, Tesla said every car it was building had the hardware for full self-driving. At its Autonomy Day in April 2019, Musk said FSD would be “feature complete” by the end of that year and that Tesla would have over a million robotaxis on the road in 2020. You could argue the name was a bet on the future back then. A bad bet, but a bet.
Tesla has missed that target every single year since. It’s now been almost exactly 10 years since the 2016 announcement, and Tesla has admitted that the cars it sold as self-driving capable from 2016 to 2023 don’t have the hardware to do it. So at what point does an aspirational name become a false one? A California judge answered that last December, calling the name “unambiguously false and counterfactual.”

This is not "corporate puffery" - it's fraud, plain and simple. They lied about that demo drive and potentially millions of people bought a car believing it. Add to that that in many EU countries, people who paid for FSD still don't have TAD, and many of them can't get it without a hardware upgrade.

Now it dropped the name in Europe the moment a regulator it needed asked.

title: Tesla opens 14 Semi Megacharger stalls between Atlanta and Savannah
content:
Fred Lambert
| Oct 9 2026 - 6:13 am PT
Image: Tesla
Tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger sites in the Southeast: an 8-stall station just south of Atlanta and a 6-stall station outside Savannah, each rated for up to 1.2 MW per stall.
The Savannah site is also the first Megacharger at a Pilot truck stop, a rollout that was supposed to start this summer. Together, the two stations give the Tesla Semi its first public charging corridor outside California.
Two sites on one freight lane
The Tesla Semi account announced the openings on X on Thursday with a map of the route and a note that more Southeast sites are coming.
New Megacharger sites between Atlanta & Savannah now online
Many more Southeast sites coming soon
The Atlanta end is in Conley, Georgia, about 10 miles south of downtown near I-285 and I-675.
Tesla’s location page
lists it at 1820 Rock Cut Road with 8 Megachargers at up to 1.2 MW.
The other end is in Ellabell, about 20 miles west of Savannah on I-16.
Pilot confirmed
the same day that it’s the first site to come out of
its Megacharger deal with Tesla
: six stalls at Pilot #1390 on Interstate Exchange Way.
The two stations are roughly 220 miles apart on I-75 and I-16. That’s an easy one-way run for either version of the truck. Tesla rates the Semi at 325 miles for the Standard Range and 500 miles for the Long Range at 82,000 lbs, and it says a Megacharger puts back up to 60% of that in 30 minutes.
So a Standard Range truck can leave the Savannah port area, drive to Atlanta, charge during the driver’s break, and drive back. Without a charger at both ends, that 440-mile round trip is out of reach for the 325-mile truck.
Tesla’s aerial photo of one of the sites shows pull-through stalls in the middle of a truck yard, with a Semi tractor parked at one of them.
Pilot’s first Megacharger is a season late
When Pilot and Tesla announced their partnership in January, the first sites were due this summer. The first one opened on October 8.
Three more Pilot sites are getting ready: a Flying J in Tulare, California, which opens today, then a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, and a Pilot in North Las Vegas, Nevada. Nine others are under construction behind them, according to Pilot, and each site gets four to eight stalls.
That last one is in the same corner of the Las Vegas valley where
Tesla just filed a permit for a Semi service center
The state list changed, too. January’s announcement named California, Georgia, Nevada, New Mexico, and Texas. This one drops New Mexico and adds Indiana.
Shannon Sturgil, who runs alternative fuels at Pilot, said the first sites make fleet electrification “a more accessible option for long-haul transportation.”
Where the Megacharger network stands
Tesla’s public Megacharger list now shows three sites: Vernon and Bloomington in California, with six stalls each, and Conley. Ellabell isn’t on it yet. Count it, and that’s four customer-facing sites and 26 stalls.
That’s well short of the plan. Tesla’s Q4 2025 report showed about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026, and the company has said it wants 46 by early 2027. In February, it
put 66 Megacharger locations on its map
, four of them in Georgia.
And the trucks are coming. Tesla
launched volume production of the Semi
two weeks ago at a Nevada factory built for 50,000 trucks a year, days after it was named primary supplier on a 2,500-truck order.
Electrek’s Take
Megacharger deployment is likely a good way to track progress as it is essential to Tesla Semi deployment.
Savannah is one of the busiest container ports in the country, and a lot of that freight heads to Atlanta. If you run that lane, you can now buy a Semi and never put diesel in it. There’s also some irony in the location. Ellabell is home to Hyundai’s Metaplant, which
moves parts with hydrogen fuel cell trucks
. Tesla just put megawatt charging at a truck stop in the same town.
But Tesla is way behind its own schedule. It planned about 37 sites this year and it has four in the second week of October. Not great, but Tesla could still surprise us with an efficient rollout in the next two months.

title: Volkswagen's best-seller has gone electric, and it will replace the ID.4 and ID.5 [Images]
content:
Volkswagen
Volkswagen ID.4
Peter Johnson
| Oct 9 2026 - 7:14 am PT
Volkswagen unveiled the ID. Tiguan, an all-electric version of its best-selling vehicle. The ID. Tiguan will go on sale in early 2027, replacing
the ID.4
and ID.5 with up to 372 miles of range and plenty of other upgrades.
Meet the ID.4’s replacement, the Volkswagen ID. Tiguan
The ID.4 and ID.5 are on the way out as the new ID. Tiguan steps in. With over 950,000 models sold since they went on sale in 2021, the ID.4 and ID.5 have been at the core of Volkswagen’s EV lineup.
Following the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, the ID. Tiguan is the next to go on sale as a “True Volkswagen,” as the company calls it, bringing more than just a new name.
The ID. Tiguan is an upgrade in nearly every aspect over its predecessors, with a new design, updated tech, and refined interior.
Its “hallmark feature,” according to VW, is the completely redesigned exterior. Based on its new Pure Positive design language, the ID. Tiguan looks more like the gas-powered version with a traditional boxy SUV profile.
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen’s new electric SUV trades the ID.4’s aerodynamic design for a wide, chunky front end. It also drops the flush door handles in favor of traditional pull-style handles.
As a result, the new ID. Tiguan “looks like a vehicle from the premium segment,” Volkswagen claimed.
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan (Source: Volkswagen)
Inside, the ID. Tiguan features Volkswagen’s new interior design. The overhauled interior includes its new infotainment system, including a 10″ Digital Cockpit and 15″ center display screens. Plus, there’s an optional 12″ passenger screen.
One of the biggest changes inside is the return of physical buttons, which are now found below the center display and on the steering wheel.
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan interior (Source: Volkswagen)
There’s also a fun new “Retro” mode that transforms the Digital Cockpit with iconic blue-red instruments from the Golf IV.
Meanwhile, drivers can choose from six different classic VW models to display in a virtual “garage” on the infotainment screen: Golf I, Golf II Country, Golf IV, Tiguan I, Race Touareg, and Beetle.
The new Volkswagen ID. Tiguan will be available with two battery packs and three performance levels:
a rear-wheel-drive version with 140 kW (190 PS) and a 58 kWh battery
a rear-wheel-drive version with 210 kW (286 PS) and a 77 kWh battery
and a 220 kW (299 PS) 4MOTION all-wheel-drive variant, also with a 77 kWh battery.
Depending on the battery size and configuration, the ID. Tiguan offers a WLTP range of up to 372 miles (600 km), a “new benchmark” for Volkswagen’s electric SUVs in Europe.
With up to 295 hp (299 PS), the ID. Tiguan can tow up to 4,400 lbs (2,000 kg) with the 77 kWh battery. With the 58 kWh battery, towing capacity is around 4,000 lbs (1,800 kg).
Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Digital Cockpit with Retro Mode (Source: Volkswagen)
The ID. Tiguan also comes with standard one-pedal driving and Volkswagen’s new Connected Travel Assist. It also supports vehicle-to-load (V2L), enabling it to power external electronics like an electric grill or e-bike.
For an added cost, buyers can upgrade to electronically adjustable front seats with memory and ventilation, a premium Harmon Kardon sound system, and a panoramic sunroof.
Volkswagen will launch the ID. Tiguan in Germany and several other European markets on October 13, with prices starting at 42,695 euros ($47,800). It will be available in four trims: Trend, Life, Style, and R-Line.
After it goes on sale in Europe through early 2027, Volkswagen said the ID. Tiguan will replace the ID.4 in North America.
“The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars,” VW Brand CEO Thomas Shafer said, adding that “The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together.”
Prices and other details will be announced “in due course,” the company said. The current VW ID.4 uses an 82 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 291 miles in the RWD version. The AWD model offers around 263 miles.
Given the European model features nearly 25 miles (40 km) more WLTP range than the outgoing ID.4, the ID. Tiguan will likely offer over 300 miles on the EPA scale.
Volkswagen has not yet announced US prices. The outgoing ID.4 has a starting MSRP of around $45,000.

title: California Opens Up $28 Million In Funding For EV Chargers
content:
The state will cover up to 100% of eligible costs to install new public DC fast chargers, at up to $100,000 each.
Photo by:
Alpitronic
7:46am ET
California is spending at least $28 million to install new DC fast chargers.
The state’s Fast Charge California Project is subsidizing up to $100,000 per charging port.
Funding will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis.
California has kicked off another incentive round to install new public DC fast chargers for electric vehicles, and it’s offering up to $100,000 per charging port. The California Energy Commission’s
Fast Charge California Project
is offering at least $28 million as part of its second funding window, which runs through January 14, 2027.
The program is available statewide on a first-come, first-served basis, with projects located in disadvantaged and low-income communities being prioritized.
Incentives are capped at $55,000 per charging port for stalls that deliver between 150 kilowatts and 274.99 kilowatts, while ports that can deliver a minimum of 275 kW can receive a maximum of $100,000. The incentives cover the purchase and installation of eligible DC fast chargers, but only projects that are ready to build, including having an issued permit and final utility service design, will be approved.
Applicants must own the charging equipment, the chargers must be publicly available, and the sites must have a minimum of 50% CCS connectors. For this funding round, charging hubs, hotels, and business districts are no longer eligible. At the same time, eligible locations may include businesses, public facilities, high-traffic destinations, and sites along major travel routes.
“California needs reliable fast charging in communities across the state to support the growing number of electric vehicles on the road,” said Spencer Reeder, director of CEC’s Fuels and Transportation Division. “This next round of Fast Charge California Project funding will help move ready-to-build projects forward, expand access to public charging, and put state investments to work in communities that have historically had fewer charging options.”
The latest round of funding comes after the Fast Charge California Project’s 2026 round, which awarded $56.9 million in EV charging incentives, funding over 1,200 ready-to-build fast-charging ports.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
A third funding window will run from February 24 through May 27, 2027, but incentives will be capped at $55,000 per charging port.
The funding campaign is part of the California Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Project (CALeVIP), the largest EV charging incentive initiative in the United States. Since its introduction in 2017, the program has supported 10,200 charger installations across California.

title: Hyundai’s Next Two EVs Could Be A Little More Normal
content:
Two reported electric SUVs could bring more familiar shapes and family-friendly packaging to Hyundai’s already large electric lineup.
Photo by:
8:51am ET
Hyundai reportedly plans two boxier electric SUVs, potentially named Ioniq 4 and Ioniq 7.
The smaller SUV could complement the Ioniq 3, while the larger model would slot between the Ioniq 5 and 9.
Neither model is confirmed for America, where Hyundai’s EV lineup has narrowed.
Hyundai’s electric cars rarely look like they were designed by a committee determined not to offend anyone—they seem deliberately polarizing. The Ioniq 5 that started this trend still looks like a concept car that escaped into production, while the Ioniq 6 takes a streamlined sedan idea to its logical, slightly odd-looking conclusion.
Their willingness to experiment is part of what draws buyers in. But it may also be driving some away, who just want a reasonably sized electric SUV with room for everyone’s stuff.
According to
Auto Express
, Hyundai reportedly has two more EVs coming, and they might be a lot boxier and more conventional than what it currently offers. The company reportedly plans to introduce small and midsize electric SUVs within the next 12 to 18 months. The publication expects them to wear Ioniq 4 and Ioniq 7 badges, although neither name is confirmed.
Hyundai Ioniq 3
Photo by: Hyundai
The Hyundai electric lineup already covers plenty of ground. Its European range stretches from
the tiny Inster
through the Kona Electric and new
, then on to the Ioniq 5, Ioniq 6 and three-row Ioniq 9.
The automaker has likely seen an opportunity to offer two slightly more traditional choices within that spread; it isn't really conquering any new size brackets it doesn’t already cover. Hyundai’s latest EV, the Ioniq 3, illustrates the same point because it’s only marginally smaller than the familiar Kona, yet it offers more distinctive styling and undercuts it on price.
The proposed Ioniq 4 would offer a more upright alternative with a very similar footprint, broadly comparable in size to Kia’s EV3. This means a boxier shape with more interior space while possibly sharing the Ioniq 3’s 42- and 61-kilowatt-hour battery and the same basic 400-volt architecture.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The larger SUV would address a different shopping dilemma. We’ve praised the Ioniq 9’s ability to carry a family in comfort, but not everyone needs a vehicle that large or expensive. The prospective Ioniq 7 would sit between the Ioniq 5 and the Ioniq 9, reportedly closer in size to the latter, using the same
800-volt platform
but with a more upright body.
In the U.S., Hyundai’s EV selection is considerably narrower. The Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 9 do most of the heavy lifting, with the 5 N offering a very specific experience. The Kona Electric is
skipping the 2026 model year
, while the regular
Ioniq 6 has been dropped
, leaving just the high-performance N version to carry the sedan’s flag.
That gives a smaller electric SUV a potential opening, provided Hyundai can price it far enough below the Ioniq 5 to make the choice meaningful. Nothing confirms an American launch for the proposed Ioniq 4 or 7 yet, though both would have plausible roles to play.

title: Nissan's New Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Is Part Of A Much Bigger China Trend
content:
Nissan's New Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Is Part Of A Much Bigger China Trend
The Nissan Frontier Pro is made and developed in China, but this plug-in hybrid pickup truck is going global.
- The Nissan Navara Pro/Frontier Pro is a PHEV mid-sized pickup truck made in China.
- It's heading to markets like Mexico and Australia.
- It shows that China's export boom isn't all about Chinese brands.
Meet the Nissan Frontier Pro. On Thursday, the automaker said it's bringing this midsize plug-in hybrid pickup to global markets like Mexico and Australia. But it's more than just another electrified vehicle Americans can't have. Developed and made in China, the truck shows that the country's massive export push isn't just coming from homegrown brands like BYD and Geely.
Designed for China by Zhengzhou Nissan, the automaker's joint venture with China's Dongfeng, the Frontier Pro comes with a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine and an electric motor mounted in the transmission that produces 402 horsepower. A 33-kilowatt-hour battery feeds that electric motor. Those are the specs for the Chinese market, where the Frontier Pro is already sold. Nissan hasn't shared details for markets outside of China yet.
Nissan said the truck will launch in Mexico this month, followed by other Latin American markets later this year. In 2027, it'll arrive in Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines, and the Middle East as the Navara Pro, the company said.
It's part of a trend of non-Chinese automakers exporting their made-in-China cars abroad.
In Mexico, much of Chevrolet’s lineup is actually rebranded Chinese cars. For example, the Chevrolet Groove is a rebadged Wuling Xingchi, a car made by GM’s joint venture with SAIC and Wuling. Same with the Chevrolet Captiva EV, which is a rebranded Wuling Starlight S. Mazda’s Changan-made EZ-60 EV is making inroads in Europe and Asia, and so is Toyota’s GAC-made bZ3 crossover.
Nissan itself also announced its intention to bring the N7 EV sedan to markets outside of China. On Thursday, it said the Frontier Pro's launch abroad highlighted "China's growing role as an innovation and export hub" for the company. Meanwhile, Volkswagen Group CEO Oliver Blume has said the company could start importing some China-built cars to Europe.
If you’re outside of the U.S., it isn't uncommon to find a new car from a familiar brand that may have ties back to China.
What's also notable is that China is building vehicle types that are specifically palatable outside of the country. Sure, the Frontier Pro is sold in China, but pickup trucks aren't big sellers there because of laws that make it hard to drive one daily in any Chinese city. However, Chinese brands seem willing to meet other markets where they are. The Navara Pro PHEV is the latest in the line of PHEV pickup truck models introduced to other markets, following the Chery Stockman and BYD Shark.
There’s pretty much no chance this Nissan PHEV truck will ever make it to the U.S., for several reasons. This truck is subject to extremely high import tariffs on Chinese vehicles and non-US-made trucks. Since it's at least partially designed by Nissan’s Chinese partner, it likely would be subject to the ban on Chinese connected cars, too.
That doesn’t mean we won’t get some sort of electrified Nissan truck here in the U.S., though. Recently, Nissan said it wants hybrids to become the dominant powertrain for its lineup in North America by 2030, and the new Rogue Hybrid kicks that off. Maybe that means an electrified Nissan pickup is in the works too.

title: Polestar Sales Are Booming. Thank The Country That Just Banned It
content:
American buyers helped Polestar post record sales. But its shrinking business elsewhere shows why replacing the U.S. won’t be easy.
Photo by:
Mack Hogan/InsideEVs
3:37pm ET
Polestar’s global Q3 sales rose 1%, but fell 8% excluding the United States.
U.S. sales more than doubled as Polestar sold inventory ahead of its model-year 2027 ban.
New models must help replace American sales, while profitability remains a separate challenge.
Polestar just recorded its strongest third quarter ever. That’s great news for the electric automaker, but the awkward part is where the growth came from: the country that has effectively barred it from selling cars.
The EV maker’s worldwide sales edged up 1% year over year in Q3, but remove the United States, and they fell 8%. America is helping Polestar keep its numbers positive as the company prepares for a future without access to it.
Third-quarter deliveries reached an estimated 14,371 vehicles, up from 14,222 a year earlier. Outside the U.S., volume fell to 12,211 from 13,256. Subtracting those figures, American sales came to 2,160 vehicles, up from 966—an increase of about 124%. Those additional 1,194 deliveries more than offset the 1,045-car decline elsewhere.
Polestar 4 and Polestar 4 SUV
Photo by: Polestar
Global sales in the first nine months of 2026 reached a record 44,790, up 0.6% from 44,511. Excluding America, they fell 0.5% to 40,773 from 40,968. That implies U.S. sales of 4,017 versus 3,543, up around 13%.
In June, Polestar was shut out of selling cars in the United States under a new Department of Commerce rule prohibiting certain Chinese connectivity and driver-assistance technology. While Volvo, which also falls under the Geely Group umbrella, was granted an exemption, Polestar's effort to get around the ban was denied.
In the wake of the decision, Polestar deeply discounted its cars to clear out inventory.
Polestar 4 discounts reached $25,000
. There were great deals to be had on Polestar 3s too. That may be behind the stronger sales, but the Polestar did not share a model-by-model breakdown for the U.S. So this was more of a sugar high than a sign of sustainable growth for Polestar, which posted around $1 billion in operating losses in 2025 despite record sales of 60,119 cars.
Polestar will continue selling existing inventory and says it will maintain customer service even once it can no longer sell new cars. In August, the manufacturer said
it was blindsided by the decision and still didn't quite understand
why Volvo was treated differently, despite the Polestar 3 and Volvo EX90 sharing the same South Carolina assembly line.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Elsewhere in the world, the lineup is expanding beyond the Polestar 2 fastback, 3 SUV and original 4 crossover. Customer deliveries of the Polestar 5 grand tourer have begun. The new Polestar 4 SUV adds a more
practical (distinctly wagon-like) body
, more cargo space, and a view out the back, with shipments scheduled for the fourth quarter.
A replacement Polestar 2 will arrive in 2027
, followed by
the compact Polestar 7
in 2028. The Polestar 6 roadster remains planned. The bigger lineup could help Polestar attract more buyers and build to long-term sustainability. It'll just have to do that without the U.S.

title: Rivian EVs Are Becoming Ghostbusters This Halloween
content:
Rivian EVs Are Becoming Ghostbusters This Halloween
All Rivian EVs are in for a surprise software update. A special R1 and Bill Murray are also part of the story.
- Rivian is bringing the Ghostbusters universe to its EVs for Halloween.
- All R1 and R2 models will get a software update that adds visual and sound effects inspired by the 1980s classic.
- The startup also built a full-scale R1S Ecto-1 replica and brought in Bill Murray to tie it all together.
Rivian has a bit of history when it comes to fun, Halloween-inspired software updates for its electric cars, but this year, the California startup is really going above and beyond.
The company partnered with Sony Pictures to bring the Ghostbusters universe to all R1 and R2 EVs on the road, topping it all off with a full-on R1S Ecto-1 replica and a promo video starring none other than Bill Murray, who starred as Dr. Peter Venkman in the original Ghostbusters movie from 1984.
For Rivian owners, the Halloween software update comes with several sound and visual effects that can be activated from inside the car or from the Rivian smartphone app. The Lights & Sounds option pairs custom exterior LED sequences with Ghostbusters-inspired soundscapes. Drivers can choose between Ecto-1, Proton Pack, Slimer, Ghost Trap, Peter Venkman, or Random. In true Halloween spirit, owners can also enable Motion Mode, which lets the vehicle react with sounds and lights when someone walks by.
Custom lock sounds are also part of the pack. First-generation R1 owners can swap the stock sound to Ecto-1, while R1 Gen 2 and R2 drivers can choose between Ecto-1, Proton Pack, or Chant.
The interior displays also get a Ghostbusters makeover. Opening the Ghostbusters in-vehicle app while parked pulls up a retro command console with a big red toggle switch that controls the whole experience, syncing interior lighting, themed audio, and exterior displays.
Flipping the Trick or Treat Mode on takes over the driver and rear displays and starts playing the Ghostbusters theme song. On the main infotainment display, the Scavenger Hunt add-on hides interactive cue cards with hidden characters inside familiar screens like Drive Modes, Gear Guard, and the Energy app. When players discover a Ghost Guard or a Slimer, it triggers a unique animation and audio.
While parked, passengers can also play ‘Mallow Mash on the center screen, where they pop Mini-Pufts marshmallow men against the clock. The Rivian Assistant voice also picks up an eerie tone for the season, and drivers can ask it to run an exterior light show, read a hunt clue, or play a sound effect.
Gallery: Rivian Halloween Ecto-R1
Paying homage to the 1984 classic is a custom-made Rivian R1S SUV inspired by the white Ecto-1 station wagon that actors used to hunt down ghosts in the movie. The build comes with a roof rack that packs all of the accessories needed to catch fridge-munching baddies: sirens, a radar dish, and the original emergency lights from the movie car, which were sourced and restored for this project.
The electric SUV rides on 22-inch wheels with white covers, and there’s a No-Ghost logo on the hood and front doors.
To get the special sound and visual effects, Rivian owners need to make sure their vehicle software and mobile app are up to date (R2 needs version 2026.36.40, while R1 needs 2026.36.0). When updated, the driver display will ask if you’d like to “hunt some ghosts.” Halloween Mode features will be live from October 9 through November 2, 2026.
Fans can enjoy the full-scale Rivian Ecto-R1 homage builds at several events across the country. The startup’s retail spaces in Laguna Beach, Austin, Miami Brickell, San Francisco, and New York City Meatpacking District are throwing local parties with limited-edition merchandise and themed refreshments.

title: Rivian R2's Ventilated Seats Just Got Downgraded. Buyers Are Outraged
content:
New Rivian R2s no longer push air through their seat backs. Some buyers say the change is enough for them to cancel their orders.
Photo by:
Patrick George
1:51pm ET
Rivian has quietly changed how the ventilated seats work in the R2.
Air no longer circulates in the seatback. Rivian says this is due to excessive cabin noise.
The internet has exploded over the small change and buyers are even cancelling their orders.
Rivian quietly changed how the ventilated seats work in the R2. The company's fans and would-be buyers aren't happy about it.
To be clear, the ventilated seat feature isn't completely gone. Rather, Rivian has removed the ability for the seat to push air through the seat back and instead focused all of the airflow through the base of the seat. News of the change bubbled up on forums and was also reported on by the
RivianTrackr
Rivian forums, subreddits, and Facebook groups have exploded with intense
criticism
over the decision, with some users even going as far to
cancel their preorders
and threatening to
file credit card chargebacks
on non-refundable order fees. The EV startup has built up an unusually loyal fanbase of people who dig its outdoorsy image and friendlier-than-Tesla vibes. The seat-ventilation dustup has many of those same fans feeling played.
Photo by: Rivian
"The strong ventilation was one of the best features of the R2," said one
Redditor
, echoing what our very own
Mack Hogan
shared about his experience with the R2's powerful ventilated seats. "Quietly breaking that functionality and pretending it’s not a big deal is a really bad look."
"Not gonna lie, this one pisses me off,"
another. "If you're going to take something away, do the right thing and tell people. I want to know why they took it out and why they aren't compensating people that are getting less of a car than what they test drove."
"I placed my order a week ago and I'm pretty pissed about it. You mean to tell me the seats in my wife's Mach E are going to be miles better than what Rivian can put out?," another
. "Very annoying."
A not insignificant number of commenters said the switch was enough for them to cancel their R2 preorders. It turns out many car buyers—or at least the most vocal ones—care a whole lot about having their backs cooled, and not just their rear ends.
"I’m also walking away," one commenter
. "Will now need to go to the drawing board and find another car that has the seat cooling cause I’m in freaking hot as hell TX. This is extremely annoying."
Some would-be buyers were mostly peeved because of the
lack of transparency
over why the feature was removed. A Rivian spokesperson told InsideEVs the move was a response to excessive cabin noise from the old system.
"R2 ventilated seats are designed to deliver active airflow through the seat cushion, where occupants retain the most heat," the spokesperson said. "Because the seat back ventilation generated excessive cabin noise, we streamlined the system. R2 seat heating is unchanged."
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
It's not clear how exactly Rivian streamlined the system. Rivian hasn't said whether R2s on the road will continue operating as they did when owners purchased them (with the "noisy" ventilation), or whether software will eventually change that. We asked Rivian about this and will update this story if we hear more.
There are rumors online that Rivian has removed the actual hardware responsible for providing the circulation, though that remains unconfirmed. Likewise, some commenters
they were told that this is a
supplier
constraint, but we weren't able to verify that.
This small electric fan created an impressively large debacle for Rivian. But for people who live in climates with sweltering summers, cool seats can be the difference between a drenched, sticky back and a comfortable commute. For others, it was less about the seats themselves and more about wanting to support a brand without getting burned.
"I don't care for ventilated seats," one Redditor
. But I am really concerned about the lack of transparency. Now I have to worry about other features being stealth nerfed too."

title: Tesla Is Building Megachargers For Semis Where Truckers Already Stop
content:
Tesla Is Building Megachargers For Semis Where Truckers Already Stop
Pilot’s first Megacharger station is already open for business in Georgia, and a dozen more are under construction.
- Pilot and Tesla are building over a dozen megawatt-capable charging stations across the U.S.
- The stations feature four to eight Tesla Megachargers, designed specifically for the Semi electric truck.
- The first Tesla Megacharger station at a Pilot Travel Center is already online.
Pilot, the largest travel center network in North America, and Tesla are building over a dozen high-powered charging stations for the electric Tesla Semi along major freight corridors in the United States.
The first Tesla Megacharger station is already operational at a Pilot location in Ellabell, Georgia, with a dozen more under construction across the country. The Ellabell Megacharger station features six stalls, each capable of delivering up to 1.2 megawatts of power to a Tesla Semi. Drivers need to back up into the charging bay, as the site’s design doesn’t allow for pull-through charging.
Earlier this week, Tesla energized another Semi station in Conley, Georgia, but it isn't affiliated with Pilot. This site has pull-through stalls.
Pilot’s travel centers, which are popular stops for truckers, will get between four and eight Megachargers. The stations will be built at select locations along I-5, I-10, and other major freight corridors across California, Indiana, Nevada, and Texas.
“Pilot is proud to bring heavy-duty charging directly to key trucking routes and pair it with the services and amenities drivers rely on,” said Shannon Sturgil, senior vice president of alternative fuels at Pilot. “With these initial locations, we’re making fleet electrification a more accessible option for long-haul transportation and are excited to continue working with Tesla to move at the pace and preference of our customers.”
The second Pilot-Tesla Semi charging station will go online today at the Flying J location on E. Paige Ave. in Tulare, California. Another Flying J in Fort Stockton will get a Megacharger station soon, followed by a Pilot Travel Center in North Las Vegas. Another nine sites are actively under construction, but their locations haven’t been revealed yet.
Pilot’s travel centers have plenty of amenities, including quick service restaurants. That’s great news for electric truck drivers, who can take a break while their rig is charging. In the Tesla Semi’s case, a 30-minute top-up will boost the state of charge by 60%.
Besides welcoming heavy-duty charging stations for Tesla Semis, Pilot already has over 1,000 fast-charging stalls for regular EVs. The company partnered with General Motors and EVgo, and has so far energized 1,300 stalls at 300 locations throughout the country, with more on the way. In the near future, no fewer than 2,000 chargers will be available across 500 Pilot travel centers.

title: Tesla Supplier Reports Record Earnings From EV And Energy Storage Batteries
content:
Tesla Supplier Reports Record Earnings From EV And Energy Storage Batteries
Europe's EV boom and a bet on energy storage batteries in the U.S. spurred record sales for LG Energy Solution in Q3.
- LG Energy Solution slowed down its electric vehicle battery production in North America due to low demand.
- Now losses related to that are being offset by strong growth in energy storage batteries for data centers and grid upgrades.
- Production credits in the U.S. and Europe's record EV sales are also helping the battery maker's bottom line.
Battery giant LG Energy Solution posted record quarterly earnings Thursday thanks to its burgeoning energy storage business in the U.S. and growing electric vehicle sales in Europe, the company said in a regulatory filing in South Korea.
It’s been a disruptive couple of years for battery makers in North America, as they’ve had to roll back their EV ambitions due to slower-than-expected sales. Many have offset those losses by tapping into a growing market for stationary energy storage batteries, which are in high demand due to power hungry AI data centers and grid upgrades.
Now the bet on stationary storage has started paying off for LGES, while strong plug-in vehicle sales in Europe have buoyed the company’s EV-battery business. Per preliminary results, the company’s third quarter revenue grew 59% year-over-year to $7.21 billion, and its operating profit grew 25% to $565 million. It will disclose the full official results in November.
LGES cylindrical battery cells.
According to The Korea Herald, the battery company’s plant in Poland is seeing strong demand from Volkswagen and Renault’s growing EV sales in Europe. Here in the U.S., growth in AI data centers has spurred demand for its energy storage system (ESS) batteries, which it now produces locally at multiple U.S. plants.
The surge in earnings can also be attributed to battery-manufacturing credits the company received through the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and compensation from automakers for failing to meet minimum EV battery purchase requirements, according to Reuters.
While the Trump administration’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act wiped out many pro-climate policies enacted under the Biden administration, including axing the federal tax credit and rolling back fuel economy rules, it largely preserved the Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production tax credits for domestic battery manufacturing. Those remain available through 2032.
LGES is also bringing more of its battery supply chain to North America. The company signed a multi-year offtake agreement with Canada’s Elevra Lithium on Thursday. As a part of that deal, LGES will receive 240,000 metric tonnes of raw lithium concentrate from Elevra’s mine in Quebec.
In August, the company also opened its $2 billion gigafactory in Lansing, Michigan—which InsideEVs had the chance to tour in person—where it is producing energy storage lithium-iron-phosphate batteries for Tesla and nickel-manganese-cobalt EV batteries for Toyota.

title: The 2027 Chevy Bolt Can Drive Farther Than You Think At 60 MPH
content:
The 2027 Chevy Bolt Can Drive Farther Than You Think At 60 MPH
In a highway range test, the Bolt was far more efficient at 60 mph than it was at 70 mph.
- YouTuber Tom Moloughney drove the 2027 Chevy Bolt at a steady 60 mph to see how far it could go.
- The results show that slowing down can have a profound impact on range.
- He ran the same test at 70 mph and 80 mph, and we compare the numbers here.
When every other car is passing you like you're standing still, doing 60 mph on the highway can feel like a crawl. But if you're driving an EV, sticking to that slow speed can have a big enough range payoff to make the slog worthwhile. And who cares if other drivers think you're a senior citizen? You'll be laughing all the way to the next charging stop, which could be over 60 miles farther away than if you drove like someone with somewhere to be.
In a new highway range test, State of Charge host Tom Moloughey drives his brand-new 2027 Chevrolet Bolt on the New Jersey Turnpike from 100-0% at a steady 60 mph to see what it can do. More importantly, he recently did the same test at 70 mph and 80 mph. So he has enough data to determine just how much more efficient the Bolt is at lower speed. The difference is pretty massive.
Moloughney did the test on a sunny morning, with ambient temps between 52-63 degrees Fahrenheit—so just about perfect. There was also very little traffic, so he could easily maintain his 60 mph. Using Super Cruise for much of the way, he was able to drive 280.3 miles on a full charge of the Bolt's 65 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery. That means he blew past the EPA's claimed highway range of 232 miles by almost 50 miles. That also nearly reached the EPA's claimed city range of 294 miles. (The Bolt's combined figure is 262 miles.)
At 60 mph, the Bolt was able to achieve an average efficiency of 4.1 miles-per-kWh. That's pretty dang good for the highway.
What about at 70 mph? Upping the speed by 10 mph dropped the Bolt's total range to 243.1 miles, which can be a huge difference if you're using your last bit of juice to find a charger. That's an average consumption of 3.6 miles/kWh.
At 80 mph, things dropped significantly, but not as far as the drop from 60-70 mph. The Bolt only managed 219.3 miles at 80 mph, at 3.2 miles/kWh. The temps were warmer in the 70 mph and 80 mph tests, but not by enough to drastically change the outcomes.
So there you have it. In the Bolt at least, cutting your speed by 20 mph can increase highway range by just about 60 miles. Going 60 instead of 70 mph boosts it by about 40 miles. You just might have to be okay with driving like a grandpa.

title: The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Looks Like A Big Upgrade Over The ID.4
content:
The Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Looks Like A Big Upgrade Over The ID.4
This new crossover has more buttons, one-pedal driving, and even a frunk.
- Volkswagen on Friday unveiled the ID. Tiguan, its replacement for the ID.4.
- It serves up upgrades in key areas, including better software and a frunk, something the old ID.4 did not have.
- It goes on sale in Europe in early 2027, and will hit the U.S. sometime after that.
Goodbye, ID.4. Volkswagen is replacing its compact EV crossover with this, the ID. Tiguan. It’s about the same size as the old car, but with a more familiar name and some big changes that should make it a much better electric vehicle.
The ID.4 first went on sale in 2021. It was known for being a spacious EV and a good value, especially since at one point it was made in the U.S. and qualified for the EV tax credit. But over its run, people also complained about some key features, like the car’s software and some elements of the driving experience.
Gallery: Volkswagen ID. Tiguan (2027)
Earlier this year, VW announced that it was stopping production of the EV in the U.S. in favor of gas vehicles, leaving it without a mainstream electric offering in this market. Now the ID. Tiguan is on the way to succeed the ID.4 (and the ID.5 in markets where that's sold). And it looks like Volkswagen has taken some of the criticism to heart.
For starters, the ID. Tiguan has an upgraded infotainment and software stack. There are up to three screens now, including one directly in front of the passenger for apps and entertainment. The driver’s display and center screen are bigger and can be switched to a special “retro” mode that has stylized virtual gauge clusters from old Volkswagen models from the past. It’s the same system we’ve seen on the new ID. Polo.
Oh, and Volkswagen highlights that there are many more actual buttons now. There are new physical button pads on the steering wheel, as well as a row of buttons just below the main infotainment screen. A volume knob is back, right on the center console. That’s a big improvement over the annoying, touch-sensitive sliders dating back to the ID.4’s launch. The infamous push-for-rear window switches are gone, replaced with four traditional ones.
The ID. Tiguan also gets handy EV-specific features the ID.4 never had. The crossover gains a frunk—albeit a tiny one with just 1.1 cubic feet of storage space. It gets one-pedal driving. And VW has added vehicle-to-load functionality, accessed via an outlet adapter that plugs into the charging port.
Stylistically, the ID. Tiguan comes off like a more mature version of the ID.4. The hood visually looks longer and more upright, while the side surfacing gives off a more expensive vibe. The interior looks to be a real upgrade, with Alcantara or suede surfaces on the R-line model.
On Friday, Volkswagen only released the European-spec ID. Tiguan deets. Powertrains are similar to what you'd find in the old ID.4; the ID. Tiguan is available in rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive, with two different battery sizes.
The smaller 58 kWh battery produces 187 horsepower and is RWD only. The larger 77 kWh pack comes with either 282 horsepower in RWD form or 294 horsepower in AWD 4Motion trim. Maximum range is advertised at up to 600 kilometers (372 miles) for the 77 kWh model in RWD trim, based on the WLTP cycle. That's 26 km more than ID.4's rating in Europe, suggesting the U.S. model might get a range boost too.
Pricing starts at about 42,695 euros (about $49,000), which is roughly the same as what the current ID.4 costs in many European markets.
And yes, the ID. Tiguan is coming to the U.S. market too, a Volkswagen spokesperson said. The European version of the ID. Tiguan will launch in early 2027. Volkswagen told us that it will share U.S.-specific details sometime after that.

title: VW ID.4 Recalled Over Fire Risk, Owners Told Not To Charge Past 80%
content:
VW ID.4 Recalled Over Fire Risk, Owners Told Not To Charge Past 80%
An issue with certain batteries can cause a fire while charging above 80%, according to a recall notice.
Volkswagen is recalling 22,524 ID.4s over the potential for battery fires, according to recall documents filed this month with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
Until it comes up with a fix for the issue, VW is advising owners to not charge their car past 80%, as it says incidents can happen above that state of charge. VW estimates that 0.1% of the recalled cars, which include 2023-2026 models, are actually affected.
"The root cause is unknown, however in certain high-voltage batteries within the affected vehicle
population, certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation within the high-voltage battery," VW said in a filing.
Volkswagen says it still isn't sure exactly what is happening to the batteries, which are supplied by SK. It made the call to issue a recall on September 23, 2026, after 22 different instances from U.S. customers that occurred between January 18, 2024 and August 7, 2026.
While no permanent solution is available, VW does have a couple of temporary ones. The first one is simple: Post-It notes. OK, so not exactly Post-Its, but warning stickers to be placed in certain areas of the car to remind owners not to charge past 80%. I imagine they'll be on the dashboard and under the charge port flap. VW also said that "Depending on the vehicle configuration and online connectivity, some vehicles may be configured to limit the maximum state of charge of the high-voltage battery to 80 percent," suggesting an over-the-air update may be in the cards.

title: VW’s Electric Polo GTI Just Got Faster. Thank The Customers
content:
The ID. Polo GTI opens for orders with revised specs and a price slightly higher than previously advertised.
Photo by:
Volkswagen
5:09am ET
Customer feedback prompted VW to raise the ID. Polo GTI’s top speed is 118 mph.
German pricing starts at €39,995, with adaptive dampers and a limited-slip differential standard.
A hotter Clubsport could bring around 282 hp and simulated gears, but its specs remain unconfirmed.
Volkswagen’s first electric GTI has picked up some extra speed before reaching customers. Apparently, potential buyers had a say in how fast it should go.
The ID. Polo GTI
now tops out at 118 mph (190 km/h), up from the 109 mph (175 km/h) we reported previously. Volkswagen attributes the new maximum to customer feedback.
Pre-sales opened on October 7, with German pricing starting at €39,995 ($44,900), slightly higher than the earlier indication that it would start just under €39,000. Maximum WLTP range also edges up from 424 to 431 kilometers, or around 268 miles.
There’s more detail on the equipment, too. Adaptive dampers for the lower suspension and progressive variable-ratio steering are standard. A steering wheel-mounted GTI button adjusts the drive, steering, suspension, sound, and instrument cluster graphics together.
Gallery: Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI 2026
Optional Connected Travel Assist can recognize red lights and automatically stop the car when adaptive cruise control is enabled. The options list also includes massaging front seats, a panoramic roof, and 425-watt Harman Kardon audio.
VW is also offering a specially developed performance tire for the GTI’s 19-inch wheels. The release doesn’t name the supplier or quantify the improvement, but it’s an option worth watching because it promises extra grip and potentially higher cornering speeds.
The specs of the single front-mounted electric motors remain unchanged. It makes 223 horsepower and 214 pound-feet of torque channeled to the wheels through an electronically controlled limited-slip differential, and draws from a 52-kilowatt-hour usable battery.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The 0–62 mph (100 km/h) sprint happens in 6.8 seconds. Charging peaks at 105 kW, with a quoted 24-minute stop to go from 10% to 80%.
The GTI also arrives with expectations beyond its performance figures.
My review of the regular ID. Polo
found it to be a very grown-up little EV that might justify its relatively high price. Meanwhile, reports of strong demand and lengthy waiting lists suggest the electric Polo formula is finding an audience.
A higher performance version of the ID. Polo GTI is reportedly on the way. The GTI Clubsport is believed to have around 282 hp (59 hp more), a fully mechanical limited-slip differential, paddles to
shift simulated gears
, and lower, stiffer suspension. It should also have unique exterior badging and details to set it apart from the standard GTI.

title: 10nm 以下迎来新玩家！格罗方德目标 2028 年量产 7nm 级 FD-SOI 工艺
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，GlobalFoundries（GF，格罗方德）当地时间今日公布了其全新 FD-SOI（完全耗尽型绝缘体上硅）先进制程技术平台 FDX Fusion 平台的计划。
FDX Fusion 平台的第一代技术预计将提供 7nm 级的数字性能。格罗方德计划 2027 年初向客户交付演示芯片、2027 年中提供初步的 PDK，2028 年在德国德累斯顿晶圆厂启动量产。
这意味着格罗方德将成为又一家独立的 10nm 以下级逻辑芯片制造商，也是首家将 FD-SOI 扩展至 10nm 以下级的企业。
IT之家了解到，FDX Fusion 瞄准物理人工智能市场，在优秀的数字逻辑性能外也拥有不俗的模拟 & 混合、射频表现，同时支持存内计算、嵌入式非易失性存储器。
格罗方德正与多家客户合作开展 FDX Fusion 的早期开发和评估工作，利用实际应用需求指导产品设计，并加速该技术从平台定义到量产就绪的进程。
格罗方德同日宣布，其德累斯顿生产基地的 SPRINT 扩展项目实现封顶，预计到 2028 年底将产能提升至每年超 100 万片 300mm（12 英寸）晶圆。

title: Counterpoint：苹果全新 MacBook Pro 将推动 OLED 笔记本面板市场增长，预计今年市场出货量同比增长 50%
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，市场研究机构 Counterpoint Research 发文，认为苹果触控屏 MacBook Pro 预计将推动 OLED 笔记本电脑面板市场增长。预计 2026 年 OLED 笔记本面板出货量将同比增长 50%，2027 年还将进一步增长 24%。
在高端笔记本显示面板市场中，Counterpoint 预计 OLED 面板相对于 Mini LED 面板将进一步扩大领先优势。预计 OLED 面板在该市场的出货占比将从 2025 年的 56% 升至 2026 年的 75%，Mini LED 面板的占比则将从 44% 降至 25%。
除苹果产品换代外，高端 AI PC 需求持续增长，以及 OLED 面板技术和制造工艺的进步，也进一步推动 OLED 面板市场扩张。
展望未来，Counterpoint Research 预计 2024 年至 2030 年 OLED 笔记本面板出货量的复合年增长率将达到 26%，面板收入的复合年增长率则有望达到 35%。随着苹果带动厂商逐步将 OLED 引入高端笔记本产品，相应技术面板在笔记本电脑市场中的占比预计还将继续提升。

title: 中国科学院院士郭华东获颁 2026 年度国际宇航联合会“名人堂”奖，主持研发全球首颗可持续发展科学卫星 1 号
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，据央视新闻报道，10 月 9 日，第 77 届国际宇航大会在土耳其闭幕。闭幕式上，国际宇航联合会为中国科学院院士、中国科学院空天信息创新研究院研究员郭华东颁发 2026 年度国际宇航联合会“名人堂”奖，以表彰其毕生深耕宇航领域并作出卓越贡献。
郭华东院士此次获奖的一项重要成果，是主持研发了全球首颗可持续发展科学卫星 1 号（SDGSAT-1）。该卫星通过“光-热-谱”多载荷昼夜协同探测，实现对“人类活动痕迹”的精细刻画，为可持续发展目标系统性监测提供新途径。目前，该卫星数据实现全球开放共享，惠及 121 个联合国会员国，开创了中国卫星数据全球服务新模式。
国际宇航联合会“名人堂”奖旨在表彰为全球航天事业进步做出开创性、终身性贡献的顶尖学者，是全球航天领域公认的权威荣誉。
IT之家查询获悉，2021 年 11 月 5 日，全球首颗专门服务联合国 2030 年可持续发展议程的科学卫星“可持续发展科学卫星 1 号”（SDGSAT-1）成功发射。该星的发射是纪念我国恢复联合国合法席位 50 周年系列活动之一。
SDGSAT-1 卫星由中国科学院“地球大数据科学工程”先导专项研制，是可持续发展大数据国际研究中心规划的首发星。该卫星搭载了热红外、微光和多谱段成像仪三个有效载荷，并设计了多种数据获取模式和星上定标模式，可以实现对人类活动与自然环境相互作用过程的精细刻画，满足服务全球可持续发展的数据获取效率和定量化探测需求。

title: 剧情驱动末日生存沙盒《永冻纪元》登陆 Steam：国区首发价 ¥95.20，支持简中配音
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，由 SpaceRocket Games 开发、Toplitz Productions 发行的剧情驱动末日生存沙盒游戏《永冻纪元》（Permafrost）今日正式登陆 Steam 开启抢先体验，国区首发享 20% 折扣，折后价为 ¥ 95.20，优惠截止至 10 月 23 日。游戏支持简体中文界面与完整中文音频，目前尚无玩家评价。IT之家附游戏商品页（https://store.steampowered.com/app/2254990/Permafrost/）。
《永冻纪元》背景设定在不远的未来，一系列灾难导致月球破碎，地球陷入永无止境的寒冬。玩家将扮演拥有重建能力的工程师“Rook”，凭借一段失联好友的无线电信号踏入这片冰封末日，在严酷环境中挣扎求生。官方介绍如下：
严寒，才是你真正的敌人！寒冷无处不在，仿佛拥有生命。冻伤、暴风雪与逐渐侵蚀的低温将伴随你的每一次行动，让准备、庇护与时机成为生死关键。在这片世界中，城市废墟逐渐过渡为荒野。这里没有持续的枪火，也没有奇幻设定，只有寂静与匮乏构成的紧张生存体验。只有寒冬、孤独，以及坚持下去的意志。
游戏核心特色包括：
- 开放世界探索：穿越冰封的城市废墟与荒野，在各方势力控制的区域中周旋，逐步深入这片冰封世界
- 生存建造玩法：狩猎、搜集、制作道具，修复废弃避难所并搭建避难所网络，利用旧时代技术生存下去
- 忠诚狗狗伙伴：从废墟中救下的狗狗会为你探路、预警危险、搬运物资，成为末日中最可靠的伙伴
- 多人合作模式：支持 1 到 4 人联机合作生存，玩家可以分工协作、共同建设避难网络，一起对抗严寒
本作目前处于抢先体验阶段，开发者表示计划至少保留 12 个月的抢先体验时间，在此期间会根据玩家反馈新增更多生物群系、任务、机制和优化内容，正式版推出后价格可能会上调。当前抢先体验版已实装大部分核心玩法，包含多个生物群系、数百种物品、建造蓝图和制作配方，主线开篇与大量支线任务、最多 4 人合作模式均已可用。

title: 商务部：中欧双方以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解
content:
感谢IT之家网友 火瓶座 的线索投递！
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，2026 年 10 月 8-9 日，中国商务部部长王文涛与欧盟委员会贸易和经济安全委员马罗什 · 谢夫乔维奇在北京举行中欧贸易投资磋商机制（以下简称机制）第二次例会。商务部今日发布了中欧贸易投资磋商机制第二次例会联合声明。
成果共识清单中包括，双方将继续探讨在世贸组织规则框架下降低部分商品关税的可能性。
经密集磋商，中欧双方以符合世贸组织规则的方式就混动汽车贸易达成谅解。双方忆及电动汽车反补贴案价格承诺指导文件，并将继续电动汽车反补贴案企业价格承诺和复审相关程序。
双方赞同提升全球产业链供应链可预期性与稳定性的重要性。中方愿通过“绿色通道”机制，为稀土及永磁体对欧出口许可审批继续提供便利。欧方将继续与成员国一道，为解决两用领域对华重点许可个案提供便利。
IT之家从中欧贸易投资磋商机制第二次例会联合声明了解到，双方商定，将于 2027 年 3 月召开机制第三次例会，在此之前双方将保持密切沟通，包括 1 月举行部长级视频会议。

title: 国务院发布《关于发展新质生产力的意见》：加快推进智能网联新能源汽车、人工智能手机和电脑、人形机器人等新一代智能终端场景应用
content:
感谢IT之家网友
10 月 9 日消息，中共中
务院今日发布《关于发展新质生产力的意见》，提出 19 条重大发展改革任务，坚持“创新主导、改革为要、因地制宜、先立后破”4 条原则。
《意见》将“大力推进科技创新”作为 5 大任务之首，提出加强原创性颠覆性科技创新、加快突破关键核心技术、统筹国家战略科技力量建设、强化企业科技创新主体地位、加速科技成果向现实生产力转化。
在培育壮大新兴产业方面，《意见》提出着力打造新兴支柱产业。加快新一代信息技术、新能源、新材料、智能网联新能源汽车、机器人、生物医药、高端装备、航空航天等战略性新兴产业发展，因地制宜建设各具特色、优势互补的战略性新兴产业集群，推动资源集聚、主体集中、成果集成、分工合作。深化产业内、产品内专业分工，促进跨行业跨区域融合，
避免“内卷式”竞争
。以产业链为主导、以企业为主体建立跨区域产业协作机制，支持东部地区带动中西部和东北地区因地制宜发展新兴产业。在确保安全前提下，
推动低空经济、商业航天健康有序发展
前瞻布局未来产业。探索多元技术路线、典型应用场景、可行商业模式、市场监管规则，推动
量子科技、生物制造、氢能和核聚变能、脑机接口、具身智能、第六代移动通信
等未来产业发展，加快形成比较完备的产业生态。建立未来产业投入增长和风险分担机制，充分用好现有财政政策支持未来产业发展，引导社会资本持续加大投入。
全面实施“人工智能 +”行动。推进人工智能对传统产业的改造，加快推进
智能网联新能源汽车、人工智能手机和电脑、人形机器人
等新一代智能终端场景应用。加快人工智能等数智技术创新，突破基础理论和核心技术，强化算力、算法、数据等高效供给。因地制宜、分业施策布局国家人工智能行业应用中试基地和高价值应用场景，大力推动人工智能在各行业应用。构建技术监测、风险预警、应急响应体系，确保人工智能安全、可靠、可控。

title: 漫威新剧《幻视任务》首曝中字片段：奥创以人类形态回归，10 月 14 日 Disney+ 开播
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，漫威新剧《幻视任务》今日首曝两段中字片段。本剧也是《旺达幻视》三部曲的终章，将于今年 10 月 14 日在 Disney+ 开播。
据介绍，《幻视任务》是继《旺达幻视》《女巫阿加莎》后 MCU 衍生剧系列三部曲的最后一部，将讲述幻视试图恢复记忆和人性的故事。
IT之家查询获悉，保罗 · 贝坦尼 / 詹姆斯 · 斯派德 / 埃米丽 · 汉普希尔 / 托德 · 斯塔什维克 / 法兰 · 塔希尔将出任主演。
其中，保罗 · 贝坦尼继续出演幻视，詹姆斯 · 斯派德回归饰奥创（将以人类形态回归），鲁阿里德 · 莫利卡饰旺达和幻视的儿子汤米，特里 · 马塔拉斯担任运作人。
《幻视任务》主创 Terry Matalas 在接受 ScreenRant 采访时确认，他们将在这部剧中引入一支新的复仇者团队，即“AI 复仇者”。该团队主要出现在幻视的思维空间（Mindspace）内，成员为被救援的斯塔克工业 AI，包括：
- 伊迪丝（EDITH）：托尼 · 斯塔克（钢铁侠）生前开发的高级人工智能安全与防御系统，主要出现在《蜘蛛侠：英雄远征》的 AR 眼镜中。
- 星期五（F.R.I.D.A.Y.）：托尼的第二代超级人工智能管家，首次亮相于电影《复仇者联盟 2：奥创纪元》（2015 年），主要负责协助托尼和钢铁侠战甲，直至《复仇者联盟 4：终局之战》。
- 贾维斯（J.A.R.V.I.S.）：随《钢铁侠》（2008）登场的超级人工智能管家，在星期五之前负责管理托尼的豪宅与斯塔克大厦，后来在《复仇者联盟 2》被上传至振金之躯，蜕变为幻视。
- 笨笨（D.U.M.-E）：托尼 · 斯塔克在车库里最早亲手制造的、带有液压机械臂的初代智能机器人助手。在《钢铁侠》中，它在托尼测试飞行战甲时总是提前举着灭火器严阵以待，在托尼还没着火时就喷了托尼一脸干粉，气得托尼威胁要把它捐给社区大学，后来在托尼命悬一线时递上了初代反应堆从而救了托尼一命。后来它在《钢铁侠 3》中随着托尼的悬崖豪宅被炸毁，而托尼在电影结尾用吊车从海底打捞出了其残骸，后续被修复并带到了复仇者联盟新总部以及他的湖边林间小屋，继续负责一些基础的搬运和杂活，直到《蜘蛛侠：英雄无归》时还帮忙搭建彼得 · 帕克的死星乐高模型，最后被灾害控制局（DODC）查封。
- U：笨笨的双胞胎兄弟，其主要工作就是手持摄像机，全程拍摄托尼在车库里的各项战甲测试和实验 Vlog。除了拍照摄影，小 U 也具备基础的抓取和递送功能，会在托尼组装战甲时在旁边递送关键零件。

设计方面，猛士 X700 承袭猛士“雄魂美学”理念，保留狮吼梯形前脸、剑指苍穹尾灯等家族识别符号，并采用贯穿式止戈为武大灯与数字银河灯带。
内饰方面，猛士 X700 配备悬浮式中控屏、大尺寸液晶仪表和 HUD 抬头显示，采用双 15.6 英寸华为智慧双联屏、HUAWEI SOUND 音响，同级首发鸿蒙座舱 6。同时该车搭载同级唯一云感魔毯座椅，配备 60 个可调气袋；行业首发实体橡胶凸点指压按摩（10 点按摩）；副驾配备双 127° 零重力座椅，二排配备座椅通风加热按摩、小桌板，还有同级唯一纯平二排大床房。
配置选装方面，猛士 X700 支持外挂备胎、行李架以及 2.5 吨拖挂资质等多项选装，还有“自定义情绪屏”等智能模块，可适配多元场景；首发 Robo 旅拍功能，可以将运动相机通过螺纹口固定在汽车引擎盖上，在车内通过专属按键开启和停止录制。
车身尺寸方面，猛士 X700 长宽高为 5035×1999×1910mm，轴距 2920mm，定位中大型 SUV。新车提供 265/65R18 与 255/60R20 两种规格轮毂可选。车辆拥有 850L 容积后备箱、7L 车载冷暖箱，还有同级唯一野趣拓展台，支持 6kW 对外放电
动力方面，猛士 X700 提供增程版和插混版两种选择，均搭载 1497ml 发动机，增程版功率 95kW，最大净功率 90kW；插混版功率 113kW，最大净功率 110kW。车辆采用 800V 平台架构，配备 68.1kWh 宁德时代越野专用电池，CLTC 纯电续航 360km；零百加速 4.93 秒，综合功率可达 518kW。

title: 第二艘国产大邮轮“爱达 · 花城号”明年将以香港作为母港营运
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，爱达邮轮在港正式发布第二艘国产大型邮轮“爱达 · 花城号”的航线及产品布局，“爱达 · 花城号”将于明年正式以香港为母港，这艘邮轮将于今年 11 月启航并造访香港。
据介绍，“爱达 · 花城号”将于 2027 年全面展开香港母港航季，预计营运近 20 个邮轮航次。航线设计灵活多元，增设 3 个海上游航次，为本地旅客提供“邮轮即是目的地”的海上体验。
爱达邮轮表示，香港兼具国际化区位优势、成熟的邮轮母港条件和多元客源基础是爱达邮轮深耕大湾区、连接国际的重要支点。此次“爱达 · 花城号”在香港开启母港航季，是完善广州、深圳、香港三港协同，持续深化大湾区布局的重要一步。爱达邮轮将持续增加在香港的运力投放，全力支持香港巩固亚洲国际邮轮枢纽的地位。
作为首艘国产大型邮轮“爱达 · 魔都号”的姊妹船，“爱达 · 花城号”全长 341 米，总吨位达 14.19 万，拥有 2130 间豪华客房和套房，可容纳约 5232 名旅客。邮轮在空间设计、餐饮娱乐与智能科技上进行了全面升级。
IT之家注意到，第二艘国产大型邮轮“爱达 · 花城号”与 5 月 27 日完成为期 12 天的试航任务并靠港。
在试航期间，技术人员完成了对主推进器、船舶操纵、航速耐久性、全船振动噪声、无人机舱运行及救助艇释放等核心难点项目验收。试航涵盖的 45 份调试程序、149 项试验验证全部完成，全方位高标准验证了船舶的操纵性、自动化水平、安全舒适性及排放指标。

title: 遏制有害水生物传播，我国牵头制定的船舶压载水管理系统调试测试国际标准发布
content:
IT之家 10 月 9 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，国际标准化组织（ISO）近日发布《船舶与海洋技术压载水管理系统（BWMS）电解法压载水管理系统的调试和测试程序》国际标准。该标准由中国牵头，美国、德国、加拿大、瑞士、挪威、丹麦等国专家参与制定。
报道称，船舶压载水携带的外来生物是海洋生物入侵的重要途径之一，严重威胁海洋生态安全。压载水管理系统是杀灭这些入侵生物的关键设备，其杀灭效果取决于产品本身设计性能及安装后现场调试水平。
IT之家从报道获悉，该标准规范了电解法压载水管理系统调试测试技术要求，规定系统运行时长不少于 60 分钟、排放采样体积不少于 1 立方米，并对大于等于 50 微米和 10 微米至 50 微米两类生物进行达标验证，确保满足国际公约排放标准，为全球船东、船厂、设备制造商和行业主管部门提供统一的、科学的压载水管理系统调试测试程序和验收依据。
截至目前，我国牵头制定 3 项压载水管理系统相关国际标准，覆盖系统设计、调试等关键环节，为遏制有害水生物通过压载水跨海域传播发挥重要作用，助力全球海洋生态环境保护。
船舶压载水是指船舶为控制吃水、稳性和船体受力而注入或排出船舱的海水及悬浮物。船舶在港口装载货物时需排出压载水，从而将始发港海域的生物、病原体带入目的港海域，这是外来海洋生物入侵的重要途径之一。为此，国际海事组织（IMO）于 2004 年通过了《2004 年国际船舶压载水和沉积物控制与管理公约》，该公约于 2017 年 9 月 8 日在全球范围内生效。
公约附则中的 D-2 排放性能标准是压载水处理的强制性要求，其具体限值为：每立方米中最小尺寸大于或等于 50 微米的可生存生物应少于 10 个；每毫升中最小尺寸小于 50 微米但大于或等于 10 微米的可生存生物应少于 10 个。此外还规定了指示微生物限值，如有毒霍乱弧菌、大肠杆菌、肠道球菌等。报道中提到的两类生物达标验证，正是对照这一 D-2 标准。
所谓电解法压载水管理系统，其原理是让海水先经过滤器滤除大块泥沙及大型微生物，再利用电解单元电解海水，生成具有杀菌能力的次氯酸钠等物质以灭活压载水中的生物；排放时则通过中和单元将余氯控制在 IMO 规定范围内。电解法技术成熟、处理能力大，是当前大中型船舶压载水处理市场的主流方法之一。

Die Studienfinanzierung ist oftmals herausfordernd. Dies betrifft besonders Studierende aus dem Ausland, die keinen Anspruch auf Ausbildungsförderung haben und neben den Studieninhalten auch die Sprache lernen müssen. Die Kieserling Stiftung unterstützt Logistikstudierende der Hochschule Bremerhaven, die aus finanziellen Gründen mit Herausforderungen im Studium zu kämpfen haben. Kürzlich wurden drei Stipendien vergeben. Iryna Gutsul, Quang Minh Nguyen und Tran Pham nahmen diese von Studiengangsleiter Prof. Dr.-Ing. Carsten Dorn und im Beisein des Dekanats des Fachbereichs 2 der Hochschule entgegen.
Studierende aus dem Ausland sind nach ihrem Abschluss begehrte Nachwuchskräfte in deutschen Unternehmen. Neben ihrem Fachwissen besitzen sie sprachliche und interkulturelle Kompetenzen, die besonders für die weltweit agierende Logistikbranche wertvoll sind. Gleichzeitig stehen ausländische Studierende vor großen Herausforderungen. Sie müssen sich in einem fremden Land zurechtfinden und die Sprache lernen, ohne die Studienleistungen zu vernachlässigen. Hinzu kommt die Studienfinanzierung. In der Regel kommen die Eltern für Unterhalt und Semestergebühren auf. Wenn sich deren finanzielle Situation verschlechtert, zum Beispiel durch Krieg oder Krankheit, bedroht dies den Studienerfolg.
Die Kieserling-Stiftung ermöglicht der Hochschule Bremerhaven, ihren Logistikstudierenden in solchen Fällen finanziell unter die Arme zu greifen. Zum ersten Mal können sich gleich drei Personen über ein Stipendium freuen. Im Beisein von Dekan Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Gerhard Feldmeiner und Prof. Dr.-Ing. Dieter Heimann, Studiendekan, überreichte Studiengangsleiter Prof. Dr.-Ing. Carsten Dorn symbolische Schecks an die Stipendiat:innen Iryna Gutsul, Quang Minh Nguyen und Tran Pham.
Iryna Gutsul stammt aus der Ukraine. In der Schule hatte sie bereits Deutschunterricht, was ihr Interesse an der Sprache und Kultur geweckt hat. Die praxisnahen Lehrmethoden an deutschen Hochschulen und die guten Berufschancen nach dem Abschluss haben sie vor Kriegsausbruch für ein Studium nach Deutschland geführt. Bisher hat sie ihr Studium durch einen Nebenjob finanziert. Da sie nun ihre Abschlussarbeit schreibt, ist das so nicht mehr möglich. Das Stipendium der Kieserling-Stiftung ermöglicht Frau Gutsul, sich auf ihr Studium zu konzentrieren und es zeitnah abzuschließen.
Quang Minh Nguyen ist aus Vietnam nach Deutschland gekommen. Er interessiert sich sehr für die Bereiche Logistik, Transport und internationale Wirtschaft. Daher möchte er nach seinem Abschluss in einem internationalen Unternehmen in Bremen arbeiten, um Transportketten nach Vietnam mit aufzubauen. Da Deutsch nicht seine Muttersprache ist, benötigt er mehr Zeit, um sich die Inhalte der Lehrveranstaltungen selbst zu erarbeiten. Dank des Stipendiums kann er seinen Lebensunterhalt ohne Nebenbeschäftigung finanzieren und sich somit auf sein Studium konzentrieren.
Tran Pham stammt ebenfalls aus Vietnam. Nach ihrem Bachelorabschluss in englischer Linguistik hat sie sich bewusst für einen fachlichen Neuanfang in der Logistik entschieden. Besonders interessant findet sie die Verbindung von Technik, Wirtschaft und Organisation sowie die Möglichkeit, Waren- und Informationsflüsse effizient und nachhaltig zu gestalten. Neben finanzieller Unterstützung durch ihre Familie plant sie, ihr Studium mithilfe eines Nebenjobs zu finanzieren. Mit dem Stipendium der Kieserling-Stiftung erhält sie zusätzliche Unterstützung, sodass ihr Studium nicht unter der Doppelbelastung leidet.
Die Bremer Kieserling Stiftung engagiert sich für verkehrswirtschaftliche und logistische Themen. Zweck der Stiftung ist die Förderung von Wissenschaft und Forschung, Bildung und Erziehung sowie die Förderung der Jugendhilfe. Die Hochschule Bremerhaven hat Fördermittel erhalten, um hilfsbedürftige Studierende aus dem Bachelorstudiengang Transport, Wirtschaft, Logistik und dem Masterstudiengang Logitics Engineering and Management zu unterstützen.

title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Sprachmodelle, die jeden Buchstaben sehen
content:
Künstliche Intelligenz: Sprachmodelle, die jeden Buchstaben sehen
Die meisten KI-Sprachmodelle bekommen die einzelnen Buchstaben eines Wortes nie direkt zu sehen. Eine neue Methode ändert das, indem sie bestehende Modelle mit einem Bruchteil des üblichen Trainingsaufwands umrüstet.
Bevor große Sprachmodelle (LLMs) Text verarbeiten können, zerlegen sie ihn in Einheiten wie Wörter oder Wortfragmente. Das LLM hinter ChatGPT zerlegt beispielsweise „LMU München“ in die drei Einheiten „LM“, „U“ und „München“, sodass es die einzelnen Buchstaben in „München“ nie direkt sieht. Dieser als Subwort-Tokenisierung bezeichnete Schritt macht LLMs zwar effizient, verursacht jedoch eine Reihe von Problemen, wie beispielsweise ein eingeschränktes Verständnis auf Zeichenebene. Modelle, die Text stattdessen Byte für Byte lesen (wobei grob ein Byte einem Buchstaben entspricht), vermeiden diese Probleme. In der Praxis sind sie jedoch noch keine brauchbare Alternative zu LLMs mit Subwort-Tokenisierung geworden.
In einer neuen Studie, die in der Fachzeitschrift Nature veröffentlicht wurde, haben Forscher der LMU, des Allen Institute for AI, der University of Cambridge, der University of Washington und des Imperial College London eine Methode entwickelt, die bestehende LLMs in Modelle auf Byte-Ebene umwandelt, ohne sie von Grund auf neu trainieren zu müssen. Diese „Byteifizierung“ erfordert weniger als ein Prozent des für ein solches Modell üblicherweise benötigten Trainingsaufwands und bewahrt weitgehend die Leistung des ursprünglichen LLMs, während gleichzeitig die Vorteile der Verarbeitung auf Byte-Ebene hinzukommen. Die daraus resultierenden Modelle übertreffen alle bisher veröffentlichten LLMs auf Byte-Ebene vergleichbarer Größe.
„Wir glauben, dass die ‚Byteifizierung‘ und LLMs auf Byte-Ebene im Allgemeinen das Potenzial haben, einige seit langem bestehende Mängel von LLMs zu überwinden“, sagt Valentin Hofmann, Juniorprofessor für Informations- und Sprachverarbeitung mit Methoden der KI an der LMU München und Leiter der Studie. „Herkömmliche LLMs haben Schwierigkeiten mit Aufgaben, die Fähigkeiten auf Zeichenebene erfordern, wie zum Beispiel das rückwärts Buchstabieren eines Wortes. Unsere ‚byteifizierten‘ Modelle sind darin deutlich besser.“ Diese Fähigkeiten sind mehr als nur eine akademische Spielerei: „Eine gute Darstellung der Feinstruktur von Text ist in vielen Bereichen der Wissenschaft entscheidend, zum Beispiel bei der Arbeit mit Code oder biologischen Sequenzen“, erklärt Hofmann.
Die Forschenden hoffen, dass die Byteifizierung Modelle auf Byte-Ebene zu einer praktischen Alternative zu den heutigen LLMs macht und neue Forschungsrichtungen eröffnet. Die Modelle, der Code und die Trainingsdaten sind öffentlich zugänglich.

Ein Forschungsprojekt begleitete über 32 Monate den Umstieg von Dieselbussen auf batterieelektrische Busse im öffentlichen Linienverkehr in Salzburg. Ein intelligentes Lademanagement reduzierte Lastspitzen deutlich und lieferte konkrete Erkenntnisse für die weitere Elektrifizierung des öffentlichen Personennahverkehrs. Der vollständige Ergebnisbericht steht online kostenfrei zur Verfügung.
Wie lassen sich wachsende E-Bus-Flotten zuverlässig, wirtschaftlich und energieeffizient betreiben? Dieser Frage widmete sich das Forschungsprojekt „OptiChargE“. Über mehr als zwei Jahre begleiteten Salzburg Research, EQOS Energie Österreich GmbH und Consilio Information Management GmbH die Umstellung und Skalierung des elektrischen Busbetriebs bei der Albus Salzburg Verkehrsbetrieb GmbH.
Im Mittelpunkt stand ein integriertes Lademanagement, das Fahrzeug-, Lade-, Betriebs- und Infrastrukturdaten aus verschiedenen bestehenden Systemen zusammenführt und für die gemeinsame Steuerung und Optimierung der Ladevorgänge nutzbar macht. Die entwickelte Lösung wurde in einem 13-monatigen Pilotbetrieb unter realen Bedingungen getestet und laufend weiterentwickelt. In dieser Zeit wuchs die elektrische Flotte von sieben auf 58 batterieelektrische Busse. Zugleich wurden die Zahl der Ladepunkte von 20 auf 56 erhöht und die installierte Photovoltaikleistung von 480 auf 1.420 kWp ausgebaut. Damit konnte eine reale Skalierung direkt im laufenden Betrieb untersucht werden.
„Die Forschungsergebnisse zeigen, dass die Elektrifizierung von Busflotten weit mehr ist als der Austausch des Antriebs. Fahrzeuge, Ladeinfrastruktur, Energieversorgung, Daten, Software und betriebliche Abläufe müssen als Gesamtsystem betrachtet werden“, sagt Cornelia Zankl von Salzburg Research, die das Projekt leitete.
Deutlich geringere Lastspitzen durch intelligentes Lademanagement
Ein wesentliches Ziel war, die verfügbare elektrische Leistung effizient auf die Fahrzeuge zu verteilen, Lastspitzen zu vermeiden und gleichzeitig sicherzustellen, dass alle Busse rechtzeitig mit ausreichendem Ladestand einsatzbereit sind.
Im Vergleich zu einer ungesteuerten Referenzstrategie, bei der jeder Bus sofort mit maximaler Leistung geladen würde, sank die Spitzenlast je nach Monat um rund 55 bis 75 Prozent. Über den Pilotzeitraum entsprach dies einer rechnerischen Einsparung von rund 80.000 Euro an leistungsabhängigen Netzleistungskosten. Auch gegenüber einer einfachen zeitgesteuerten Ladestrategie reduzierte das aktive Lastmanagement die Spitzenlast meist nochmals um etwa 15 bis 35 Prozent.
„Ein leistungsfähiges Lademanagement muss Betriebssicherheit und wirtschaftliche Optimierung verbinden“, erklärt Markus Klein, stellvertretender Leiter der Business Unit Energietechnik bei EQOS Energie. „Das Projekt hat gezeigt, dass intelligente Steuerung Lastspitzen deutlich reduzieren und vorhandene Infrastruktur effizient nutzen kann.“
Betriebssicherheit steht an erster Stelle
Eine zentrale Anforderung war die Integration bestehender IT-Systeme, etwa für Disposition und Abrechnung. Gleichzeitig zeigte sich: Betriebssicherheit hat oberste Priorität. Monitoring, automatisierte Alarmierungen und manuelle Eingriffsmöglichkeiten sind entscheidend, damit die Fahrzeuge zuverlässig einsatzbereit bleiben.
Auch betriebliche Abläufe beeinflussen die Energieeffizienz. Durch angepasste Disposition und gezielte Zwischenladungen lassen sich etwa Ladefenster schaffen, in denen eigener Photovoltaikstrom tagsüber besser genutzt werden kann.
„Für uns war entscheidend, dass sich das Lademanagement unter realen Betriebsbedingungen bewährt“, sagt Hermann Häckl, Geschäftsführer der Albus Salzburg Verkehrsbetrieb GmbH. „Die Erfahrungen aus OptiChargE helfen uns, die weitere Elektrifizierung unseres Linienverkehrs praxistauglich und betriebssicher umzusetzen.“
Daten und Schnittstellen als Schlüssel
Für ein leistungsfähiges Lademanagement müssen Informationen aus unterschiedlichen Systemen zusammengeführt werden – darunter Fahrzeug- und Ladezustandsdaten, Dispositionsinformationen sowie Energie- und Wetterdaten.
Im Projekt wurden detaillierte Telematikdaten für Verbrauchsmodelle und Prognosen genutzt. Dabei zeigte sich, wie wichtig standardisierte Schnittstellen und ein verlässlicher Datenzugang sind.
„Verlässliche Fahrzeug- und Telematikdaten sind eine zentrale Grundlage für ein intelligentes Lademanagement“, betont Klaus Satz von Consilio Information Management GmbH. „Datenzugang, Schnittstellen und Datenqualität sollten deshalb bereits bei der Beschaffung und Planung zukünftiger E-Busflotten mitgedacht werden.“
Energieverbrauch: Wetter und Verkehr wichtiger als der Fahrstil
Die Analysen zeigten zudem, dass Wetter und Verkehrslage den Energieverbrauch der E-Busse stärker beeinflussten als der individuelle Fahrstil. Zwar gab es geringe Unterschiede zwischen einzelnen Lenkerinnen und Lenkern, ein signifikanter Einfluss unterschiedlicher Fahrstile ließ sich jedoch nicht feststellen.  Aus den gemessenen Unterschieden ließ sich kein ausreichendes Einsparpotenzial ableiten, das zusätzliche Schulungen wirtschaftlich begründen würde.
Elektrifizierung als integrierter Planungsprozess
Die Erfahrungen aus OptiChargE zeigen, dass Flotte, Ladeinfrastruktur, Energieversorgung, Software, Daten und betriebliche Prozesse gemeinsam weiterentwickelt werden müssen und dass betriebliches Know-how aufgebaut werden muss.
Bewährt hat sich ein stufenweises Vorgehen: Vor jeder Ausbaustufe gilt es, Prozesse zu stabilisieren, standortspezifische Erfahrungen zu sammeln und den nächsten Schritt gezielt vorzubereiten. Gleichzeitig sollte das langfristige Zielbild vor Beginn der Flottenumstellung entwickelt werden – insbesondere bei Netzanschluss, Ladeinfrastruktur und Energieversorgung.
Das Projekt liefert damit praxisnahe Handlungsempfehlungen für Verkehrsunternehmen, die ihren Busbetrieb elektrifizieren oder bestehende E-Bus-Flotten weiter ausbauen möchten.
Über OptiChargE
Das kooperative Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprojekt „OptiChargE – Optimised and automated charging management for battery electric bus fleets“ lief von Februar 2024 bis September 2026 und wurde im Rahmen von Zero Emission Mobility durch den Klima- und Energiefonds gefördert und von der FFG abgewickelt. Projektpartner waren Salzburg Research Forschungsgesellschaft mbH (Projektleitung), Albus Salzburg Verkehrsbetrieb GmbH, EQOS Energie Österreich GmbH und Consilio Information Management GmbH.

Der renommierte Robotik-Forscher Philipp Rothemund, Professor an der Universität Stuttgart, übernimmt eine zentrale Rolle in der Aufbauphase des neuen baden-württembergischen Forschungs- und Graduiertenzentrums für angewandte Künstliche Intelligenz.
Prof. Philipp Rothemund wird Gründungsdirektor der connAIx Research School for Applied AI in Heilbronn und hat den damit verbundenen Ruf auf die W3-Professur für Soft Robotics for Autonomous and Biomedical Systems an der Universität Stuttgart angenommen. Damit stehen zwei von drei Gründungsdirektor*innen der neuen Forschungseinrichtung fest. Gemeinsam mit der Tübinger Professorin Veronika Eyring, die im Juni berufen wurde, wird Rothemund den Aufbau von connAIx gestalten.
Das Forschungs- und Graduiertenzentrum für angewandte Künstliche Intelligenz wurde im Januar 2026 vom Land Baden-Württemberg mit Unterstützung der Dieter Schwarz Stiftung ins Leben gerufen. Die drei Trägereinrichtungen, die Universitäten Stuttgart und Tübingen sowie das Karlsruher Institut für Technologie (KIT), bündeln darin ihre Expertise in der KI-Forschung. Sie arbeiten eng mit Unternehmen zusammen, um Forschung schneller in die Anwendung zu bringen, und schaffen den Rahmen für eine exzellente Qualifizierung des wissenschaftlichen Nachwuchses. Inhaltliche Schwerpunkte liegen auf Zukunftsfeldern der angewandten KI wie Chipdesign, Robotik und Cybersicherheit.
Forschung im Zukunftsfeld Soft Robotics
In seiner Arbeit an der Schnittstelle zwischen Mechanik, Materialwissenschaft und Robotik erforscht Philipp Rothemund das grundsätzliche Verhalten funktioneller weicher Materialien. Rothemund schafft nicht nur wichtiges Grundlagenwissen, sondern entwickelt mit seiner Gruppe innovative, funktionale Materialstrukturen, die auf Temperatur, Feuchtigkeit und elektrische Felder reagieren. In Soft-Robotics-Systemen der Zukunft könnten diese Materialien eine zentrale Rolle spielen – beispielsweise als Aktoren, Sensoren, Steuerungen oder Energiequellen.
Ungewöhnliche und mutige Wege
„Wir freuen uns sehr, nach Professorin Veronika Eyring den zweiten Gründungsdirektor für connAIx in Heilbronn gewonnen zu haben. Professor Philipp Rothemund ist ein aufstrebender, international bestens vernetzter Wissenschaftler, der in der Robotik ungewöhnliche und mutige Wege geht“, sagt Baden-Württembergs Wissenschaftsministerin Petra Olschowski. „Rothemund nimmt dabei besonders die Materialebene in den Blick und arbeitet nicht wie bei herkömmlichen Robotern meist üblich mit Aluminium, Stahl oder Carbonfasern, sondern mit weichen, oftmals bioinspirierten Stoffen wie Gummi. Er passt so perfekt zu der Ausrichtung von connAIx. Denn hier arbeiten künftig international herausragende Forscherinnen und Forscher mit Nachwuchswissenschaftlerinnen und -wissenschaftlern interdisziplinär an Fragen der angewandten KI zusammen.“
„Wir sind stolz, dass wir Philipp Rothemund an der Universität Stuttgart halten und ihn für die wichtige Position des connAIx-Gründungsdirektors gewinnen konnten“, betont Prof. Peter Middendorf, Rektor der Universität Stuttgart. „Er wird gemeinsam mit weiteren herausragenden KI-Forschenden aus Stuttgart, Karlsruhe und Tübingen das Forschungs- und Graduiertenzentrum voranbringen und einen wichtigen Beitrag für die langfristige Zusammenarbeit von Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft sowie für die Nachwuchsförderung auf international höchstem Niveau leisten.“
Spitzenstandort für Künstliche Intelligenz und Robotik
„Ein neues Zentrum von Grund auf aufzubauen und seine wissenschaftliche Identität von Beginn an mitzuprägen, ist eine außergewöhnliche Aufgabe, auf die ich mich sehr freue“, sagt Philipp Rothemund. „Mit connAIx bietet sich die große Chance, einen international sichtbaren Spitzenstandort für Künstliche Intelligenz und Robotik zu schaffen und damit das Forschungs- und Innovationsökosystem in Baden-Württemberg nachhaltig zu stärken. Unser Anspruch ist klar: Wir wollen Spitzenforschung betreiben, wissenschaftlich neue Maßstäbe setzen und herausragende Talente für diesen Standort begeistern.“
„Mit Philipp Rothemund gewinnen wir einen Forscher, der intelligente Materialien und physische Robotik auf faszinierende Weise zusammenbringt“, so Prof. Gunther Friedl, Geschäftsführer der Dieter Schwarz Stiftung. „Seine Arbeit hat internationale Strahlkraft und wird ambitionierte Talente aus aller Welt nach Heilbronn ziehen. Wir freuen uns sehr, ihn als Gründungsdirektor an Bord zu haben, um connAIx zukunftsweisend mitzugestalten.“
Über Philipp Rothemund
Philipp Rothemund ist Professor für Soft Robotics for Autonomous and Biomedical Systems an der Universität Stuttgart und Gründungsdirektor der connAIx Research School for Applied AI in Heilbronn. Er war zuvor Tenure Track Professor für Functional Soft Robotic Matter am Institut für Adaptive Mechanische Systeme (IAMS) der Universität Stuttgart. Er promovierte 2018 in den Ingenieurswissenschaften an der Harvard University. Weitere akademische Stationen führten ihn an die ETH Zürich, an die University of Colorado Boulder und das Max-Planck-Institut für Intelligente Systeme. 2024 gründete er gemeinsam mit Prof. David Remy das Institut für Adaptive Mechanische Systeme (IAMS) der Universität Stuttgart. 2025 erhielt er den renommierten ERC Consolidator Grant. Rothemund hat sich nicht nur mit seiner Expertise im Bereich Soft Robotics einen Namen gemacht, seine Stimme findet auch in der Wissenschaftspolitik Gehör. 2025 wurde er für ein Jahr zum Sprecher der Jungen Akademie gewählt, dem Sprachrohr für junge Wissenschaftler*innen in Deutschland, und 2026 in das renommierte WIN-Kolleg der Heidelberger Akademie der Wissenschaften aufgenommen.
